3. Sales Operations & Process

4. Cross-Functional Collaboration

- Partner with product, marketing, and operations to align on go-to-market strategy

- Provide customer feedback to inform product and positioning

- Ensure seamless handoffs from sale to onboarding

5. Team Development (as you scale)

- Help recruit, onboard, and mentor future sales hires

- Set the standard for performance, discipline, and accountability

- Contribute to building a scalable sales culture

Who You Are 

Player-Coach

- Proven ability to both sell directly and build systems

- Leads from the front with strong individual contribution

Partnership-Oriented Seller

- Comfortable selling through relationships, channels, and complex deals

- Able to navigate multi-stakeholder environments

Operator Mindset

- Data-driven and structured in how you manage pipeline and performance

- Brings rigor without slowing down execution

High-Performance Background

- Competitive, resilient, and disciplined

- Thrives in fast-paced, high-accountability environments

Low Ego, High Ownership

- Willing to do the work—prospecting, closing, problem-solving

- Takes full ownership of outcomes

Preferred Background

title: Office Manager
description:
Accelerating embodied AGI. 

The next ten years of AI will not be won in software. They will be won in the physical world: in factories, hospitals, kitchens, fields, and homes. The companies that own that data will own the century.

microagi is building it. We are a data research and deployment lab. Atlas captures the manual work inside Europe’s industrial champions, trains foundation models on it, and deploys the right robot onto the floor, with no teleoperation and no interruption to the line. Shift records how physical work actually happens and turns it into training-ready data.

We were founded by former Formula 1 engineers from Red Bull Racing and Mercedes, together with a researcher from the Alan Turing Institute. Our $55M seed round, the largest in German history, was led by Hummingbird with Northzone, LocalGlobe, Village Global, and redalpine. We are based in Munich, with our research centre in Zürich and teams in London, New York, and Istanbul. We are now building the engineering and research teams that will take Atlas into new industries.

As our Office Manager in Munich, you'll have an incredible role as a people driven person who's passionate about the day to day operations and administrative needs of the office, to helping curate a best in class workplace environment and assisting on events. 

- You’ve worked at a startup. You’ve been through the speed and the ambiguity, and the “we’re doubling headcount next quarter” moments. You know how to build processes without slowing anyone down.

- You care how the office feels. You notice the small things: the coffee, the light, how a new joiner’s first morning goes, whether the meeting rooms actually work. You want people to come in because they’d rather be there.

- You’re an operator at heart. You’ve managed vendors, facilities, supplies, budgets, health and safety, access and maintenance, and you keep it all running smoothly in the background.

- You can run events. You’ve planned team socials, all-hands, offsites, investor visits and community nights. You can take one from a rough idea to a polished event, often with little notice.

- You’re very organised and you follow through. You juggle a dozen moving parts, and nothing gets dropped or waits on someone else to chase it.

- You’re a great communicator. You build good relationships with everyone, from new engineers to the founders, landlords and suppliers. People find you warm, approachable and dependable.

- You’re happy owning things alone. You don’t need a playbook. You see what’s needed, set a high bar and get it done.

Who Will Thrive at microagi

Everyone we hire is assessed on the same four traits:

- Mission and vision: you care about what we are building and why it matters, and your past choices show it.

- Intensity: you work at a pace that matches the size of the opportunity, and you sustain it.

- Entrepreneurial: you start things nobody asked for, and you finish them.

- Raw IQ: you learn fast, reason from first principles, and get sharper when the problem changes.

This is for you if: 

- You would rather own a problem end to end than wait for a spec.

- You use AI every day, and you can tell a correct answer from a plausible one.

- You want to work in person, in the office, with people who are very good at what they do.

This is not for you if: 

- You are looking for a predictable 9-to-5.

- You would forward output you cannot explain.

- "That’s not my job" feels like a reasonable answer.

How We Hire

We read every application and reply within five working days.

- Talent Screen (30 min): a first conversation, both ways.

- Technical or Functional Interview (60 min): how you think when the problem changes.

- Your Work (60 min): bring something you are proud of and walk us through it.

- Leadership (30 min): a conversation with our CEO.

- Coworking Day (engineering and research roles): a day building with the team on a real problem.

Then a decision, usually within a few days.

Pay Transparency

Compensation includes base salary and equity. The salary range for this role is shown on this posting.

What We Offer

- Agency: real ownership from day one, and decisions that actually matter.

- Freedom: to choose how you solve the problem, without layers of approval.

- A seat on a rocketship: one of Europe’s fastest-growing deep-tech companies, at the earliest stage.

- Free food and drinks in the office.

Equal Opportunity

microagi welcomes applications from everyone. We assess candidates on their work and potential, regardless of ethnic origin, gender, religion or belief, disability, age, or sexual identity.

title: Senior Product Engineer (Incident Response, remote)
description:
(Fully remote, async-first, DevTools SaaS, 32-40h/week, time zones: UTC-3 to UTC+3) 

Help turn Checkly's incident response, on-call and status pages from a young product that customers already pay for into a core part of our platform. In 2027 agents will be on call and we want to be ready for that. You'll shape what we build in 2027, build it with AI coding agents, and talk directly to the teams who use it in the middle of an incident.

The best engineering teams don't wait for users to tell them something's broken. They build resilient, reliable systems to catch it first: in the pull request, in staging, or production at 3am, before a single customer notices. That instinct is Checkly's whole reason to exist.

Checkly gives developers, SRE teams and their agents the tools to own reliability the way they own their code: testing and synthetic monitoring defined as code, built on OpenTelemetry and Playwright. From pull request to post-mortem, in one place.

This role is about the post-mortem end of that line. We've built incident management, status pages and on-call into Checkly, and it's already bringing in revenue. Now we want to drive it strategically. Figure out together with us how to evolve incident management with clear signals and with agents being on call.

Thousands of teams, from AI companies like Mistral and resolve.ai to large engineering organizations like LinkedIn, Citi and 1Password, build with us. In 2024 we raised $20M in Series B funding from Balderton, CRV and Accel.

Our stack is AI (Claude, Codex, use what you like best), Vue.js, TypeScript, Go, Postgres, ClickHouse and AWS. We don't filter on programming language. If you ship full-stack with AI, you'll pick ours up. We ship to prod all day, every day, practice Agile (not scrum), keep meetings low and take pride in good documentation and good looking products.

What you'll do

- Shape a product from early stage to strategic. You'll be involved early in how we build incident response out as a platform, technically and on the product side. That means a lot of ownership, influence and visibility.

- Build the foundation first. Incident management, status pages, on-call, and tight integration with the rest of Checkly. For at least the first six months this is solid product engineering. AI-assisted incident response comes once the foundation is in place.

- Build and ship with AI. Coding agents are how you work: exploring solutions, scaffolding, refactoring, testing and debugging.

- Talk to the people on call. You'll be directly involved in customer conversations. You'll learn how responders work under pressure and turn that into what we build next.

- Find the right problems to solve. In a world where the cost of building software trends to zero, the hard part is picking what to build. You will favour pragmatic solutions that ship quickly, validate assumptions in production, and compound into long-term reliability improvements.

- Own your work end to end. From the first idea to rollout to how it behaves in production. You'll join the on-call and support rotations like everyone else.

What you should have

- You've built incident management, on-call, alerting or status page products before. You know what responders need from a tool when something breaks at 3am.

- You have shipped features with AI, not just experimented with them. You have taken work from zero to shipped with a comparable stack, made implementation decisions that held up, and put things in front of real users.

- You have built and run production software. You know the realities of operating software that people depend on: edge cases, incidents, regressions, and the need for observability and follow-up. You are not surprised when things break. You help fix them.

- You can drive a product area, not just pick up tickets. You make decisions without perfect information, and you ask for input when it counts. You have opinions about what we should build and why, and you change your mind when someone makes a better case.

- You work well without an office around you. You are autonomous and self-motivated in a remote setup, and you still enjoy getting to know your colleagues and helping other people get unstuck.

- You share work early. Drafts, rough MVPs and half-finished docs go out for feedback before they’re polished. In an async team, that’s how good ideas get better fast.

- FULLY remote role, within the UTC-3 to UTC+3 time zones. You need to be able to travel to (other) European countries without waiting for a visa appointment, for our annual kickoff, team meetups or conferences.

What you will hate about us

We would rather tell you now than have you find out in month two.

- We use AI for everything, and we mean everything. AI skepticism is not a thing here. If you have the slightest hesitation about working with AI every day, this is not the place for you, and that is completely fine.

- We write more than we talk. We are async-first, so a lot of decisions happen in documents and threads, not meetings. If you do your best thinking out loud in a room full of people, you will miss it here.

- We are lean, so you own the unglamorous parts too. There is no separate QA team, no ops layer to hand things off to, and you are on the support rotation and the on-call rotation like everyone else.

- We ship constantly and change our minds. Priorities move as we learn from customers. If you need long, stable planning cycles, this will feel chaotic.

- Customer signals come first, and most of the time they matter more than your instinct. We build what customers actually want, not the clever thing we dreamed up.

How we build with AI

Don’t take our word for it. Here’s what that looks like in practice, written by the team:

- Checkly and the agentic software layer : Hannes on why the CLI is how agents use software, including running monitoring and incidents.

- Your software factory stops at deploy : Stefan on what happens after deploy, when a failing check should kick off the fix.

- We let AI agents rewrite a 92M-message-a-day service in Go : Eddie on porting a core service with an agent, and zero incidents.

- Why I built my own AI agent orchestration tool : Immanuel on running 10 to 20 coding agents at once.

Benefits

- Transparent salary because your salary shouldn't be dictated by how good a negotiator you are. (more info below)

- Remote-first , flexible work hours , async-first (low meeting, high productivity) and transparent culture 

- Become part of a fast-growing, international, and remote team where your work matters, and your impact won't get lost in layers of bureaucracy.

- Stock options

- 27 days of paid vacation + your local public holidays

- Paid sick leave & up to 14 weeks of paid parental leave

- Co-working budget or home office setup

- Annual company kickoffs

Find out more here .

What we pay

Fair, competitive, and transparent pay is very important for us. Therefore we work with a standardized salary calculator that includes several factors such as seniority level as well as location.

For this role, the range is

- €88k - €107k for someone in a similar cost of market as UK, Germany etc, + stock options

- €79k - €97k for someone in a similar cost of market as Spain, Poland, Ukraine etc, + stock options

Apply

If this sounds interesting, please apply! Studies by several different sources have shown that on average men will apply for a job if they meet 60% of the application requirements. Women, non-binary people and POC will seek to match a much higher percentage of requirements before applying. If you're not sure you're the right fit, apply anyway and let us know what you bring to the table. We'd love to hear from you!

We're all about being transparent and setting clear expectations. That's why we've put together our hiring playbook and open-sourced our employee handbook . There you'll find a sneak peek of who we are, how we work and what you can expect in our hiring process.

title: Security Architect/Spezialist (m/w/x)
description:
Projektbeschreibung:

Technologie begeistert Sie? Uns auch!
Zur Verstärkung unseres Expertenteams bei unserem Kunden aus der Funk- und Kommunikationsbranche suchen wir einen Security Architect/Spezialist (m/w/x) in Festanstellung bei K-tronik.
Wir freuen uns darauf, Sie persönlich kennen zu lernen - und gemeinsam mit Leidenschaft und Teamgeist an spannenden Projekten und zukunftsweisenden Technologien zu arbeiten.

Aufgaben:

- Du entwirfst und bewertest Architekturen und Konzepte unter Berücksichtigung von Sicherheits-, Zulassungs- und Zertifizierungsaspekten
- Du führst Bedrohungsanalysen durch und leitest daraus Security-Anforderungen ab
- Du führst Risikoanalysen für Bedrohungen und Schwachstellen durch
- Du setzt Sicherheitsmaßnahmen auf Konzept- und Architekturebene um
- Du unterstützt und befähigst Entwickler dabei, Sicherheitsanforderungen korrekt umzusetzen („Enabling“)
- Du stellst die Informationssicherheit in den Projekten gemäß ISO 27001 und NIS-2 sicher

Qualifikationen:

- Du hast ein relevantes abgeschlossenes Studium oder vergleichbare Ausbildung und verfügst über praktische Erfahrung im Bereich Cyber- und IT-Security
- Du arbeitest prozessorientiert nach etablierten Sicherheitsstandards und -prozessen (z. B. Common Criteria)
- Du hast Erfahrung in Zulassungsprozessen sowie im BSI IT-Grundschutz
- Du kennst EU-Sicherheitsnormen wie Data Act, Cyber Resilience Act und Radio Equipment Directive
- Du verfügst über Kenntnisse im Bereich Informationssicherheit (ISO 27001, NIS-2)
- Du beherrscht Deutsch und Englisch sehr gut (jeweils in Wort und Schrift)

Benefits:

- Kollegiales und freundschaftliches Arbeitsklima
- Flexible Arbeitszeiten
- 30 + 1 Urlaubstage und flexible Urlaubsplanung
- Regelmäßige Team-Events
- Auszeichnung als Kununu TOP Company
- Corporate Benefits (Mitarbeiterangebote)
- Kostenlose Getränke
- Individuelle Weiterbildungsmöglichkeiten
- 360° Betreuung: Feedbackgespräche, Karriereplanung, Unterstützung bei Umzug, etc.
- EGYM Wellpass Firmenfitness
- Berufseinstieg

title: Founding Recruiter (m/f/x)
description:
01 · Why this role exists

Invest in Values. Produce in Freedom. Boost Europe. 

Behind every megawatt hour our customers save, there are people who make it happen. RIZM helps Europe's largest industrial companies, together around 2% of Europe's energy demand, make their energy decisions with AI. Our agent RIZMO works like a digital colleague. The colleagues we need most are the ones we haven't found yet.

Finding them is your job. We're about 15 people and growing fast, with open roles in engineering, value engineering and the public sector. There is no recruiting playbook yet and no HR department. You'll write the playbook and decide who RIZM becomes.

02 · Meet Diana, your teammate

Hi, I'm Diana. I run recruiting at RIZM today, 20 hours a week next to my studies, together with Lorenz, our Founders Associate. We've built the first funnel, but there are more good people out there than two part-time recruiters can reach. That's why we need you: someone who owns hiring full-time and takes it further than we can. You'll have Josh, our co-founder, as your sparring partner for offers and tricky decisions. Questions before you apply? Message me on LinkedIn. 

Diana 

03 · What you'll do

- Own hiring end to end: From the first message to the signed offer, for every open role at RIZM.

- Build the system: Design our process, stations, scorecards and tools from scratch, and later bring more recruiters and sourcers on board.

- Find the right people: Source engineers, energy experts and product people via LinkedIn, Juicebox, universities, communities and your own network.

- Win people over: Run first conversations, tell our story well and make every candidate feel looked after, even when the answer is no.

- Make it smart: Automate sequences, screening and reporting with AI, and always know where the funnel gets stuck.

- Get us seen: Careers page, job ads, events, university partnerships.

04 · What you bring

- Experience: A few years in recruiting or talent acquisition, ideally in startups or tech, including technical profiles.

- People sense: You spot potential that isn't on the CV and talk to engineers as equals.

- AI-native: You try new tools, build your own workflows and enjoy making things faster.

- Builder drive: You'd rather create structures than step into them, independently, reliably and fast.

- Ownership: You care about results, not activity, and you're motivated by being paid for them.

- Languages: Fluent German and English, written and spoken.

05 · Why you should apply now

You're the first full-time recruiter. What you build stays.

- Pay that follows your impact: A fixed salary plus uncapped variable pay and equity. Every hire you make shows up directly in what you earn.

- Direct line to the founders: Hiring is their top priority.

- A network that moves you forward: Sparring and learning with the networks of our investors Point 9 and Earlybird.

title: Group Product Manager (m/w/d) / Team Lead Product
description:
Einleitung

Bei Peter Park ist "Product" nicht einfach nur ein Unternehmensbereich. Hier trifft alles aufeinander: Wohin wir als Unternehmen wollen, was wir verkaufen, wie wir wachsen, was unsere Kunden erleben. Als Group Product Manager verantwortest du eine Product Area im Produktmanagement, führst ein Team von Product Managern und arbeitest täglich mit einem breiten Stakeholder-Feld zusammen. Wenn du wirklich gestalten und führen willst, ist das die richtige Stelle.

Was ist Deine Aufgabe?

- People Leadership, Coaching & Culture: Du hast die volle disziplinarische Verantwortung für ein Team von 2–3 Product Managern und prägst die Teamkultur mit dem Ziel, wachsende Eigenverantwortung und Empowerment im Team zu entwickeln.

- Produktstrategie & Alignment: Du entwickelst und verantwortest die Strategie für deine Product Area und stellst das kontinuierliche Alignment mit unseren Unternehmenszielen sicher. Du managst den Produktlebenszyklus und pflegst den Product Governance Prozess – schnell liefern, ohne Qualität zu opfern.

- Business Impact & Markt: Du steuerst Ressourcen für maximalen Impact und bewertest und verbesserst kontinuierlich die Kundenzufriedenheit auf Area-Ebene. Dafür hast du Markttrends und den Wettbewerb stets im Blick.

- Stakeholder-Management: Du hältst für deine Product Area die Fäden zusammen und hast stets das große Ganze im Blick. Dabei kommunizierst du sicher mit unterschiedlichen Unternehmensbereichen und Managementebenen.

Deine Fähigkeiten:

- Du bringst 7+ Jahre relevante Erfahrung als Senior PM, Lead PM oder Team Lead im Product Management mit – idealerweise in einem schnellwachsenden Start-up, Scale-up, SaaS- oder IoT-Umfeld.

- Du hast über 1,5 Jahre Erfahrung in der disziplinarischen Führung.

- Du hast eigenständig eine Produktstrategie auf Area-Ebene entwickelt und verantwortet – inkl. Roadmap-Planung.

- Du arbeitest sicher mit agilen Methoden und bist vertraut mit Outcome-Metriken und datenbasierter Entscheidungsfindung.

- Du verfügst über exzellente Kommunikationsfähigkeiten für unterschiedliche Zielgruppen und eine ausgeprägte Fähigkeit zur internen Kollaboration.

- Du sprichst fließend Deutsch und verfügst über gute Englischkenntnisse.

Work Setup:

- 40 Stunden pro Woche (Vertrauensbasis)

- Homeoffice Policy: 3 Tage im Office / 2 Tage remote

- Unbefristeter Arbeitsvertrag

- Team: 6 Kolleg:innen

- Teamgeist und Impact-Kultur: Bei uns zählt Deine Stimme! Wir leben flache Hierarchien und eine Kultur des "Du" vom ersten Tag an. Das bedeutet: kurze Entscheidungswege, direkter Austausch mit allen Ebenen und ein Team, das Dich aktiv unterstützt. Deine Ideen sind hier nicht nur willkommen, sondern werden gehört.

- Freiraum für Deine Ideen: Du übernimmst Verantwortung und kannst Deine Ideen aktiv einbringen. Wir fördern Deine Entwicklung – mit echtem Vertrauen in Deine Fähigkeiten.

Das bieten wir Dir zusätzlich

- Dein Plus: Betriebliche Altersvorsorge, Corporate Benefits und Jobrad-Leasing – und on top wählst du selbst zwischen einem bezuschussten Deutschlandticket oder EGYM Wellpass

title: Talent Acquisition Manager (m/w/d)
description:
Als neues Teammitglied stehen Sie bei uns an erster Stelle. Sie möchten nicht nur Positionen besetzen, sondern Recruiting-Strukturen aufbauen und verbessern? Verstärken Sie unser Group-HR-Team in Düsseldorf als Talent Acquisition Manager (m/w/d). In dieser Rolle verbinden Sie operatives Recruiting für Holding und Werke mit der Entwicklung einer gruppenweiten Recruiting-Strategie, dem Rollout unserer Recruiting-Plattform JOIN und ausgewählten Aufgaben der HR-Administration.

Die DIHAG Gruppe ist eine der führenden Gießerei-Gruppen in Europa. Unter ihrem Dach vereint die DIHAG traditionsreiche und moderne Gießereien sowie Bearbeitungszentren in Deutschland und Europa. Unsere Tochtergesellschaften agieren eigenständig in ihren jeweiligen Marktsegmenten und sind zugleich eng miteinander vernetzt. Gemeinsam entwickeln und fertigen wir hochwertige Gussprodukte für anspruchsvolle Anwendungen in Industrie, Mobilität, Maschinenbau und Infrastruktur. Dabei verbinden wir langjährige Erfahrung, technisches Know-how und Innovationskraft mit dem Anspruch, für unsere Kunden leistungsfähige und zuverlässige Lösungen zu schaffen.

Aufgaben

- Eigenständiges End-to-End-Recruiting für Holding und Werke: Bedarfsklärung, Erstellung von Ausschreibungen, Bewerbermanagement, Interviews, Auswahlkoordination und Vertragsvorbereitung

- Entwicklung und Umsetzung einer gruppenweiten Recruiting-Strategie unter Berücksichtigung von Personalbedarfen, Zielgruppen, Suchkanälen und internen Besetzungsmöglichkeiten

- Implementierung und Rollout der Recruiting-Plattform JOIN in allen Werken einschließlich Prozesskonfiguration, Anwenderschulungen und laufender Plattformbetreuung

- Gruppenweite Standardisierung von Tätigkeits- und Funktionsbeschreibungen sowie Ableitung einheitlicher Anforderungsprofile und Stellenausschreibungen

- Aufbau eines internen Recruitingprozesses mit internen Stellenausschreibungen, transparenten Bewerbungswegen und Abstimmung mit den lokalen HR-Bereichen

- Aktive Kandidatenansprache, Aufbau und Pflege von Talentpools sowie professionelle Begleitung der Bewerbenden entlang der gesamten Candidate Journey

- Beratung von Führungs- und Werksleitungen sowie lokalen HR-Bereichen zu Anforderungsprofilen, Interviewführung und Auswahlverfahren

- Mitgestaltung des Employer Brandings und der Arbeitgeberkommunikation sowie Steuerung von Jobportalen, Personalberatungen und weiteren Recruiting-Partnern

- Definition, Auswertung und Weiterentwicklung relevanter Recruiting-Kennzahlen wie Time-to-Hire, Bewerbungsquellen und Cost-per-Hire

- Sicherstellung einheitlicher, datenschutz- und AGG-konformer Recruiting-Abläufe; Abstimmung erforderlicher Beteiligungen der Arbeitnehmervertretungen mit zuständigen Stellen

- Vorbereitung und Verwaltung von Arbeitsverträgen, Zusatzvereinbarungen, Zeugnissen, Bescheinigungen und personalbezogener Korrespondenz nach Freigabe

- HR-Administration vom Eintritt über Onboarding und Vertragsänderungen bis zum Austritt, Pflege von Personalakten und Stammdaten sowie Abstimmung mit Payroll

Qualifikation

- Sie verfügen über eine abgeschlossene kaufmännische Ausbildung mit HR-Bezug oder ein einschlägiges Studium, beispielsweise in Betriebswirtschaft oder Personalmanagement

- Sie bringen mehrjährige Erfahrung im operativen Recruiting mit und haben idealerweise bereits Recruiting-Prozesse für mehrere Standorte oder Gesellschaften betreut

- Sie kennen digitale Bewerbermanagementsysteme und Recruiting-Plattformen; Erfahrung mit JOIN oder bei der Einführung neuer HR-Tools ist von Vorteil

- Sie können Stellenanforderungen in klare Tätigkeitsprofile und überzeugende Ausschreibungen übersetzen und kennen strukturierte Auswahl- und Interviewverfahren

- Sie verfügen über Kenntnisse in der HR-Administration und in der Erstellung personalbezogener Dokumente, insbesondere bei Eintritten, Änderungen und Austritten

- Sie kennen die Anforderungen an Datenschutz und AGG im Recruiting und berücksichtigen die Beteiligungsrechte der Arbeitnehmervertretungen

- Sie arbeiten eigenständig, konzeptionell und lösungsorientiert, steuern mehrere Projekte parallel und nutzen Kennzahlen zur Prozessverbesserung

- Sie überzeugen durch kommunikative Stärke, Serviceorientierung und Freude an der Zusammenarbeit mit Führungskräften und lokalen HR-Teams

Benefits

- Eine verantwortungsvolle Position in einer der führenden unabhängigen Gießereigruppen Europas

- Ein vielseitiges Aufgabengebiet zwischen operativem Recruiting, HR-Administration und gruppenweiter Strategieentwicklung

- Die Chance, JOIN gruppenweit einzuführen und einheitliche Recruiting-Standards sowie interne Besetzungswege mitzugestalten

- Kurze Entscheidungswege, ein kollegiales Arbeitsumfeld und eine sorgfältige Einarbeitung

- Eine leistungsgerechte Vergütung

- 30 Tage Urlaub pro Jahr

- Eine regelmäßige wöchentliche Arbeitszeit von 40 Stunden

- Modernes Büroumfeld mit der Möglichkeit zum Homeoffice

- Möglichkeiten zur fachlichen Weiterbildung und persönlichen Entwicklung

- Eine gute Work-Life-Balance und ein verlässliches Arbeitsumfeld

title: Head of Operations (m/w/d) · 11 Gameshow-Filialen · Remote mit Reisen
description:
Vollzeit · Festanstellung · Start sofort · Firmenwagen · Berichtet an den Gründer

Du führst 80+ Werkstudenten in 11 Filialen in ganz Deutschland. Filialleiter gibt es nicht. Du arbeitest von zu Hause, bist jede Woche in einer Filiale und greifst, wenn nötig, auch am Wochenende ein.

Gamer - Die Gameshow

Bei uns wird ein Ausflug mit Freunden oder Kollegen zur Gameshow. Aus über 20.000 Google Bewertungen haben wir 4,9 Sterne. 2027 wachsen wir weiter stark mit vielen neuen Filialen.

Spiele, Technik und Software sind unsere Stärke. Der Betrieb unserer Filialen ist es bisher nicht. Trotz guter Bewertungen zeigt das Feedback unserer Gäste, dass es vor Ort zu oft hakt, z. B. bei der Sauberkeit und beim Wohlfühlen. Uns fehlt die Erfahrung, Strukturen und Abläufe so aufzubauen, dass sie auch funktionieren, wenn niemand von uns da ist. Diese Erfahrung bringst du mit.

Deine Aufgabe

- Der Betrieb unserer 11 eigenen Filialen liegt bei dir: Teams, Abläufe und alles, was nötig ist, um Gäste vor Ort glücklich zu machen.
- Du führst die mehr als 80 Werkstudenten: von der Auswahl über das Training bis zum Abschied.
- Du baust die Strukturen auf, die heute fehlen. Welche das sind, findest du selbst heraus.
- Du bringst neue Filialen operativ an den Start.
- Du startest nicht allein: In deinem Team ist ein starker Operations Manager, der unsere Filialen und Werkstudenten sehr gut kennt.
- Die Richtung stimmst du direkt mit unserem Gründer ab.
Daran merken wir, dass es klappt

- Gäste loben die Filiale, statt sie zu bemängeln. Auch an einem vollen Samstag.
- Die Teams arbeiten auch dann nach Standard, wenn niemand zuschaut.
- Gute Werkstudenten bleiben und werben andere an.
- Der NPS in jeder Filiale steigt deutlich, die Personalkosten dagegen steigen nicht.
Der schwierigste Teil

- 11 Filialen, ein Besuch pro Woche: Jede Filiale siehst du nur einmal im Quartal.
- Dazwischen führst du über Systeme, Telefon und das Feedback der Gäste, das du in Echtzeit siehst.
- Standards zu entwickeln ist der leichte Teil. Der schwierige ist, dass sie auch ohne dich gelten.
Wie wir arbeiten

- Remote-First ohne Headquarter.
- Wir schreiben lieber, als zu telefonieren. Entscheidungen fallen in Minuten per Chat, nicht in einem Meeting.

description:

Aufgaben

Als Senior Fullstack Developer treibst du zusammen mit uns die Entwicklung unseres Backends, Frontends und unserer API voran. Du setzt neue Features eigenständig um und bist aktiv in Architektur- und Technologieentscheidungen eingebunden. 

Uns ist es wichtig, eine Applikation zu entwickeln, die nicht nur leistungsfähig, sondern auch für jede*n Nutzer*in leicht verständlich und angenehm zu bedienen ist.

Qualifikation

- Du hast bereits mit modernen Frameworks wie Ruby on Rails, Spring Boot oder Laravel entwickelt. Rails-Erfahrung ist ein Plus, aber wir legen vor allem Wert auf deine umfassende Fullstack-Kompetenz.

- Frontend-Entwicklung bereitet dir Freude. Wir nutzen Rails in Kombination mit Vue.js, um interaktive Features umzusetzen.

- Du hast den Gesamtüberblick über die Applikation und liebst die Arbeit sowohl am Backend als auch am Frontend.

- Du arbeitest dich gerne in neue Themen und Technologien ein und löst komplexe Probleme kreativ.

- Du möchtest ein Produkt maßgeblich mitgestalten, triffst gerne technische Entscheidungen und hast die Bedürfnisse der Kund*innen immer im Blick.

- Gute Deutschkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift.

Benefits

- Unbefristete Festanstellung in Vollzeit.

- Flexible Arbeitszeiten: Du bestimmst, wann du am produktivsten bist.

- Freie Wahl der Arbeitsmittel: Mac, mechanische Tastatur, Plugins, IDE – du entscheidest, was du brauchst, und wir sorgen dafür.

- Regelmäßige Teamevents: Wir legen Wert auf eine gute Unternehmenskultur – wir arbeiten zusammen, nicht nur nebeneinander.

- Von Anfang an Verantwortung übernehmen, unterstützt durch regelmäßiges Feedback.

- Raum für eigene Ideen, Erfahrungen und Eigeninitiative.

So läuft der Bewerbungsprozess bei uns ab 

Uns ist ein transparenter und fairer Auswahlprozess wichtig. Wir möchten dich und deine Fähigkeiten bestmöglich kennenlernen – gleichzeitig sollst auch du ein gutes Gefühl dafür bekommen, wer wir sind und wie wir arbeiten. Deshalb besteht unser Prozess aus drei klar strukturierten Schritten:

1. Kurzes Telefoninterview (ca. 30 Minuten) 

In einem ersten Gespräch lernen wir uns gegenseitig kennen. Wir stellen dir die Position, unser Team und unsere Arbeitsweise vor und beantworten alle deine Fragen. Gleichzeitig interessiert uns, was dich motiviert, welche Erfahrungen du mitbringst und was du dir von deiner nächsten Rolle wünschst.
Warum? – Der persönliche Eindruck zählt. Wir möchten herausfinden, ob wir gut zueinander passen – fachlich und menschlich.

2. Eignungsdiagnostik (ca. 2–3 Stunden, flexibel einteilbar) 

In diesem Schritt bitten wir dich, drei Bausteine zu absolvieren:

- Coding Challege : Du kannst deine Coding Skills zeigen.

- Einen kognitiven Leistungstest , der hilft, dein analytisches Denkvermögen objektiv zu erfassen.

- Einen kurzen Persönlichkeitsfragebogen , der Aufschluss darüber gibt, wie du arbeitest, kommunizierst und Probleme angehst.

Warum? – Wir glauben an eine fundierte und faire Entscheidungsgrundlage. Unsere Diagnostik-Tools helfen uns (und dir), besser zu verstehen, wo deine Stärken liegen und wie du am besten ins Team passt – ganz ohne Bias.

3. Technisches Interview (ca. 60–90 Minuten) 

In einem vertiefenden Gespräch mit unseren Entwickler*innen schauen wir uns gemeinsam die Ergebnisse der Challenge an, besprechen Lösungswege und tauschen uns über Architektur, Code-Qualität und deinen Entwicklungsstil aus. Dabei ist uns wichtig, dass du Fragen stellen kannst und wir auf Augenhöhe miteinander sprechen.

Warum? – Wir wollen sehen, wie du denkst, wie du Probleme angehst und welche Perspektiven du in unser Team einbringen kannst. Gleichzeitig bekommst du einen realistischen Eindruck davon, wie wir als Team arbeiten und mit welchen Technologien wir umgehen.

title: Senior DevOps Engineer
description:
At Ledgy, we’re on a mission to make Europe a powerhouse of entrepreneurship by building a modern, tech-driven equity management and financial reporting platform for private and public companies. In 2026, we aim to be the leading provider for European IPOs and reporting for share-based payments. We are a value-based company with a core focus on being humble, transparent, ambitious and impactful, all in order to delivery the best experience for our customers and end users.

We are proud to partner with some of the world’s leading investors. New Enterprise Associates led our $22m Series B round in 2022, with Philip Chopin joining Sequoia’s Luciana Lixandru on our board.

We were founded in Switzerland in 2017 and today we operate globally from offices in Zurich and London. We encourage diversity and are an international team coming from 26 different countries and speaking 25 different languages.

About the Role 

As a Senior DevOps Engineer at Ledgy, you'll build the infrastructure and tooling that help our engineers ship quickly and reliably. You'll join our Platform team, collaborating with engineers and InfoSec to improve CI/CD, observability, and cloud infrastructure for a product that helps companies manage equity.

Our challenge is to make delivery faster, production easier to operate, and AI-assisted development safer - while keeping complexity and costs in check.

Location: We hire remotely across Spain, Germany, Poland, and Romania.

The team you'll join: Platform - Builds the infrastructure and tooling that help our engineers ship quickly and reliably, working with InfoSec to improve CI/CD, observability, and cloud infrastructure.

What You'll Work On 

- Cloud infrastructure. Evolve our GCP and Kubernetes cloud architecture and setup with Terraform, improving reliability, simplicity, and cost visibility and enabling scaling to multiple availability regions.

- CI/CD and developer experience. Speed up feedback loops, reduce flaky builds, and turn recurring support requests into self-service tooling.

- Observability. Reduce alert noise, define meaningful SLOs, and make production issues easier to diagnose.

- Security and automation. Partner with InfoSec on secure delivery, access controls, and guardrails for AI-assisted workflows.

You'll also join our incident-response on-call rotation during working hours and help prevent recurring issues. As we expand our servicing of public companies and jurisdictions, this on-call might evolve to compensated 24h/7 hour rotation.

You'll Thrive in This Role If You 

Don't worry if you don't tick every box. These are the things that would make you an especially good fit.

- Have strong DevOps / SRE background designing and operating cloud infrastructure and production systems

- Have worked with Kubernetes and infrastructure as code, ideally GCP and Terraform

- Enjoy building fast, reliable CI/CD pipelines and improving developer experience

- Can diagnose issues across networking, infrastructure, and application code

- Write maintainable code and bring a practical approach to observability and security

- Value collaboration, mentorship, and thoughtful trade-offs between reliability, complexity, and cost

- Are curious about supporting AI-assisted development safely - no AI specialism required

Experience with Node.js, MongoDB or Temporal is a plus.

Our Tech Stack 

We work in TypeScript: React, Tailwind CSS, and tRPC on the front end, and tRPC, Node.js, MongoDB, and Temporal on the back end. Infrastructure runs on GCP, Terraform Cloud, Kubernetes, Docker, and GitHub Actions. For observability and incident response we use Grafana, Sentry, and PagerDuty.

You don't need to know all of it. We don't expect proficiency in every part of this stack. Strong infrastructure fundamentals and the ability to learn matter more than knowing every tool already.

What Your Journey Could Look Like 

First 30 days: 

- Get to know Ledgy, the Platform team, and our internal users with an onboarding buddy

- Explore our infrastructure and delivery workflows, and ship your first improvement

- Analyze current state of our cloud infrastructure and propose meaningful enhancements

First 3 months: 

- Independently deliver improvements to CI/CD, observability, or infrastructure design

- Share operational ownership and help reduce recurring friction for engineers

- Contribute to architecture discussions and document what others need to operate our systems

First 6-12 months: 

- Own DevOps and SRE function and DevOps initiatives from problem definition through rollout and adoption

- Deliver measurable improvements to developer experience, reliability, or cost

- Help shape our platform's direction and mentor other engineers

The interview process 

- Getting to know you (45 min): Meet with someone from our people team to talk about your experience and to ask questions about the role

- Live Coding (60 min): An equity domain problem to solve collaboratively using your preferred language and IDE. We want to see how you think, so this step does not allow AI. But you can freely look up syntax questions if you need to.

- System Design (60 min): A system design session where you will design an architecture for a problem from the Ledgy domain using a visual tool of your choice

- DDSA (45 min): A Deep Dive into real System Architecture that you have built, owned and monitored.

- Culture Interview: A chance to meet one of our founders and your hiring manager for a 30-minute chat about Ledgy's mission and values

- Offer 🎉

Being part of Ledgy means 

- Recharge and re-energize with flexible working hours, 25 days of vacation, and up to 40 days of remote work from outside your home country.

- We make space for your own professional development, with a generous yearly learning & development budget.

- This role will receive a competitive salary + benefits + equity. All salaries are aligned with competitively benchmarked ranges based on work location and levelling.

description:
Inside Sales Manager (m/w/d) – Nachunternehmer 

Du hast Biss, Hunger auf Erfolg und willst Deals closen, statt nur über Leads zu reden? Dann ist das hier dein Spielfeld.

Cosuno ist die größte Plattform, auf der Auftraggeber im Bau ihre Projekte ausschreiben und Handwerksbetriebe neue Aufträge finden. Der Nachunternehmer-Bereich ist unser am schnellsten wachsender Bereich, und 2027 wollen wir den Umsatz verdoppeln. Dafür suchen wir Closer, keine Verwalter.

Deine Aufgaben 

- Full Cycle: vom ersten Call über die Demo bis zum unterschriebenen Vertrag

Dein Setup 

- Jeden Morgen schlägt dir die KI deine besten Leads vor.

Woran wir dich messen 

- Umsatz gegen dein Monatsziel – das ist die Zahl, die zählt.

- Aktivität und Qualität: Calls, Demos, Conversion

- Entwicklung: wie schnell du Feedback umsetzt und dich anpasst

- Team: was du teilst und wie du andere besser machst

Das alles siehst du transparent im täglichen Team-Ranking.

Dein Profil 

- Mindestens 2 Jahre Vertrieb, idealerweise B2B und Full Cycle

- Du kannst belegen, dass du deine Ziele konstant übertriffst, also über 100 %.

- Closing-Mindset: Für dich zählt der Abschluss, nicht der Prozess.

- Du überzeugst am Telefon, per Mail und in der Demo.

- Du nutzt AI-Tools selbstverständlich, verstehst Prozesse und hast Lust, sie mit zu automatisieren.

- Du lernst schnell, nimmst Feedback an und willst jeden Monat besser werden.

- Verhandlungssicheres Deutsch (C2); Englisch ist ein Plus.

Was wir bieten 

- Fixum plus ungedeckelte Provision, jeden Monat ausgezahlt (optional: sechsstellig bei Zielerreichung) 

- Ein klarer Karrierepfad: vom Inside Sales Manager über Senior bis zum Account Executive oder Teamlead, mit Fast Track für Overperformer

- Onboarding und Coaching durch die Top-Performer im Team

- Ein ambitioniertes Team in einem Markt, der gerade erst digital wird

Warum wir?

- Gestalte ein Produkt mit echtem Impact: Wir lösen reale Probleme in einer der größten Industrien Europas – der Bauwirtschaft.

- Performance-Kultur: Ungedeckelte Provision, transparente Regeln und 100 % Eigenverantwortung für deinen Erfolg.

- Flexibilität: Arbeite remote oder in unserem modernen Office in Berlin-Friedrichshain.

- Team-Spirit: Internationales, dynamisches Team mit flachen Hierarchien und echtem Zusammenhalt.

- Wachstum: Regelmäßiges Feedback, 1:1s und Entwicklungsgespräche – wir wollen, dass du dich weiterentwickelst.

- Erfolge feiern: Ob Firmenevents oder Teamevents – wir gewinnen und feiern gemeinsam.

title: Automation Engineer - Facilities SCADA & PLC (f/m/d)
description:
The Role 

We are looking for an experienced Automation Engineer to take technical ownership of the Facilities Monitoring and Control System (FMCS) that keeps our fab running - the system that supervises every utility our production depends on, from cleanroom air and chilled water to process cooling, exhaust and power monitoring. The system is delivered and commissioned by an external integrator; from handover, it's yours. You won't be building it from scratch - you'll be the person who understands it well enough to keep it running, diagnose it when it misbehaves, extend it as we grow from pilot line to full production, and hold suppliers to account. If the FMCS has an issue at 03:00, you're the one who knows what to do.

To join our team, you should be excited to: 

- Operate, monitor and maintain our SCADA system (Siemens WinCC OA or Yokogawa DCS Centum) across servers, operator stations and displays

- Maintain and diagnose our Siemens S7-1500 PLCs and their remote I/O, and adapt control logic within the existing standardised structure

- Plan and perform loop checks end to end - tracing each signal from the field device through wiring, I/O and PLC all the way to the operator screen, and confirming that commands actually move valves, dampers and actuators

- Investigate and resolve alarms, communication faults and unexpected equipment behaviourduring live operation

- Verify instrument calibration and troubleshoot analog and digital field signals - multimeter in hand, not only from a screen

- Add new datapoints, screens, trends and reports, and tune alarms so operators trust the system

- Keep documentation current - as-built drawings, tag lists, change records - and uphold change control

- Act as the technical counterpart to contractors and vendors, and support qualification and audits with system evidence

Your Qualifications 

- One of two equivalent qualification paths: a completed apprenticeship as an Electronics Technician for Automation Technology plus further training as a state-certified technician (Techniker), or comparable - or a degree in Electrical Engineering, Automation Engineering or a related field, or comparable

- 5+ years of hands-on experience with industrial SCADA and PLC systems in a production environment - commissioning, operating or supporting, not only design

- Solid experience with Siemens S7 PLCs (TIA Portal / Step 7) - going online, reading and modifying logic, diagnosing faults on a running plant; experience with comparable PLC platforms is also welcome

- Strong SCADA engineering skills - ideally Siemens WinCC OA or Yokogawa DCS Centum, but experience with another platform (e.g. WinCC, PCS 7, Ignition, Aveva, Zenon) plus the willingness to grow into WinCC OA is just as welcome

- Practical experience with loop checks, instrument calibration and signal troubleshooting, and with reading P&IDs, loop diagrams and I/O lists

- A structured, disciplined approach to documentation and change control, and the confidence to say no to a change that compromises safety or system integrity

- Good command of English; German is a strong advantage given the site, suppliers and local contractors

Our work culture 

People Over Processes. At Black Semiconductor, flexibility is key—we ensure work adapts to life, not the other way around. We champion work-life harmony, where careers are meaningful and enriching. Our processes are human-centric, allowing you to focus on what matters

Let’s grow together. Your potential is our priority. We provide the autonomy to make a lasting impact and nurture your growth through a culture of continuous learning. We invest in your journey for professional and personal development

Your Health and Future Matter. Your well-being is paramount. We offer a comprehensive benefits package with outstanding insurance, pension and virtual stock options for your mental, physical, and financial health. Your peace of mind is our priority - in the present and future

We Live Openness. Collaboration and inclusivity are the cornerstones of our culture. We practice openness, fostering trust and respect. Individuality is our collective strength, fueling innovation and driving us forward

We connect chips – and people. We encourage qualified individuals from any background to apply. We foster an inclusive and supportive work environment that values collaboration, innovation, and growth. Join our team and be part of an organization dedicated to making a difference in the industry

This Technical Account Manager (TAM) role is part of the DataOne business within the ClearScore Group. The TAM role will work closely with the rest of the DataOne business which includes Product, Engineers, Analytics and Commercial counterparts in order to deliver the best experience to our partners.

I joined hx in January 2025 as a Senior People Partner and have recently stepped into the People Lead role. Outside of work, I’m an F1 fan and dog mum, so I’m no stranger to fast-paced environments or the occasional pit stop for walkies.

Our People team supports all things people at hx, from performance and engagement to the systems, insights and day-to-day operations that help our teams do their best work.

We’re growing the team and looking for someone to own our People reporting and analytics, while helping keep the operational side of the function running smoothly.

It’s a great opportunity for someone who enjoys turning data into meaningful insights, wants to make a real impact and is excited to help shape how the People team grows alongside the business.

Interested? Read more about the role and life at hx below.

About hyperexponential (hx)

At hyperexponential, we're building the AI-powered platform that enables the world's most critical decisions in a $7 trillion industry, which risks to take, and how to price them. These are the decisions that shape real-world outcomes: whether rockets successfully launch into space, autonomous vehicles make it to market, or communities recover after major storms.

Until now, insurance has been making billion-dollar decisions using outdated tools. We're changing that. Our platform brings together data, AI, and human expertise to give insurers the fastest path from submission to decision, helping them move faster, act smarter, and take on more risk with confidence.

Backed by a16z, Highland Europe, and Battery Ventures, we're scaling globally, already trusted by nearly 50 of the world's largest insurers, with zero churn and billions in premiums flowing through hx.

What began as a single product in one market has rapidly evolved into a multi-product, multi-territory platform powering every stage of pricing and underwriting. AI is at the core of what we do, from building the world's first domain-specific AI peer programmer for insurance (think GitHub Copilot with a PhD in actuarial science) to shaping agentic workflows that reinvent how this industry operates.

What makes hx different is the people who build it. Here, impact isn't tied to title or tenure, it's defined by the challenges you take on and the discipline you bring. Surrounded by peers who stretch you, you'll do the best, hardest work of your life in a company engineered to endure. If that sounds like you, join us in building what comes next.

About the People team

Our People team owns the systems and data that keep hx a high-performance, high-engagement place to work: performance and growth, people analytics, compensation and benefits, and HR compliance. We are building the reporting layer that lets the business make faster, better-evidenced decisions about its people rather than relying on instinct, and we work closely with Talent to connect hiring and pipeline data with performance and engagement data so leaders see the full employee lifecycle instead of fragments of it.

Inside People and Talent, AI has already changed how we screen, how we write up interviews and how we surface insight to leaders. There is far more to do. Plenty of what we do still runs on manual effort that could be designed out, and this role exists to go after that. We care much more about what you have built and put in front of real users than about the size of the team you have sat in, and impact here isn't tied to title or tenure.

You will work directly with People Leaders, with real scope to shape how the team works as we grow. One thing worth being direct about: there is no finished playbook here. If you need a well-defined remit and clear instruction to do your best work, this will be frustrating. If you would rather find the problem yourself and build the fix, you will have a lot of room..

What you'll be doing

- Build the AI tooling that our People and Talent function runs on. Agents that answer the questions currently landing in our inbox, skills that draft the documents we write manually, workflows that pull our systems together. This is the core of the role rather than a project on the side.

- Build out the People reporting layer, including dashboards on retention, attrition and engagement, and get to the point where you can tell us what the numbers mean, not just what they are.

- Work with Talent to connect hiring and pipeline data to People data, and make that view something leaders can interrogate themselves.

- Learn our people processes properly, starting with onboarding, payroll data integrity and the performance cycle, then rebuild the parts that depend on manual effort.

- Support our performance review cycles in Lattice and our engagement surveys, help analyse what comes out of them, and automate the parts that should not need a person.

- Help keep our HRIS data accurate, including records, reporting and system troubleshooting.

What you'll need to have done

- Built and shipped something with AI that other people used, whether that is an agent, a script, a tool, a bot or a side project.

- Got past the first version. We will ask how you tested it, what it got wrong with real users and what you changed as a result. If you have a long list of things you have experimented with, we want to hear what each one taught you.

- Worked with more than one model or platform, and formed a view on what each is good for.

- Worked with a real dataset, cleaned it up, and drawn a conclusion you could defend.

- Been responsible for keeping a system or record accurate, whether that is a tracker, a membership list, a codebase or admin for a part-time role.

- Handled something that needed to stay confidential, or can show us how you think about handling sensitive information.

- Genuine interest in how organisations work, and the willingness to learn a domain where the detail matters and the consequences of getting it wrong land on real colleagues.

How we build in an AI-forward company 

hx is a maximally AI-forward company because we believe AI should amplify what exceptional people can achieve. Everyone here is a builder. That means staying close to what’s changing, continuing to learn, and using AI to raise the quality, pace and ambition of your work.

We expect everyone to actively experiment with AI and agentic systems, whether at work or in their personal lives. This means going beyond prompting, exploring what agents can do autonomously, and learning by doing. You don't need to be an engineer, but you do need to be curious, hands-on and willing to push what's possible.

Your current environment is context, not the answer. We’re interested in how you think about what should be possible now, not simply how things are done where you work today. We care about judgement, creativity and ownership, not simply using more tools.

The bar is simple: your work should be meaningfully better because of how you operate in this new world.

Compensation

This role sits within a £40,000 - £55,000 salary range. At hx, we're committed to salary transparency, you'll always have clarity on pay early in the process, and our Talent Partner will share more detail with you during initial conversations. We're also working towards publishing salary information for all roles globally.

Because we're building at the intersection of technology/SaaS and insurance, our roles don't always map neatly onto traditional benchmarks. Our approach is to design compensation that's competitive in the market, fair across teams, and aligned with the impact our people make.

Benefits

- £5,000 training and conference budget for individual and group development.

- 25 days of holiday plus 8 bank holidays (33 days total).

- Company pension scheme via Penfold.

- Mental health support and therapy via Spectrum.life .

- Individual wellbeing allowance via Juno.

- Private healthcare insurance through AXA.

- Income protection and Life Insurance.

- Cycle to Work Scheme.

Additional perks

- Top-spec equipment (laptop, screens, adjustable desks, etc.).

- Regular remote and in-person hackathons, lunch and learns, socials, and games nights.

- Team breakfasts and lunches, snacks, drinks fridge, and a fun office at The Ministry.

- Exceptional opportunities for personal development and growth as we build something remarkable together.

Interview process

- Initial call with our Talent team to kick things off and learn more about your background.

- Manager interview with our People Lead to explore your experience in more depth.

- Skills assessment, presenting a People Analytics deliverable to the team.

- Values interview to get to know how you work and how that aligns with hx's culture with our VP of People and Senior Director of Finance and Operations.

- Meet the CEO

Our commitment to Diversity

hxer's are at the centre of everything we build. We know that progress depends on diverse perspectives, and we are committed to creating an environment where everyone can thrive, grow, and make an impact. We recognise there is always more to do, and we take responsibility for shaping a workplace that is not only diverse but genuinely inclusive.

Diversity is not just the right thing to do, it is key to solving the complex challenges we choose to take on. By welcoming people from all backgrounds and experiences, we strengthen our ability to question assumptions, push boundaries, and design solutions that endure.

If you're energised by complexity and motivated to grow, we encourage you to apply and join our global team.

Next steps

If this opportunity resonates with you, we encourage you to apply or share it with your connections! Our dedicated talent team reviews all applications, and we promise to provide feedback regardless of the outcome.

For more information about applying and to view other opportunities, you can visit our careers page.

Check out our blog at Insights & Blog - hyperexponential

We handle all background checks sensitively and in full compliance with relevant regulations. All applicant data will be processed in accordance with data protection regulations and our privacy policy.

About the Team 

OpenAI’s Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) team turns research breakthroughs into production-grade systems. We operate at the intersection of deployment and development – working closely with OpenAI Research, Product and Partnerships.

About the Role 

As a Deployment Lead, you will define how OpenAI delivers complex systems to Semiconductor customers. You will focus on the semiconductor vertical to deploy next-generation AI capabilities. Success will be measured first and foremost by impact - deployments that deliver measurable value against customer goals, drive adoption, and become critical to their workflows. Additional measures of success include delivery reliability (milestones hit, low reopen/churn), operating leverage (patterns reused across deployments), judgment under pressure, and product impact (field signal that shifts roadmaps/architectures).

- Have strong technical fluency and sharp sequencing instincts. Confident discussing technical details, pressure-testing architectures, and making trade-offs.

title: Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE), Cyber - London
description:
About the Team 

OpenAI’s Forward Deployed Engineering team builds with customers to bring frontier AI into production. Our Cyber FDEs partner with the security and engineering teams that defend globally critical systems, from enterprise software to the core infrastructure it runs on. Cyber FDEs work closely with our Product, Research, and Go-to-Market teams to adapt our products and models to what customers need to defend their systems.

About the Role 

You’ll build systems that give defenders an advantage at a scale few engineering teams encounter. You might help an enterprise identify, test, and deploy patches across hundreds of thousands of code repositories, or help a security team analyze petabytes of logs for signs of malicious agents or coordinated attacks. Across these deployments, you’ll build tools that customer engineers can trust to support consequential security decisions.

You’ll work directly with customer security teams, from CISOs to frontline analysts. As AI changes how attackers operate, you’ll help these teams determine where their defenses need to evolve, prioritize what to build, and validate solutions with the engineers who will operate them. Alongside OpenAI’s account teams, you’ll translate security priorities into deployed systems that help defenders cover more ground.

You’ll also help shape what OpenAI builds next. When you identify a gap between what defenders need and what today’s models or products can do, you’ll partner with Research and Product to define, build, and test capabilities that address it.

This role is based in London. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week. We offer relocation assistance. Travel up to 50% is required.

In this role you will: 

- Partner with customer security leaders and OpenAI’s Go-to-Market team to scope engagements, establish responsibilities, and define measurable success criteria.

- Lead technical design and implementation alongside customer engineers. Integrate agents into security workflows, establish access boundaries, and determine which actions require human review.

- Build evaluations grounded in the decisions defenders make. For a patching agent, test whether a fix blocks a known exploit while preserving expected application behavior. For a detection system, replay historical attacks alongside normal traffic to measure detection speed and false-positive rates.

- Guide production rollout with the engineers who will operate the system. Provide the observability and controls they need to understand system behavior, intervene when necessary, and expand adoption with confidence.

- Translate successful approaches across deployments into reusable tools and engineering practices that other defenders can adopt.

You might thrive in this role if you: 

- 5+ years of software engineering experience, including building and shipping production software.

- Experience protecting production systems through work in security engineering, infrastructure, SRE, DevOps, or product engineering.

- Experience building and evaluating AI agents for software engineering workflows.

- Experience with CI/CD pipelines and practices that maintain code quality, reliability, and security.

- Ability to navigate unfamiliar codebases and contribute maintainable, production-quality changes.

- Ability to communicate technical concepts and trade-offs to engineering teams and senior security stakeholders.

Additional experience includes: 

Cybersecurity spans many disciplines, and while we’re primarily looking for strong engineering generalists, we’d love to hear about deeper experience in any of the following areas:

- Security curiosity and experimentation: You read CVE write-ups because you want to understand how things break. You may have built an agent honeypot to test a hypothesis—or prove a point—and enjoy turning a security question into a hands-on experiment.

- Security community engagement: You enjoy exchanging ideas with defenders, whether that’s discussing security strategy with a CISO at Black Hat or comparing technical approaches with frontline practitioners.

- Application security: You’ve written CodeQL queries or Semgrep rules, built fuzzing harnesses, or discovered and responsibly disclosed vulnerabilities.

- Automated remediation: CI/CD is your happy place. You’ve built tooling that turns security findings into tested patches, dependency upgrades, or configuration changes across large codebases.

- Detection engineering: You’ve written and deployed detections using Sigma, YARA, Splunk, or KQL and tested them against attacker behavior.

- Cloud and identity security: You’ve designed cloud IAM architectures and investigated abuse of workload identities, role hierarchies, or cross-account trust.

- Security research: You’ve reverse-engineered malware, developed exploit reproductions, or contributed to vulnerability research.

- Agent security: You’ve tested agents for prompt injection, tool misuse, or credential exposure and built defenses against them.

description:
About the Team 

The Adoption, Innovation, and Transformation team within OpenAI for Government helps government organizations turn OpenAI products into durable capabilities and measurable mission impact.

We work alongside public servants to move from initial exploration to confident, responsible, organization-wide use of AI. Our work combines hands-on enablement, adoption strategy, deployment support, community, content, and practical transformation tailored to government missions and operating environments.

By translating the potential of OpenAI’s technology into better individual workflows, stronger teams, and improved public services, we help government customers deepen adoption, build lasting organizational capability, and spend more time on mission.

About the Role 

The Enablement Lead, Government is a specialist role focused on delivering high-impact enablement and adoption services across OpenAI’s product suite. This role is responsible for designing and delivering experiences that support repeatable adoption frameworks, drive sustained activation, expand the breadth and depth of usage, and produce measurable value for government organizations.

This role sits at the intersection of enablement, education, adoption, community, content, and customer experience. title: Account Executive
description:
View our much better version of this job spec on our careers page: https://juro.notion.site/ae 

***

THE KEY BITS

- Location : We can currently only accept applications from candidates that are located and have long-term working rights in the UK.

- Flexibility : We have office hubs in London and Boston, plus remote teams across several European countries. Under our choice-first work approach, you can work fully remotely from Day 1. That said, we’ve found people generally ramp faster when they spend a few days a week in the office alongside the team (esp. in the early months) and we hope you’ll want to.

- Salary : We benchmarked £62-70k base + 100% variable (OTE £124-140k) with accelerators, at IC3 level in our progression framework for someone based in the UK.

- Interviews : 3 stages totalling around 3 hours over about 3 weeks.

- Start date : As soon as you can start.

- Reporting to : Max Baldry-Steen, Director of Sales

- More info : The FAQ below, juro.com/careers , our handbook or ask ----- anything.

HELP US HELP THE WORLD AGREE FASTER

Juro has big ambitions: to make it incredibly easy for anyone to agree and manage legal contracts. And we'll need help doing it . 

Legal tech is on the rise, with Goldman Sachs estimating that 44% of legal tasks can be automated with generative AI. With the brand we have built and the agility of early stage we are well placed to capture this opportunity.

Buyers come to Juro because we're easy to use and fast to implement, AI runs through the whole product and our product team ships fast. To keep up with that demand in 2027, we're growing our Account Executive team.

Your role is to drive new business growth at Juro. That means:

- Meet or beat your ARR target (around $800k new business a year).

- Build a strong pipeline, with a good share of it from leads you generate yourself.

- Land a clear value narrative with prospects: real pain, a business case, buy-in from several stakeholders.

- Keep your CRM and forecast reliable and accurate.

- Run a high-velocity motion that makes it easy for smaller companies to buy Juro, alongside larger $100k+ deals.

We care about building a diverse team where everyone feels they belong. That’s why our perks & benefits and choice-first work approach are designed with inclusivity in mind. Read more in our diversity, inclusion & belonging hub . 

WHO WE LOOK FOR 

Research shows that while men apply to jobs if they meet ~60% of criteria, women and those in traditionally under-represented groups tend to apply only if they check all boxes. So if you think you have what it takes but don't meet every single point above, please still get in touch. We'd love to have a chat and see if you could be a great fit. 

To succeed here: 

Every Juror finds their balance across our four Principles . We hire, develop and celebrate people who live them every day.

Curious how you’d fit? Try our personality quiz to see how you map against our principles.

On top of that, you have been part of a journey where: 

- You carried and hit a quota of around $800k a year at a B2B SaaS scale-up, incl. a good share of pipeline you built yourself.

- You sold in a high-velocity motion - 5-week cycles and ACVs around $20-50k — you also closed some larger deals.

- You multi-thread by default, and your discovery builds a business case with several stakeholders, not a feature tour.

- You use AI every day in your sales work (research, call prep, follow-up) and have opinions about what works.

This job likely isn’t for you if: 

- Your quota, velocity or ACV are far from ours. Quotas under $600k, 90+ day cycles, or deals well outside $20-100k usually make ramping here hard.

- You’re waiting for marketing to fill your pipeline. Our inbound is strong, but the best reps here build their own.

- You rely on a single champion to carry the deal.

- You wait for the buyer to set next steps. Here, AEs ask for the deal and drive it.

- You don't want regular feedback. We share call scorecards and pipeline data openly, and we expect you to act on them quickly.

- Your pitch is "sales-y". We sell to legal and operations leaders, who dislike that style.

OUR MISSION

Juro exists to help the world agree faster by making it incredibly easy for anyone to agree and manage legal contracts.

The load on legal teams is increasing as business teams move faster with the help of AI. The only way out is to deploy AI within the legal team so that (a) routine contract work can be executed autonomously and (b) lawyers’ time is reserved for problem solving.

It’s like having an extra team member that is always on and takes on heavy lifting. Just like an in-house lawyer, Juro:

- is present for, and trusted by, business teams

- owns contracts from first draft to signature and beyond

- builds judgement from every contract it works on

…all within guardrails controlled by the legal team.

You’ll join a small AI team led by Marco, our LLM Tech Lead , working closely with our CTO, Product, Web and DevOps teams. You’ll work across data, post-training, evals, and model behavior, taking ideas from failure analysis to production.

The problems are real: personalization, character consistency, long conversations, better evals, multilingual behavior, and faster training cycles. 

If you want to shape model behavior at consumer scale, this is the role. 

Key Responsibilities

- Fine-tune open-weight LLMs using SFT, LoRA/QLoRA and post-training methods such as DPO and GRPO

- Diagnose model failures and turn them into experiments. Decide whether the answer is better data, post-training, prompting or classifiers

- Build training data and evals that directly shape what gets trained next

- Improve model behavior across personalization, consistency, tone, multilingual and group interactions

- Ship to production and use real user behavior to guide the next iteration

- Speed up the training loop so experiments are faster, easier to compare, and more reproducible

- You’ve personally post-trained open-weight LLMs for a user-facing product and shipped them to production

- Strong Python, PyTorch and Hugging Face , with hands-on GPU training and debugging

- You build data and evals yourself and make decisions from evidence

- You can take work beyond notebooks into production 

- You use AI tools daily in your own engineering work

- You are fully comfortable working with uncensored models and explicit NSFW content , including harmful material when developing and evaluating moderation system

Bonus points

- Experience with conversational AI, roleplay products, or highly personalized consumer AI

- Multilingual LLMs

- Moderation, safety, or adversarial testing

- Multimodal models

- Open-source LLM / post-training contributions

title: Manager - Transaction Services
description:
About Unity Advisory 

Unity Advisory is a modern advisory business built for today's CFO, with connected solutions across finance, deals and tax. Focussed on client outcomes, seasoned experts lead every engagement, in an operating model powered by AI and free from audit conflict.

Unity Advisory is a new kind of partner for the office of the CFO. Founded by senior leaders from the world's top advisory firms and backed by Warburg Pincus, we provide integrated finance, commercial, tax and deals support: expert advice, sharper execution, and delivery models built around how organisations operate today. CFOs need trusted advisers without legacy complexity, so we pair expert human judgement with proprietary AI workflows and smart automation, free from audit conflicts.

The Role 

We built our deals practice around the client's decision: whether to buy, whether to sell, at what price, on what terms. We work alongside our clients rather than at arm's length, in the room while the deal decision is being made, and our support carries on beyond signing: into the 100-day plan, the hold period and the eventual exit. And that support draws on the whole firm: our tax, finance and commercial specialists work as one team with the deals practice, so the advice a client gets after signing is as integrated as the diligence that came before it.

We're looking for a Manager to join our Financial Due Diligence team. You'll run buy-side and sell-side engagements day to day: getting into the numbers, managing the team on the ground, and making sure clients get clear, well-supported findings on time.

You'll bring solid FDD or transaction services experience from a Big 4 or top-tier advisory firm, and own an engagement from scoping through to final findings. You'll work alongside our Partners and Directors and directly with clients and target company management from day one. This is a hybrid role based in our Mayfair office.

What You'll Do 

• Manage buy-side and sell-side financial due diligence engagements from scoping through to completion.

• Analyse quality of earnings, net working capital, cash flow and other issues that decide a deal, and turn the findings into a clear, well-supported story for the client.

• Run the engagement team day to day: reviewing work, coaching junior staff, and keeping everyone (including the client) up to speed on progress.

• Interview target company management and build working relationships with clients, private equity investors, and other advisors on the deal.

• Draft and quality-check diligence deliverables so they're accurate, clear, and ready for Director or Partner sign-off.

• Work alongside Unity's data and AI specialists to make our analytics standard practice on every engagement.

• Take part in business development: proposals, pitches, and staying close to opportunities as they arise.

What You'll Bring 

• 5+ years' experience in Financial Due Diligence or Transaction Services from a Big 4 or top-tier advisory firm.

• Hands-on experience managing buy-side and sell-side FDD assignments from start to finish.

• Strong technical grounding in accounting and the deal issues that matter most: quality of earnings, working capital, and cash flow.

• A track record of being an excellent team player in multidisciplinary engagements.

• Clear and confident communication (both written and verbal) with clients and senior stakeholders.

• Curiosity and genuine interest in how technology and AI evolve financial due diligence practice and playing a key role in shaping it.

• Qualified accountant (ACA, ACCA, CIMA or equivalent).

Nice to Have 

• Experience with Private Equity clients or PE-backed portfolio companies.

• Exposure to cross-border or international transactions.

• Experience with data and analytics tools such as Power BI, Alteryx, or Databricks.

• Sector experience in areas like TMT, Consumer, Healthcare, Business Services and Industrials.

Additional Information 

We are committed to an inclusive and accessible recruitment process. Please let us know if you need any reasonable adjustments or support when applying or arranging your interview.

We do not accept unsolicited CVs from third-party agencies.
