title: Senior Platform Engineer
description:
Senior Platform Engineer

Permanent employee · Full-time · Berlin (HQ)

Our Mission For You

European energy costs are twice as high as in the US and China, and electricity demand is expected to double by 2050. This puts European industry under massive cost pressure – and companies need to act now.

trawa is building the solution: the first integrated B2B energy platform that brings together energy procurement, energy management and the marketing of flexible assets in one product. This helps companies save up to 30% on their recurring electricity costs while switching to renewable energy.

We're the fastest-growing B2B energy platform in Europe. Active in Germany and Austria now, and expanding operations to a third market in 2027. We're on the road to European scale and move fast – the market window is open and we intend to own it.

Now we are looking for a Senior Platform Engineer to build the foundation every trawa engineer relies on.

About trawa

trawa is a tech-driven scale-up based in Berlin with around 100 employees, combining deep energy market expertise with in-house software development. We've raised over €35M to date, most recently a €24M Series A in May 2025, backed by Balderton, Headline, Speedinvest, AENU, Magnetic and Tiny VC. This role is based in our Berlin office, where we work together in person most of the week. We offer flexible working hours, so you can shape your day in a way that works for you.

The Team

Our Platform team owns our infrastructure, shared tooling and developer experience, so your work shapes how fast and how safely the whole company ships. You'll work with engineers across the company and see the impact of your work across every team.

Who We Are Looking For

- Impact focus: You focus on impact, not just technical outcomes, and you care about what your work makes possible for others.

- Natural collaborator: People enjoy working with you, and you build strong relationships across teams.

- Platform experience: You have at least 8 years of experience in a platform, DevOps or SRE role.

- Hands-on AWS and IaC: You have deep hands-on experience with AWS and infrastructure as code, ideally Terraform.

- Distributed systems: You have built or run distributed services in production, with a strong grasp of security, reliability, observability and cost efficiency.

What You'll Do

- Build and run scalable, secure, highly available AWS infrastructure that powers our mission-critical services.

- Improve CI/CD pipelines, observability tooling and internal platforms so teams ship faster and with confidence.

- Embed security into our infrastructure and pipelines, covering access management, secrets and compliance needs.

- Partner with engineers, share best practices and make the right way the easy way.

Our Tech Stack

- AWS, Terraform, Spacelift, Docker, GitHub Actions

- Python, TypeScript

- Dash0, Sentry, Incident.io

90 Day Goals

After 6 Weeks (Onboarding): 

- Current setup: You have a comprehensive understanding of trawa's current tech stack, infrastructure and security posture.

- Team relationships: You have met the engineering teams, learned how they build, ship and run their services, and developed relationships with your key stakeholders.

Month 3 (Ramp-Up): 

- Infrastructure ownership: You own parts of our AWS infrastructure and Terraform codebase.

- Workflow friction: You have found the biggest friction points in our developer workflow and proposed ways to fix them.

- Platform improvement: You have led a meaningful platform improvement from design to rollout.

Why Us?

Impact: European SMEs spend between €150k and €10M per year on electricity – most are overpaying and locked into outdated procurement. Your work will directly change how thousands of companies buy, manage and use energy. The impact is measurable, the market is massive, and the timing is now.

Ownership: We empower our team members to take ownership of their work and drive results, regardless of background or experience level.

Learning & Growth: We provide an annual budget and dedicated time for professional development. You'll have opportunities for mentorship, learning and career progression.

Diversity and Inclusion: We're an equal opportunity employer, and our team reflects that. Our organisation brings together over 15 nationalities, contributing a variety of languages, experiences and perspectives. At trawa, we're family-friendly with parents across all levels, and our diversity is represented throughout the company, including leadership. We're committed to an inclusive environment where everyone can do their best work.

Package & Benefits: We offer a competitive compensation package including salary and stock options, 30 days of vacation, and a range of benefits including subsidies for home internet and lunches, a Sports Club membership, dedicated learning days with an annual learning budget, plus a weekly team lunch and regular team events.

At trawa, we're dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive and authentic workplace. If you're excited about this role but your experience doesn't align perfectly, we encourage you to apply – you may be the right fit for this or another opportunity.

Someone has to own the People initiative that doesn’t fit neatly into anyone’s week and the case nobody else should be handling. That someone is you — not as an escalation point, but as the person who runs the day-to-day of this function. 

THE MOMENT

Cloudscaler is 130 people today. We’ll be 170 by the end of this year, and roughly double again in 2027. The People function is being built in real time alongside that growth, rather than inherited from someone who left years ago.

You’ll be the first hire into the People team. For roughly your first year you’ll be the only People professional alongside the CPO, which means running the whole day-to-day of the function: the hardest casework and initiatives, and the operational core that keeps everything moving. A People Partner is planned to join later in 2027, and at that point the operational administration moves to them.

This is also a role built with room to grow. As the team expands beyond that second hire, we expect this role to take on day-to-day operational leadership of the People Partner practice, but that isn’t the shape of it on day one.

WHAT MAKES THIS DIFFERENT

In most People teams, the senior generalist is just a People Partner with a harder case queue. Here, the difference is ownership, not just difficulty.

- Complex casework: Rather than simply handling harder cases, you’ll own the most complex cases end to end, with no hand back.

- People initiatives: Rather than contributing to initiatives someone else drives, you’ll own them from design through to embedding.

- Decision-making: Rather than escalating ambiguity upward, you’ll make the sensible call and document your reasoning.

- CPO partnership: Rather than acting in a support role to the CPO, you’ll be an operational partner they can confidently delegate to.

To be clear about the level: The CPO still designs the People strategy and the systems architecture. You own how it runs day to day, and you’re trusted to run a whole initiative, not just a case. That is a different job to People Partner, not a bigger version of the same one.

THE ROLE

You’ll sit in the People team reporting to the Chief People Officer. Three strands make up the job:

- Casework: The employee relations situations with the most complexity or sensitivity land with you, start to finish.

- Initiatives: When the CPO needs a piece of work owned (a policy rollout, a wellbeing programme, a piece of the reward or benefits agenda), you take it from design through to something that runs.

- Operations: Until the People Partner joins, you’ll own payroll and benefits administration, onboarding, screening and security clearances, and keeping Rippling accurate.

When the People Partner joins, they’ll report to the CPO. You won’t manage them formally, but you’ll lead their handover, you’ll be the person they come to first, and your judgement will set the standard for how this function operates day to day.

WHERE THE ROLE STARTS AND STOPS

New roles get vague, so here is the boundary as we see it today.

Yours 

- The most complex and sensitive employee relations casework, end to end.

- Full ownership of People initiatives, from design to embedding.

- Acting as the CPO’s operational partner on ambiguous or cross-cutting problems.

- Until the People Partner joins (planned for later in 2027):

- Payroll and benefits administration, including the monthly payroll cycle in Rippling and Mintago.

- Pre-onboarding, onboarding and probation.

- Background screening in Zinc.

- Security clearance coordination.

- Rippling data quality, workflows and reporting.

- Our working groups and committees.

- Once the People Partner joins:

- A structured handover of the operational core.

- Day-to-day guidance for the People Partner.

Shared 

- Ashby, which Talent Acquisition owns. You’ll work in it from offer through to start date on every hire until the People Partner joins, and on senior hires after that.

- Mentoring and supporting the People Partner on their casework and initiatives, once they join.

Not yours 

- Recruitment delivery, which sits with Talent Acquisition.

- The design of the People strategy, the operating model and the systems architecture, which sit with the CPO.

- Formal line management of the People Partner, who will report to the CPO.

THE STACK

- Rippling: Our single source of truth. Until the People Partner joins you’ll run it day to day, including the monthly payroll cycle, data quality and workflows, and you’ll use its reporting at a level that supports whole initiatives.

- Zinc: Background screening. You’ll run checks for every new joiner until the People Partner joins, and stay close to the senior and sensitive hires after that.

- Ashby: Owned by Talent Acquisition. You’ll work in it from offer through to start date on the hires you’re responsible for.

- Claude: A daily tool here. You’ll use it for casework preparation, drafting policy and communications, and pulling together the analysis behind an initiative.

- Mintago: Our employee benefits and financial wellbeing platform (pensions, salary sacrifice and financial advice). You’ll administer it and keep enrolment accurate until the People Partner takes it on.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

- Own the hardest casework. You’ll run our most complex and sensitive employee relations cases end to end, with the CPO there to sense-check rather than take over.

- Own initiatives, not tasks. You’ll take a People initiative from a rough brief to something that’s running and embedded, rather than handing it back once the interesting part is done.

- Run the operational core. Until the People Partner joins, you’ll own the monthly payroll cycle in Rippling, benefits administration including Mintago, onboarding, background screening and security clearances. Accurate, on time, and documented as you go.

- Hand it over well. When the People Partner arrives, you’ll give them a working system and a clear handover, then stay the person they come to first and the judgement others in the function measure themselves against.

- Partner with senior leaders. You’ll be credible with leaders on the most difficult conversations: complex change, capability, and situations without a clean playbook.

- Use AI properly. You’ll use Claude daily to take time out of your own week, checking anything that touches a decision about a person and owning the outcome.

- Improve what you find. You’ll spot the gaps in policy, process or practice before anyone else does, and bring the CPO a considered view on the fix, not just the problem.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE AT 12 MONTHS

- You’re running the most complex ER cases with confidence, and the CPO isn’t being pulled into them.

- At least one or two People initiatives have gone from a rough brief to something genuinely embedded, owned by you.

- Payroll, benefits, onboarding and clearances run accurately and on time, and every process is documented well enough to hand over.

- You’ve helped shape the People Partner hire, so the handover is ready when they land.

- Senior leaders treat you as a credible operational partner, not an escalation point.

- You’ve made and documented sensible calls in genuinely ambiguous situations, and they’ve held up.

- The CPO can hand you an ambiguous problem and trust it gets shaped properly.

WHO WE’RE LOOKING FOR

- Deep employee relations experience. You’ve run complex disciplinaries, grievances and change situations yourself, and you know exactly when to escalate and when not to. CIPD qualification, or solid progress towards it, is welcome.

- A track record of owning initiatives. You can point to work you took from a brief to something that actually ran, not just a project you contributed to.

- Hands-on with the operational detail. You’ve owned or closely supported a payroll cycle, benefits administration and onboarding, and you’re comfortable being accountable for their accuracy while also carrying the senior work.

- Credible with senior leaders. You can hold your own in a difficult conversation with someone under real pressure and be listened to.

- Comfortable operating near-autonomously. You don’t need a playbook for everything. You make a sensible call, write it down, and check it with the CPO afterwards.

- Ready to grow into people leadership. You won’t formally manage anyone at the start, but you’ll induct and guide the People Partner when they join, and you should want to lead a team as the structure catches up.

- Discreet and organised at volume. Complex casework and live initiatives, often at the same time. You’ll need a system, and it can’t be your memory.

THE HONEST PART

This role sits in an odd space for now: senior in scope and judgement, without a team underneath it yet. Until the People Partner joins later in 2027, you’ll also be the whole operational team, so a payroll deadline and a complex grievance can land in the same week. That eases as the function grows, but it means the authority you carry day to day has to come from the quality of your work, not a job title.

You are not designing the People strategy or the systems architecture. The CPO does that. What you get instead is real ownership of the hardest cases and the initiatives that matter, a close working relationship with the CPO, and a genuine path toward leading the People Partner practice as it grows.

This probably isn’t for you if you want a formal team from day one, or if you’d rather leave payroll and onboarding to someone else. It probably is for you if you want to prove you can run this function well enough, top to bottom, that a team gets built around you.

If that sounds like the challenge you’ve been looking for, let’s talk.

title: Head of Business Development, Defence

Customer insight into product 

- Bring user needs back into product and data strategy, helping ExTrac stay ahead of market demand.

Building the defence BD function

- Establish the pipeline discipline, qualification standards and playbooks that let the team win consistently without depending on any single individual.

You should apply if

- You have a proven record winning multi-million pound opportunities in defence, intelligence or security markets, and you are ready to own the strategy, not just the deals.

- You want to build a market, a team and a function, and you see a high-growth, venture-backed environment as the reason to join rather than a risk to manage.

- You are comfortable being senior and hands-on at the same time. In the first year you will personally lead key pursuits while building the function around you.

Where this role can take you

- Build and lead the defence BD function you create as ExTrac scales across the UK and Europe.

- Shape company strategy, not just sales strategy, influencing how ExTrac positions itself at a defining moment for AI in defence and national security.

- A clear path to broader commercial leadership as the defence business grows.

Requirements

- Candidates must hold a valid UK Security Clearance (e.g. SC, DV) or be eligible to obtain UK Security Clearance to be considered for this role.

- Proven success winning multi-million pound opportunities in defence, intelligence, or security markets.

- Deep domain knowledge of UK and European defence, procurement pathways, and decision-making cycles.

- Strong relationships and extant networks across MoD, NATO, and allied defence ecosystems.

- Technology fluency, ideally in AI, SaaS, or data analytics contexts.

- Exceptional communicator, able to brief ministers, generals, and CTOs with equal confidence.

- Commercial discipline, with a track record of driving pipeline growth and closing complex deals.

- 10+ years in defence business development, capture or commercial leadership, including leading a team or a major multi-stakeholder campaign.

Desirable 

- Experience in both government service and commercial technology companies.

- Familiarity with classified and open-source intelligence workflows.

- Understanding of European defence industrial and political landscapes.

- Entrepreneurial mindset with appetite for building new markets and capabilities.

- Comfortable in a high-growth, venture-backed environment.

- Experience building or scaling a BD function in a start-up or scale-up.

- Working proficiency in a second European language.

Interview Process

We aim to ensure that each person who interviews with our team has the opportunity to showcase their experience and strengths, and to have honest conversations about whether ExTrac and the role align with their career aspirations. The process for this role is as follows:

- Initial Intro Interview - 30 Minutes

- Technical Craft & Competency-based Interviews - 45 Minutes x 2 (including a defence go-to-market case exercise)

- Senior Executive Interview - 45 Minutes

Benefits

- Competitive salary based on skills and experience.

- A generous benefits package, including Private Medical Health Insurance and enhanced pension contributions.

- Enhanced parental leave and a workplace nursery scheme.

- A sabbatical leave offer.

- £500/year education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval.

- 33 days of leave across the year inclusive of bank holidays.

- Flexible working, with the opportunity to spend 3 to 4 days a week remotely alongside regular days with our team in our central London office.

- A role that combines mission-driven purpose with cutting-edge technology in a fast-growing company.

description:

We are rebuilding the energy transaction, making it transparent and fair.

We're a 160+ person team - operators, data scientists, engineers, customer champions and energy experts - backed by top-tier investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Hitachi Ventures, Allianz, AlbionVC and Atomico. We closed a $75M Series B round in early 2026, taking our total funding to $94M, and we now power energy for over 4,000 UK businesses across 8,500+ sites , with over £75m in value returned to businesses and generators so far.

We're a technology company solving the energy industry, not an energy company. Some people call us a neo-utility, the neo-bank idea, applied to energy.

The industry is noticing. We were crowned Europe's Most Exciting Tech Company at the GP Bullhound Allstars awards , came in at #6 on LinkedIn's Top Startups 2026 in the UK, #7 on the Scaling Europe 50 of Europe's fastest-growing companies, and #14 on Sifted's AI 100 .

Learn more about us on our website .

🚀 The Role

We're hiring a People Performance Manager to join our Performance Service.

tem is growing fast. Our goal is to get better as we get bigger - revenue growing faster than headcount. In practice that means keeping our strongest people engaged and performing, getting new joiners productive quickly, and enabling our leaders to multiply their impact over time. Most companies solve that with layers of management. We don't. Our leaders (Player-Coaches) coach their teams while staying hands-on with the work, which means the systems around them have to do more of the lifting. That's where the Performance Service comes in.

We're a team of four, and we own how tem runs as an organisation: the operating rhythm (how work gets planned, tracked, escalated and reported), the onboarding and development that build capability, the frameworks that define what good performance looks like and how people progress and get paid, and the operational backbone of contracts, benefits and payroll. We don't own recruitment. We're adding a second Performance Partner because we need more hands on deck - both partnering with our leaders day to day, and building the frameworks that support them.

Your patch is sustained performance - the part that runs continuously once someone is through the door. You'll carry a portfolio of leaders across our Engines and Services that you're accountable for, and you'll co-own the frameworks that sit underneath them alongside the rest of the team. You will not be handed a finished playbook to administer. You'll report into the Performance Service Manager. HR experience is welcome but not required - we're open to operators, people who've led teams, and the sort of person who ends up owning whatever the company needs next.

In your first 12 months, you might:

- Become the first call for a portfolio of leaders on anything to do with their people - performance calls, team decisions and hard conversations.

- Co-design how progression, performance standards, evaluation and reward actually work at tem, alongside the rest of the Performance team.

- Handle live cases end to end - performance management, difficult conversations, exits and restructures.

- Use AI and automation so the operational layer runs itself and your time goes on judgement, not process.

- Turn recurring employee and manager pain points into better processes, tools, guidance or self-service, and measure whether they work.

🛠️ Responsibilities

- Coach and challenge: be a leader's first call on anything to do with their people - a decision they want a second view on, coaching on how to handle a situation, or a read on employment law - and hold a position when you disagree with them.

- Raise the bar: hold leaders to a high standard on performance, potential, pay and progression - help them make sharper calls, and hold consistency across your patch.

- Handle live cases end to end: performance management, difficult conversations, exits and restructures.

- Build to delight: shape how progression, performance standards, evaluation and reward actually work at tem, alongside the rest of the Performance team. We treat our people like top athletes, and our aim is to delight them at every step of their employee experience - the systems around them have to express that at every contact point.

- Design for our shape, not the textbook: we index on outcomes and impact in everything - how progression works, how teams are structured, what leaders spend their time on. Most standard people frameworks assume a management hierarchy we don't have.

- Automate the repeatable: use AI and automation so the operational layer runs itself and your time goes on judgement, not process.

- Think in process, scalability and iteration: turn recurring employee and manager pain points into better processes, tools, guidance or self-service. Measure whether they work and redesign when they don't fit the purpose.

✅ Requirements

You do not need a CIPD qualification, and you do not need to have worked in a large, established HR function. You might have been a founder's associate or Chief of Staff at a Series A or B startup, holding the place together while it scaled. You might have built a People function from scratch and taken it from a one-person band to a well-oiled machine. You might have run a team or an Operations function where the people calls were effectively yours, even if People or HR never appeared in your job title. Or you might have done a different job that helped you build the skills below. A background in HR might help you do this job well, but it is not a requirement.

Must-Haves 

- You've held real accountability for decisions on people - you've partnered with leaders, or managed a team yourself, where hiring, performance and exit calls were either yours or made on your guidance.

- You can be trusted with the hardest conversations in the business and you're recognised for how you handle them, and you understand how decisions about people shape culture and employer brand - balancing efficiency with empathy.

- You've worked in or towards building a high-performance culture, and you're a confident challenger who carries conviction and can influence leadership decisions.

- You're comfortable operating without a playbook, in a company where the requirements and the shape of your role change constantly.

- You think from first principles, get to the root cause of complex problems, weigh competing considerations and anticipate second-order consequences.

- You're fluent with Notion, automation and AI tooling - your instinct is to build the thing rather than do it manually a second time - and you write clearly enough that a busy person reads it once and comes away with a clear idea of the situation and the next actions.

Desirable 

- Employment relations experience in the UK, Europe or the US - we operate across the UK and Europe today, with plans to expand to the US soon.

- Experience working across multiple countries, including employer of record arrangements.

- Compensation and benchmarking experience - salary banding, pay review cycles, market data.

🎁 Benefits & Perks

- Stock options so everyone has ownership in our mission.

- 25 days holiday plus public holidays. Swap public holidays for the ones that matter most to you, and enjoy your birthday off.

- Remote first and flexible working, with clear core hours and no internal meetings on Friday afternoons.

- Up to GBP150 or EUR170 per month for wellbeing.

We move fast. Most processes take 2 to 3 weeks from first chat to offer. If you need us to adapt anything, let us know.

- Intro call with our Talent team.

We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, experiences, and identities, including those that are traditionally underrepresented in the tech and energy sectors. If you’re excited about this role but not sure you meet every requirement, we’d still love to hear from you. Your unique perspective could be exactly what we’re looking for.

title: Senior Campaign Manager (Temp Contract)
description:
About Pleo 

Messy spend management is tricky business. And tedious processes are a lose-lose situation for all involved, not just finance. At Pleo, we're changing that. With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together.

About the role 

We're looking for a Senior Integrated Campaign Manager, Brand & GTM to join our Integrated Marketing team at Pleo. In this role, you'll help architect, roll out, project manage, and drive the Go-To-Market (GTM) execution for our major 2027 brand marketing strategy and campaigns and be part of turning brand strategy, positioning, and creative concepts into operational GTM blueprints as we scale our multi-segment (SMB, Mid-Market, Enterprise) reach across 6 key European markets. If you're excited about high-visibility, full-funnel orchestration and balancing long-term brand equity building with full-funnel conversion, and are passionate about integrated brand and GTM marketing in high-growth B2B SaaS, then this is the opportunity for you!

Please bear in mind this role is a temporary contract of 1 year. 

Who you’ll be working with and reporting to 

You’ll report to our Director of Integrated Marketing and work closely with teams in Brand Marketing, Digital, Field/Events, Content, PR, Product Marketing (PMM), Marketing Ops, Data, and Sales/Growth channels. Our team is highly collaborative and dedicated to bridging top-of-funnel brand awareness with lower-funnel acquisition, ensuring every campaign moment translates into market salience, customer engagement, and measurable business impact. You’ll also have the chance to partner with teams across country teams, local market stakeholders, Sales Leadership, SDRs, and Field squads to ensure success.

What you’ll be doing 

As a Senior Campaign Manager, you will: 

- Integrated GTM Architecture & Strategic Planning : Translate the overarching 2027 brand strategy into actionable, full-funnel GTM campaign blueprints across SMB, Mid-Market, and Enterprise segments, architecting campaign flighting and distribution models across 6 European markets.

- The "Master Brief" & Cross-Functional Squad Leadership : Own and author comprehensive Integrated Campaign Master Briefs, leading the operational rhythm of cross-functional squads to execute multi-channel strategies (OOH, Paid Social, VIP activations, Digital, ABM) on time and within scope.

- Localization & Regional Adaptation : Partner with country teams and local market stakeholders to ensure master campaign frameworks balance global consistency with local relevance and execution precision.

- Strategic Brand Partnership & Enablement : Serve as the strategic execution peer to the Brand Marketing Lead, while partnering with Sales Leadership, SDRs, and Field teams to equip customer-facing squads with the stories, tools, and campaign momentum needed to capitalize on campaign-generated intent.

- Campaign Operations, Budget & ROI Accountability : Maintain and protect the integrated campaign master calendar, manage and allocate the multi-country integrated campaign budget, and partner with Marketing Ops, Data, and Brand Intelligence to track brand lift, consideration, pipeline growth, and closed-won impact.

What you bring 

You’ll thrive in this role if you have:

- A proven track record leading multi-million dollar, multi-country, full-funnel integrated campaigns in high-growth B2B SaaS or tech environments.

- Deep experience taking high-level brand frameworks and translating them into multi-channel GTM blueprints across varied audience segments (SMB to Enterprise).

- High proficiency in aligning cross-functional teams (Creative, Digital, PR, Ops, Sales) and holding squads accountable to tight deadlines and complex campaign launches.

- Deep understanding of how to run campaigns across diverse European markets, with a clear perspective on modular campaign design and local adaptation.

- Experience with tracking brand-to-pipeline performance metrics, campaign flighting dynamics, brand lift, consideration, and total ROI.

- A background in integrated marketing, GTM campaign management, or brand marketing orchestration within B2B technology or SaaS.

Why is this role a good fit for you 

This role is a good fit for you if:

- You thrive as the operational bridge between high-level brand strategy and lower-funnel demand generation, turning concepts into structured GTM blueprints.

- You love leading cross-functional squads across multiple international markets, balancing consistency with local nuances across 6 key European countries.

- You take pride in end-to-end accountability, from authoring master briefs and handling multi-country budgets to tracking downstream pipeline velocity and closed-won revenue impact.

This role is not a good fit for you if:

- You prefer focusing purely on high-level creative ideation, copy, or audience insight development without building the operational execution machinery.

- You prefer running single-channel or single-market marketing initiatives rather than orchestrating complex, multi-segment (SMB to Enterprise), multi-channel matrices.

- You are uncomfortable navigating data, campaign flighting performance, budget allocations, and downstream pipeline attribution alongside brand metrics.

How you’ll develop in this role 

In your first 6 months at Pleo, you’ll:

- Lead the architecture and rollout of the 2027 integrated brand campaign calendar across all target European markets.

- Collaborate with the Brand Marketing Lead, country teams, and Marketing Ops to stand up the Master Briefing framework and streamline cross-functional execution rhythms.

- Grow your skills in full-funnel orchestration and multi-market scale, driving measurable brand lift, consideration, and downstream pipeline velocity as Pleo continues to expand.

The location 

Please note: We can hire on a hybrid or in-person set-up in any of the locations listed on the advert but you will need to be physically based in the country of your choice with a valid right to work . We are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role in any of the listed locations.

Show me the benefits! 

- Your own Pleo card (no more out-of-pocket spending!)

- Lunch is on us for your work days - enjoy catered meals or receive a lunch allowance based on your local office

- Comprehensive private healthcare - depending on your location, coverage options include Vitality, Alan or Médis

- 25 days of annual leave + public holidays (additional days may apply in select countries based on local standards).

- For our Team, we offer both hybrid and fully remote working options

- We use MyndUp to give our employees access to free mental health and well-being support with great success so far

- Paid parental leave - we want to make sure that we're supportive of families and help you feel that you don't have to compromise your family due to work

The interview process 

We want to ensure you are set-up for success and understand what will be expected of you. If your application is successful, our interview process is as follows:

- Intro call: A 30-minute chat with our Talent Partner to discuss the role and your background.

- Hiring Manager Interview: A 45 minute chat to deep dive into your experience

- Challenge & Team Interview: We will send you a take home test and invite you to present during a 60 minute team interview. This is an opportunity to show us how you would handle the day to day of the role

- Final Interview : A final interview with a senior leader

Transparency is important to us so we also wanted to share some insights about what we’re looking for in applications to ensure you can set yourself up for success!

Last time we hired for this role, we received a total vast number of applications but only a few were selected for an intro call.Some of the key reasons why previous candidates didn’t make it past the application screening stage include:

- CV writing and content: we receive a lot of CVs, and many of them are AI-generated. We love seeing people leverage AI—it’s a big focus for us internally too—but without human intervention, these CVs can sometimes become generic and fail to show a candidate in the best light. What we're really looking for is the specific details of real impact that only you know from your previous experience. A top tip from us is to use the “Achieved X, as measured by Y, by doing Z” formula (credit: Laszlo Bock, ~2014) to give a really clear picture of what you’ve worked on. A final note: including links to your previous companies' websites is a huge help and allows us to truly understand your background!

- Application care: every single application we receive is reviewed by a human (yes, hundreds of them) because we believe that candidates' efforts should be matched by an equal level of human care. This means that we expect a similar level of attention put into your application. Read and answer the application questions carefully, they make a huge difference in our decision-making process.

- Profile to role fit: highlight most important aspects of the role, points that might get misunderstood, any specific industry requirements etc.

About your application 

- English first. Since it's our company language, please submit your application in English. You’ll be using it a lot if you join us.

- A fair look for everyone. Our talent team reads every single application to ensure the process is fair. To keep things running smoothly, we only accept applications through our system—our support team can’t pass on calls or emails.

- Diversity drives us. We can only reach our goals if our team reflects the world around us. That starts with you hitting apply, even if you don't tick every single box. We encourage people from all backgrounds and experiences to join us.

- Interview at your best. We want you to feel comfortable throughout the process. If you have any accessibility requirements or need a specific format, email ----- We’ll design a process that works for you.

- Your data is safe. When you apply, we process your personal data as a data processor. For more information on how Pleo processes personal data, read our Privacy Policy here .

- Applying for multiple roles? Nothing is stopping you, and we assess every role independently. However, we do look for alignment, so make sure you can explain why your interest and experience are right for each specific role.

- Reapplying. If you’re applying for the same role again, please wait six months from your last decision before hitting submit.

In 2026, over half of the business told us they don't know what excellence looks like in their role, or how excellence is rewarded. This is the crux of this role; to build the systems, processes and reward that sets people up for success and ensure we reward and retain our best people.

title: CDI - Senior Platform Engineer - Paris
description:
Mission 

Des groupes de premier plan font tourner leur IA sur ce que vous construisez. Infrastructure cloud, plateformes de données, chaînes de delivery, serving de modèles, runtime des agents : ces fondations portent à grande échelle les applications et les agents de nos clients, et vous les concevez et les exploitez. Grâce à ce travail, les équipes produit livrent sans risque, tandis que les coûts, la latence et la sécurité restent sous contrôle.

Ce poste est fait pour vous si vos utilisateurs sont d’autres équipes d’ingénierie et si la robustesse d’un système sous charge vous intéresse. 

Artefact accompagne les plus grandes entreprises du monde dans le déploiement de l’IA : 3 000 AI makers dans plus de 30 pays, plus de 1 000 clients. En France, le département Engineering réunit environ 300 personnes sous la responsabilité du CTO ; vous y rejoignez le chapter AI Applied Engineer, archétype Platform Engineer.

Activités et responsabilités 

Les Product Engineers et les AI Engineers déploient sur les plateformes que vous construisez ; leurs besoins se définissent avec eux, et leur accompagnement se poursuit jusqu’en production.

Sur une plateforme de données, les fondations vous reviennent : infrastructure, sécurité, réseau, calcul. Ce qui y circule relève des Context & Analytics Engineers. Le travail se mène aussi avec les équipes IT, sécurité et cloud du client, sous le regard desquelles chaque choix d’architecture doit pouvoir se défendre ; le code se relit entre pairs et les nouvelles recrues sont accompagnées.

Vos responsabilités : 

- 
Déployer l’infrastructure cloud en infrastructure as code et conduire les migrations cloud.

- 
Construire et exploiter des plateformes de données : entrepôts et lakehouses, orchestration, traitement batch et streaming.

- 
Construire des pipelines CI/CD et l’outillage MLOps et LLMOps.

- 
Construire le harness des agents : runtime, frameworks d’évaluation, observabilité.

- 
Servir les modèles et maîtriser leur coût et leur latence.

- 
Poser les fondations de sécurité : IAM, réseau, secrets, droits d’accès des agents, protection contre le prompt injection.

- 
Construire des connecteurs et des serveurs MCP que plusieurs agents réutilisent.

- 
Garantir la fiabilité : monitoring, gestion des incidents, suivi des coûts.

Profil recherché 

Les indispensables : 

- 
Vous avez construit et exploité de l’infrastructure cloud sur Google Cloud, Azure ou AWS, en infrastructure as code.

- 
Des pipelines CI/CD et des déploiements conteneurisés, par exemple sur Kubernetes, font partie de votre pratique.

- 
Les bases de la sécurité (IAM, règles réseau, gestion des secrets) s’appliquent chez vous au quotidien.

- 
Ce que vous exploitez, vous le surveillez, et vous prenez part à la gestion des incidents.

- 
Le code et la documentation que vous écrivez restent maintenables pour les équipes qui utilisent votre plateforme.

- 
Les coding agents font déjà partie de votre quotidien, et vous vérifiez ce qu’ils produisent.

Un plus, pas un prérequis : 

- 
Une expérience de plateformes de données, par exemple sur Databricks, BigQuery ou Snowflake.

- 
Une expérience MLOps ou LLMOps : serving de modèles, model registry, pipelines d’évaluation.

- 
Une expérience d’observabilité d’agents ou de LLM gateway : tracing, suivi des coûts, routage.

- 
FinOps : suivi et optimisation des coûts.

- 
Sécurité de l’IA : droits d’accès des agents, red teaming, guardrails.

- 
Une certification cloud.

Pas besoin de cocher toutes les cases pour postuler : si vous avez l’essentiel des indispensables et l’envie d’apprendre le reste, parlons-en.

Pourquoi nous rejoindre ? 

Une plateforme n’est jamais terminée : chaque nouvel agent déployé chez un client soulève de nouvelles questions de coût, de latence et de droits d’accès. Le Platform Engineer travaille à l’endroit où ces questions se posent en premier, au plus près des équipes techniques et de sécurité du client.

Nous sommes des AI makers : l’IA se construit avec nos clients, pas seulement pour eux. Leurs enjeux deviennent les nôtres, et nos choix techniques s’expliquent dans le langage du métier. Les positions que nous prenons sont claires ; elles évoluent face aux faits, jamais sous la pression.

Notre domaine change tous les mois, et ce rythme nous convient : les nouvelles technologies et les nouveaux secteurs s’apprennent vite, et les habitudes qui ne servent plus s’abandonnent sans regret. Devant un problème difficile, le réflexe est de le découper en étapes vérifiables, avec un haut niveau d’exigence sur le code comme sur les livrables.

Quand il manque quelque chose, pour un client ou pour le chapter, nous le construisons. La progression passe par des retours constructifs, par le partage des connaissances, par la demande d’aide sans attendre et par la reconnaissance du travail des autres. Il y a beaucoup à apprendre, et beaucoup à construire.

Un counsellor accompagne vos premiers mois. L’onboarding technique ouvre le parcours, suivi d’un premier projet client ; si aucun n’est prêt, les starter kits internes prennent le relais.

Le reste s’apprend sur les projets : serving de modèles, observabilité des agents, sécurité de l’IA, avec l’appui de la communauté Platform Engineer. À partir de 2027, l’archétype Platform Engineer disposera de sa propre grille de compétences et de son propre parcours de formation, en plus du socle commun à tous les AI Applied Engineers (évaluation de l’IA, responsabilité en production).

Une spécialisation en sécurité de l’IA (red teaming, guardrails, conformité à l’AI Act) est possible : elle relève aujourd’hui de l’archétype Platform Engineer. Plus tard, un rôle transverse s’ouvre (Project Tech Lead, Pre-sales Engineer, Engineering Manager), et les Platform Engineers seniors peuvent rejoindre le chapter AI Architect.

Processus de recrutement 

Le processus demande environ quatre heures, réparties en six étapes dont une seule sur site.

- 
Entretien RH (45 min, à distance) : parcours, motivations et points pratiques, comme le calendrier et les prétentions salariales.

- 
Appel avec le CTO (15 à 30 min, à distance).

- 
Screening technique (30 min, à distance, avec un membre du chapter AI Applied Engineer) : retour détaillé sur vos projets passés, puis questions techniques et de design de solution.

- 
Code review et live coding (60 min, sur site, avec un membre du chapter) : relecture d’un dépôt de code existant et correction de ses défauts, puis construction d’une nouvelle fonctionnalité avec un coding agent et présentation du résultat.

title: CDI - Senior AI Strategist - Paris
description:
Prenez en main un stream de transformation IA, au contact direct des clients, de la vision aux résultats mesurables. 

L’IA, et en particulier l’IA agentique, figure parmi les priorités des comités de direction.
Chez Artefact, nous sommes des makers. “We Make AI Work” : notre métier n’est pas de commenter l’IA, c’est de la faire fonctionner, à grande échelle, au cœur des grands groupes. 

Et tout commence par vous.

Mission 

En tant que Senior AI Strategist , vous prenez en main un stream ou une mission bien cadrée, avec autonomie sur votre périmètre et au contact direct des clients : vous cadrez, analysez, prototypez et recommandez, vous coachez les consultants juniors, et vous voyez vos recommandations prendre vie avec nos équipes Engineering.

Vous commencez là où débute toute transformation IA : par l’ambition du client, son secteur d’activité et ses processus métier, et non par la technologie. Et vous restez un maker : vous ne vous arrêtez pas au slide. Vous construisez vous-même analyses, business cases et démos fonctionnelles (vibe coding, low-code, no-code) que le client peut toucher, et vous développez un domaine d’expertise solide dans un secteur ou une fonction métier.

Vous travaillez main dans la main avec nos équipes Engineering (qui construisent et livrent des solutions d’IA agentique) et nos équipes AI Adoption (qui favorisent leur adoption) : vous cadrez les processus cibles et la roadmap de votre stream, Engineering les construit et les livre, et AI Adoption accompagne les personnes dans le changement, dès le premier jour.

Activités & Responsabilités 

- Conception de la stratégie et de la transformation IA 

Vous contribuez à cadrer la vision IA et à la roadmap du stream, qualifiez et priorisez les cas d’usage, et arbitrez entre solutions IA et non-IA. Vous investiguez les processus métier, identifiez les irritants et les causes racines, et proposez des pistes de refonte priorisées, en pensant d’abord lean et en n’utilisant l’IA que là où elle apporte de la valeur. Vous contribuez également à la conception du modèle opératoire cible et à ses conditions de succès.

- Analyses, business cases & prototypage 

Vous concevez et pilotez les travaux d’analyse du stream afin de sécuriser des décisions fondées sur les données et sur les faits : vous collectez et validez les données, revoyez les analyses des consultants juniors, construisez des business cases de bout en bout et formulez des recommandations. Vous prototypez des cas d’usage avec des outils agentiques pour illustrer la valeur par la démo et aider les clients à se projeter dans la solution finale.

- Delivery, livrables & collaboration 

Vous pilotez au quotidien la livraison d’un stream ou d’une mission cadrée : vous construisez le rétro-planning, identifiez les risques et blocages, proposez des solutions et donnez de la visibilité au N+1 et aux équipes du client. Vous produisez des sections de livrables de niveau C-suite, rédigez les storylines du stream, participez aux synthèses exécutives sur votre périmètre et construisez un narratif qui appuie la recommandation et emporte l’adhésion. Vous coordonnez votre stream avec les équipes Engineering pour la faisabilité technique et avec les équipes AI Adoption pour ancrer l’adoption sur le terrain.

- Relation client & développement commercial 

Vous construisez une relation de proximité avec votre interlocuteur direct, élargissez le réseau de parties prenantes aux équipes opérationnelles et au middle management, anticipez les résistances et animez des ateliers en autonomie. Vous identifiez des opportunités, soutenez le plan de compte avec le Manager et le Directeur et participez aux propositions et aux événements de networking.

- Équipe & connaissances 

Vous déléguez avec des instructions claires, donnez des feedbacks constructifs, animez des 1to1 avec les consultants juniors et participez aux rétrospectives et aux entretiens de candidats. Vous contribuez à la base de connaissances interne par des articles et des retours d’expérience, et animez des sessions d’onboarding et des formations internes.

Profil recherché 

Vous vous reconnaissez si … vous aimez avoir la main sur un périmètre, structurer des problèmes complexes et voir vos recommandations se concrétiser, et si vous préférez mettre une démo entre les mains du client plutôt que lui décrire une vision.

- 2 à 5 ans d’expérience au sein d’un cabinet de conseil en stratégie, en management ou en transformation data / IA.

- Une formation supérieure de niveau licence ou master, issue d’un cursus académique d’excellence.

- Première expérience de pilotage d’un stream ou d’une mission, avec coaching de consultants juniors.

- Une expérience de pilotage de missions complexes, de la vision aux résultats, avec des business cases qui résistent à l’examen d’un Comex.

- Bonne compréhension des enjeux opérationnels de l’IA (IA générative et agentique, gouvernance, cas d’usage métiers)

- Aisance dans la construction de business cases et dans la restitution à des équipes opérationnelles et au middle management.

- Première expérience d’analyse ou de refonte de processus métier, avec une appétence pour certains domaines métier.

- Un état d’esprit de maker : aisance avec les outils technologiques actuels et capacité à prototyper des cas d’usage réalistes, alignés sur le besoin du client, et à itérer rapidement à partir des retours (low-code, no-code, outils agentiques).

- Une affinité avec un secteur ou une fonction métier, et une vraie curiosité pour les impacts de l’IA.

- Maîtrise courante du français et de l’anglais (oral et écrit).

À propos d’Artefact 

Artefact est un cabinet de conseil spécialisé en data et en intelligence artificielle, qui accompagne les entreprises pour transformer ces technologies en impact business concret et mesurable. À la croisée du conseil, de la data et de la technologie, nos 2 500 collaborateurs dans 27 pays mettent leurs expertises en commun pour concevoir, développer et déployer des solutions qui répondent aux enjeux de transformation de nos clients.

Notre accompagnement couvre l’intégralité de la chaîne de valeur : AI Strategy (cadrage stratégique, opportunités à fort impact, trajectoires, modèles opératoires), Engineering (industrialisation, architectures agentiques, produits data) et AI Adoption (conduite du changement, montée en compétences, usage quotidien de l’IA).

Pour en savoir plus sur Artefact, nos expertises et notre culture : https://www.artefact.com 

Pourquoi nous rejoindre ? 

- De la stratégie à la réalisation 
Ne pas s’arrêter aux recommandations : participer à la conception et à la concrétisation de solutions IA répondant à de véritables enjeux métiers.

- Une collaboration entre expertises 
Occuper un rôle à la croisée de la stratégie (AI Strategy), de la technologie (Engineering) et de l'humain (AI Adoption).

Un rôle avec de l’autonomie et des perspectives
Piloter des streams, développer une expertise, faire grandir une équipe et contribuer au développement de l’activité. Un parcours clair de progression 

Un accompagnement concret : counsellor, parcours de formation et programme de leadership.

Processus de recrutement 

- Un entretien de fit RH (45') avec HR / Talent Acquisition

- Un business case AI-driven (60') avec un AI Strategist Manager ou Senior Manager

- Un business case de prototypage IA hands-on (60') avec un AI Strategist Manager

- Un entretien de fit final (30') avec un AI Strategist Partner

title: AI Applied Engineering – Platform Engineer Manager
description:
Mission 

Des groupes de premier plan font tourner leur IA sur ce que vous construisez. Infrastructure cloud, plateformes de données, chaînes de delivery, serving de modèles, runtime des agents : ces fondations portent à grande échelle les applications et les agents de nos clients, et vous les concevez et les exploitez. Grâce à ce travail, les équipes produit livrent sans risque, tandis que les coûts, la latence et la sécurité restent sous contrôle.

Ce poste est fait pour vous si vos utilisateurs sont d’autres équipes d’ingénierie et si la robustesse d’un système sous charge vous intéresse. 

Artefact accompagne les plus grandes entreprises du monde dans le déploiement de l’IA : 3 000 AI makers dans plus de 30 pays, plus de 1 000 clients. En France, le département Engineering réunit environ 300 personnes sous la responsabilité du CTO ; vous y rejoignez le chapter AI Applied Engineer, archétype Platform Engineer.

Activités et responsabilités 

Les Product Engineers et les AI Engineers déploient sur les plateformes que vous construisez ; leurs besoins se définissent avec eux, et leur accompagnement se poursuit jusqu’en production.

Sur une plateforme de données, les fondations vous reviennent : infrastructure, sécurité, réseau, calcul. Ce qui y circule relève des Context & Analytics Engineers. Le travail se mène aussi avec les équipes IT, sécurité et cloud du client, sous le regard desquelles chaque choix d’architecture doit pouvoir se défendre ; le code se relit entre pairs et les nouvelles recrues sont accompagnées.

Vos responsabilités : 

- 
Déployer l’infrastructure cloud en infrastructure as code et conduire les migrations cloud.

- 
Construire et exploiter des plateformes de données : entrepôts et lakehouses, orchestration, traitement batch et streaming.

- 
Construire des pipelines CI/CD et l’outillage MLOps et LLMOps.

- 
Construire le harness des agents : runtime, frameworks d’évaluation, observabilité.

- 
Servir les modèles et maîtriser leur coût et leur latence.

- 
Poser les fondations de sécurité : IAM, réseau, secrets, droits d’accès des agents, protection contre le prompt injection.

- 
Construire des connecteurs et des serveurs MCP que plusieurs agents réutilisent.

- 
Garantir la fiabilité : monitoring, gestion des incidents, suivi des coûts.

Profil recherché 

Les indispensables : 

- 
Vous avez construit et exploité de l’infrastructure cloud sur Google Cloud, Azure ou AWS, en infrastructure as code.

- 
Des pipelines CI/CD et des déploiements conteneurisés, par exemple sur Kubernetes, font partie de votre pratique.

- 
Les bases de la sécurité (IAM, règles réseau, gestion des secrets) s’appliquent chez vous au quotidien.

- 
Ce que vous exploitez, vous le surveillez, et vous prenez part à la gestion des incidents.

- 
Le code et la documentation que vous écrivez restent maintenables pour les équipes qui utilisent votre plateforme.

- 
Les coding agents font déjà partie de votre quotidien, et vous vérifiez ce qu’ils produisent.

Un plus, pas un prérequis : 

- 
Une expérience de plateformes de données, par exemple sur Databricks, BigQuery ou Snowflake.

- 
Une expérience MLOps ou LLMOps : serving de modèles, model registry, pipelines d’évaluation.

- 
Une expérience d’observabilité d’agents ou de LLM gateway : tracing, suivi des coûts, routage.

- 
FinOps : suivi et optimisation des coûts.

- 
Sécurité de l’IA : droits d’accès des agents, red teaming, guardrails.

- 
Une certification cloud.

Pas besoin de cocher toutes les cases pour postuler : si vous avez l’essentiel des indispensables et l’envie d’apprendre le reste, parlons-en.

Pourquoi nous rejoindre ? 

Une plateforme n’est jamais terminée : chaque nouvel agent déployé chez un client soulève de nouvelles questions de coût, de latence et de droits d’accès. Le Platform Engineer travaille à l’endroit où ces questions se posent en premier, au plus près des équipes techniques et de sécurité du client.

Nous sommes des AI makers : l’IA se construit avec nos clients, pas seulement pour eux. Leurs enjeux deviennent les nôtres, et nos choix techniques s’expliquent dans le langage du métier. Les positions que nous prenons sont claires ; elles évoluent face aux faits, jamais sous la pression.

Notre domaine change tous les mois, et ce rythme nous convient : les nouvelles technologies et les nouveaux secteurs s’apprennent vite, et les habitudes qui ne servent plus s’abandonnent sans regret. Devant un problème difficile, le réflexe est de le découper en étapes vérifiables, avec un haut niveau d’exigence sur le code comme sur les livrables.

Quand il manque quelque chose, pour un client ou pour le chapter, nous le construisons. La progression passe par des retours constructifs, par le partage des connaissances, par la demande d’aide sans attendre et par la reconnaissance du travail des autres. Il y a beaucoup à apprendre, et beaucoup à construire.

Un counsellor accompagne vos premiers mois. L’onboarding technique ouvre le parcours, suivi d’un premier projet client ; si aucun n’est prêt, les starter kits internes prennent le relais.

Le reste s’apprend sur les projets : serving de modèles, observabilité des agents, sécurité de l’IA, avec l’appui de la communauté Platform Engineer. À partir de 2027, l’archétype Platform Engineer disposera de sa propre grille de compétences et de son propre parcours de formation, en plus du socle commun à tous les AI Applied Engineers (évaluation de l’IA, responsabilité en production).

Une spécialisation en sécurité de l’IA (red teaming, guardrails, conformité à l’AI Act) est possible : elle relève aujourd’hui de l’archétype Platform Engineer. Plus tard, un rôle transverse s’ouvre (Project Tech Lead, Pre-sales Engineer, Engineering Manager), et les Platform Engineers seniors peuvent rejoindre le chapter AI Architect.

Processus de recrutement 

Le processus demande environ quatre heures, réparties en six étapes dont une seule sur site.

- 
Entretien RH (45 min, à distance) : parcours, motivations et points pratiques, comme le calendrier et les prétentions salariales.

- 
Appel avec le CTO (15 à 30 min, à distance).

- 
Screening technique (30 min, à distance, avec un membre du chapter AI Applied Engineer) : retour détaillé sur vos projets passés, puis questions techniques et de design de solution.

- 
Code review et live coding (60 min, sur site, avec un membre du chapter) : relecture d’un dépôt de code existant et correction de ses défauts, puis construction d’une nouvelle fonctionnalité avec un coding agent et présentation du résultat.

- 
Cas technique (45 min, à distance, avec un membre du chapter) : cadrage d’un problème métier, proposition d’une solution technique, description de la méthode d’évaluation, puis discussion de vos choix.

- 
Entretien final (30 min, à distance, avec une personne de l’encadrement du département, Engineering Manager ou Director) : reprise des points restés ouverts, choix de l’archétype et du niveau les mieux adaptés à votre profil, et réponses à toutes vos questions.

Selon les étapes, tous les outils d’IA sont autorisés, ou aucun. Lors du live coding, c’est la manière de travailler avec l’assistance de l’IA qui est observée.

Rémunération : 66 000€ à 85 000€ brut annuel (fixe) selon expérience et séniorité

Chez Artefact, nous sommes convaincus que la diversité des parcours, des expériences et des perspectives fait la richesse de nos équipes. Nous nous engageons à offrir un environnement inclusif et des opportunités équitables, où chacune et chacun peut évoluer et exprimer pleinement son potentiel. Nos recrutements reposent sur les compétences, le potentiel et l’adéquation avec le rôle.

- Prendre les commandes

description:
About WPP Media 

WPP is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands. With exceptional talent, trusted data and intelligence, and world-class partnerships – all united by our pioneering agentic marketing platform, WPP Open – we help clients navigate change, capture opportunity, and deliver transformational growth. 

WPP Media is WPP's AI-driven media operating unit, bringing together media, data, and partnerships to deliver creative personalisation at scale. Connected through WPP Open and powered by Open Intelligence, clients see exactly where, how, and why their media investment is working.

For more information, visit wppmedia.com .

Dans un souci de clarté et d’accessibilité, nous avons choisi de ne pas utiliser l’écriture inclusive dans nos communications. WPP Media est fermement engagé en faveur de la diversité : nous valorisons l'inclusion et l'égalité, en considérant tous les candidats sans distinction d'identité de genre, d'origine ethnique ou de religion. Tous nos postes sont également ouverts aux personnes en situation de handicap. 

À propos de WPP Media : 

WPP est le partenaire de confiance des plus grandes marques mondiales pour assurer leur croissance. Nous réunissons une intelligence média de pointe, une créativité de classe mondiale, une production de nouvelle génération, des solutions pour transformer le marketing à l’ère de l’IA et un conseil stratégique d’expert au sein d’une seule compagnie.

Propulsés par des talents exceptionnels et WPP Open, notre plateforme de marketing agentique, nous déployons l’IA à grande échelle pour aider nos clients à naviguer dans un monde en pleines mutations et à optimiser leurs investissements marketing.

Pour plus d’informations, visitez www.wpp.com .

WPP Media est le collectif média global de WPP. Dans un monde où les médias sont omniprésents, nous regroupons la meilleure plateforme, les meilleurs talents et les meilleurs partenaires pour développer les solutions les plus innovantes, offrant une croissance inégalée à nos clients. Pour plus d'informations, visitez www.wppmedia.com .

Chez WPP Media, nous croyons en la puissance de notre culture et de nos collaborateurs. C'est grâce à cette synergie que nous parvenons à créer des expériences véritablement exceptionnelles, tant pour nos clients que pour nos équipes internes.

Pour réussir dans ce poste, il est fondamental d'incarner les valeurs essentielles qui unissent WPP et WPP Media :

- Être Extraordinaire en favorisant un leadership collectif qui inspire une créativité véritablement transformationnelle.

- Créer un environnement Ouvert en trouvant l'équilibre parfait entre l'épanouissement de nos collaborateurs et la satisfaction de nos clients, le tout fondé sur une confiance mutuelle.

- Diriger avec Optimisme en stimulant activement la croissance et le développement pour mobiliser l'ensemble de notre organisation.

Rôle et missions : 

Au sein du Département Affichage (OOH, DOOH, Événementiel) & Média Local de WPP Media, vous rejoignez une équipe à taille humaine, experte et passionnée. Rattaché directement au Manager du pôle Études & Marketing, votre rôle est au cœur de la stratégie : faire parler la donnée pour nourrir les recommandations médias, mesurer l'efficacité de nos dispositifs et démontrer le ROI des campagnes de nos annonceurs.

En interaction étroite avec les experts trading/achat, les équipes conseil et le pôle Data & Analytics, vos missions s'articulent autour de 4 piliers majeurs :

- Études de marché, cibles et insights stratégiques : 

- Réaliser des piges concurrentielles approfondies et des bilans d’investissements publicitaires à l’aide des outils Kantar (AdExpress).

- Concevoir et analyser des cibles médias fines via SIMM-TGI afin d’identifier les univers d’affichage prioritaires (transports, mobilier urbain, centres commerciaux, etc.).

- Participer activement à la préparation des compétitions et pitchs annonceurs en produisant des fiches sectorielles et des analyses de tendances percutantes.

- Mesure de l'efficacité et post-tests de campagnes : 

- Être l'interlocuteur du pôle Data & Analytics pour co-développer et déployer les études d’impact et de branding (post-tests).

- Piloter l'ensemble du process : cadrage des besoins, activation des panels, analyse des performances et coordination du modèle de co-financement avec les régies publicitaires.

- Accompagnement Géomarketing & Campagnes Locales : 

- Exploiter l'outil propriétaire de géomarketing pour extraire des indicateurs territoriaux et des insights clés au service des stratégies locales de nos clients.

- Contribuer à enrichir et optimiser les bases de données de nos outils métiers.

- Pédagogie & Valorisation du Média : 

- Contribuer à la mise à jour des présentations de référence du département et des modules de formation interne (Media Academy).

- Assurer une veille active sur les innovations du secteur (digitalisation de l'affichage / DOOH, data, IA, nouveaux formats).

Profil Recherché : 

- Formation : De formation Bac+4/5 (École de commerce, Université ou équivalent) avec une spécialisation en Marketing, Études, Statistiques ou Communication / Média.

- Expérience : Vous justifiez d'une première expérience réussie (stage de fin d'études ou alternance) au sein d'une agence média (pôle études, marketing ou trading) ou en régie publicitaire (idéalement affichage OOH/DOOH).

- Compétences techniques : 

- Maîtrise des outils Kantar indispensables au poste : AdExpress et SIMM-TGI .

- Connaissance ou notions de la méthodologie Mobimétrie .

- Maîtrise avancée d' Excel (tableaux croisés dynamiques, formules complexes, synthèse de données) et de PowerPoint (restitution visuelle et storytelling de la data).

- Compétences relationnelles & comportementales : 

- Fort esprit d’analyse et de synthèse : vous savez transformer la donnée chiffrée brute en recommandations business claires et actionnables.

- Rigueur et précision : vous êtes garant de la fiabilité des chiffres et de la qualité des livrables.

- Curiosité intellectuelle : vous vous intéressez aux nouveaux modes de consommation média, à la data et à l’intelligence artificielle.

- Esprit d’équipe et aisance relationnelle : vous aimez collaborer au quotidien avec des profils complémentaires (consultants DTA, traders média, planneurs stratégiques).

- Langues : Anglais professionnel opérationnel (niveau B2 minimum souhaité, particulièrement à l'écrit pour la documentation et les études groupe).

La vie chez WPP Media et ses avantages : 

Notre engagement à façonner l'avenir des médias se manifeste par un soutien actif au développement professionnel de nos talents, les aidant à atteindre leur plein potentiel. Cette démarche s'accompagne d'une vision responsable dans nos stratégies d'investissement médiatique, reflétant ainsi notre double priorité : valoriser nos collaborateurs tout en adoptant des pratiques durables dans notre secteur.

Les collaborateurs de WPP Media ont un accès privilégié aux réseaux internationaux de WPP Media et WPP, leur permettant de développer leurs passions, d'étendre leur réseau professionnel et de rester à la pointe des innovations en marketing et publicité.

Nous disposons de ressources vastes et variées au service de nos collaborateurs, notre entreprise cultive activement l'inclusion des talents de tous horizons. Les réussites et expertises des équipes sont régulièrement mises en lumière lors d'événements fédérateurs qui ponctuent également les moments clés de l'année, renforçant ainsi notre culture d'entreprise collaborative et diversifiée.

Nos avantages comprennent : 

- Télétravail : jusqu'à 2 jours par semaine et 2 semaines complètes à prendre en deux fois dans l’année.

- Congés offerts : 2 jours de repos supplémentaires offerts, dont le lundi de Pentecôte.

- Ancienneté : Jours de congé additionnels par palier de 5 ans d’ancienneté.

- Santé & Équité : 5 jours de télétravail additionnels par mois pour les collaboratrices souffrant d’endométriose.

- Politique handicap : 3 jours d'absence autorisés payés par an, accès à des Chèques Emploi Service Universel, et accompagnements spécifiques pour les collaborateurs ayant une RQTH.

- Engagement sociétal : Missions solidaires possibles via le programme We care and we act .

- Tools : Accès à des outils performants et à la pointe de la technologie pour la gestion des campagnes et le reporting (WPP Open).

Process de recrutement : 

Nous nous engageons à rendre ce process aussi rapide et efficace que possible, et à maintenir une communication ouverte et transparente tout au long du process :

- Entretien avec l’équipe Recrutement : Un premier échange téléphonique ou par visioconférence avec l’équipe Talent Acquisition pour faire connaissance, aborder votre parcours et vos motivations.

- Entretien opérationnel & Étude de cas : Une rencontre avec le Manager du pôle Études & Marketing, accompagnée d'un Business Case concret permettant d'évaluer votre logique analytique et votre capacité de restitution.

- Entretien de Direction : Un échange final avec la Directrice du pôle.

Au moins l'une des étapes du process se déroulera en présentiel dans nos locaux). 

WPP Media garantit l'égalité des chances et considère tous les candidats sans discrimination ni considération de caractéristiques particulières. Nous nous engageons à cultiver un environnement de respect où chacun se sent à sa place et bénéficie des mêmes opportunités d'évolution professionnelle.

Consultez notre politique de confidentialité pour tout savoir sur la protection de vos données.

Bien que nous étudiions toutes les candidatures reçues, nous ne contactons que les personnes sélectionnées pour un entretien.

title: Mid-Market Account Executive - France
description:
Who we are 

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale. 

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term. 

About the role: 

Samsara is a fortress in a volatile market. We are a $1.9B ARR, NYSE-listed powerhouse that sells essential technology to the physical operations powering the global economy. This is a seat built for high performers and incredibly driven individuals who want to accelerate their careers — the bar for entry is high, but those who execute are well rewarded for it.

While the rest of the tech scene is scaling back, our France team continued to perform above 100% last year. We are looking for territory owners who want to manage deal cycles from € 20k to € 200k , selling a complex suite of 15+ products to 8 different personas, including MDs and Finance Directors. If you want to be pushed to your limit and rewarded with the stability of a market leader, this is the place.

Whilst the role can be worked remotely anywhere in France, there is a need to visit clients in the region as required (typically fortnightly basis).

You should apply if: 

- You want to impact the industries that run our world : Your efforts will result in real-world impact—helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.

- Your mantra is #alwaysbeprospecting : The world of operations is vast. Your customers are often out in the field and the best way to catch them is live on the phone. Samsara’s top reps do constant research to find companies and contacts to expand their pipeline.

- You have innate curiosity in how businesses work : One day you’ll meet with someone in waste management and the next you may be learning about the inner workings of a food distribution center. Our top sales team members seek to learn the ins and outs of the businesses they support in order to make a larger impact.

- You are a life-long learner : Samsara sales are complex. You will need to learn about businesses where you previously had little knowledge. The payoff is big but you have to be willing to put in the work.

- You build genuine relationships with your customers : The industries we serve have relied on pen-and-paper solutions for years and haven’t been met with the type of technology we offer. Our customers value earned trust and human relationships built over time.

- You want to be with the best: Samsara’s high-performance Sales culture means you’ll be surrounded by the best and challenged to go farther than you have before.

In this role you will: 

- Own your destiny: Operate as a pure revenue leader, responsible for 80-90% net-new logo acquisition through self-sourced pipeline.

- Get In Early: The France Mid-Market is a high-achieving segment in the company. The window to build something significant is open right now. 

- Sharpen Your Edge: Access elite enablement — Command the Message and MEDDPICC coaching — built to make you a more effective closer.

- Navigate Complexity: Move beyond feature-pushing to sell high-level ROI and safety outcomes to sophisticated economic buyers (MDs and FDs) in the field and the boardroom.

Minimum requirements for this role: 

- The Winning DNA: A minimum of 18 months in a full-cycle, outbound-heavy SaaS closing role. You must have a proven history of building your own pipe from scratch.

- Verified Overachievement: A track record of hitting and exceeding quota in a competitive, complex environment. We’ll want to see this on your resume. 

- Strategic Grit: Experience managing multi-stakeholder deal cycles and technical POCs. We value your ability to hunt more than the brand name on your previous CV.

- Native French language

An ideal candidate also offers: 

- Intellectual Curiosity: You are eager to learn the inner workings of diverse industries, from waste management to food distribution, to better align our technology with their operational pain.

- A Repeatable Sales Framework: You don’t rely on luck or intuition. You have a structured methodology that delivers success and you understand that consistent, high-quality inputs lead to predictable results.

- A Data-Minded Approach: You are a student of your own funnel. You understand how to structure your activity—prospecting volume, discovery depth, and multi-threading—to ensure a consistent output and forecast accuracy.

- Continuous Process Iteration: You possess a relentless drive for self-improvement. You are someone who actively seeks feedback, iterates on their approach, and understands that evolving your tactics is the only way to stay ahead of the market.

Total Rewards 

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working 

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual’s ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable. 

Belonging at Samsara 

At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, and other characteristics protected by law. We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.

Accommodations 

Samsara is an inclusive work environment, and we are committed to ensuring equal opportunity in employment for qualified persons with disabilities. Please email click here if you require any reasonable accommodations throughout the recruiting process.

Our Commitment to Authenticity 

We use Tofu , a fraud detection tool, to validate the authenticity of applications and protect against identity fraud. This ensures we are connecting with real people and allows us to prioritize genuine candidates. Please see Samsara’s Candidate Privacy Notice for more information.

Fraudulent Employment Offers 

Samsara is aware of scams involving fake job interviews and offers. Please know we do not charge fees to applicants at any stage of the hiring process.
