title: Financial Crime Lead
description:
What is Finary? 
Money is broken: most people’s wealth sits in products they did not choose, with fees they cannot see. We are putting a private banker in everyone’s pocket, with the same quality of advice for a €10K saver and a €10M client. Mounir launched Finary in 2021, and more than 1M people now track their wealth with us. Finary AI turns that context into a plan, and our investment products and in-house wealth advisors (Finary One) make it real.

Why now? 
AI makes this possible, and 3 things make it hard to copy: years of per-user financial data that no public dataset holds, a brand that brings in half of our new users through our own channels, and licences (PSAN, Investment Firm, MiCA) we secured before they became mandatory. We raised €40M from Hedosophia, Y Combinator and Speedinvest. Founders and leaders from Qonto, Photoroom, Bitpanda, UBS and Wise also invested.

What we offer 
We’re 70 builders with real ownership from day 1, tier-1 salary and equity, and offices in central Paris with hybrid remote. Our culture is direct and built on radical candor. AI is a real bar here: everyone has rebuilt how they work around it. Read more about our values here .

The opportunity

More than 1M people track and grow their wealth with Finary. In 2021, when a simple registration was enough to offer crypto in France, we chose to build fully regulated. Today Finary is a crypto-asset service provider under MiCA, an investment firm, a payment institution and an insurance broker. Very few European platforms hold that combination.

Our compliance team is organised by role, not by product: compliance officer, AML, senior advisory and control. Each role covers every licence. Reporting to our Head of Compliance, who is our AML/CFT officer, you'll work alongside our AML analyst and take ownership of the framework that protects our clients and our licences, with most of our exposure in crypto.

What you'll do

- Lead the AML/CFT framework: procedures, client risk classification, detection rules and tools (screening, blockchain analytics, Travel Rule), calibrated on our own data.

- Investigate and decide the hard cases: enhanced reviews of individuals and companies (ownership chains, financial statements, flows), on-chain investigations, decisions on suspicion.

- Draft and file suspicious transaction reports, and act as deputy TRACFIN declarant and correspondent.

- Handle screening and asset freezing: PEP, sanctions and adverse media hits, list updates.

- Build with AI: design and tune the agents and rules in our back-office tool that prepare files and clear first-level reviews, and keep the decision on suspicion human.

title: Product Designer - Paris
description:
As a Product Designer, you'll work on the H Platform, where our users create and run agentic AI workflows powered by our models. Nobody has written the playbook for designing these experiences yet. Our next stage is making the platform truly useful for its users and levelling it up, in design as much as in technology, and you'll build the product experiences that deliver real value in organisations.

At H Company, we believe AI should take action in the real world, and our mission is to make agentic AI genuinely useful for large organisations. We're pioneers in computer use: our own vision-language models power agents that see, click and type their way through the software businesses already run, with no integrations or rebuilds, and we own the whole stack, from research and models to the products built on top of them.

What you'll be doing

- Talking to our users constantly to understand their needs and figure out what will make the platform truly useful for them.

- Turning those insights into research and explorations, looking at problems from different angles before settling on a direction.

- Picking the right tool for each task: a Figma design, a prototype, or a small PR when a quick change is the fastest way to ship.

- Testing what you build with users, measuring its impact (A/B testing, user interviews, users daily use data...) and iterating quickly based on what you learn.

- Shaping the roadmap together with the whole team, engineers and PMs alike.

Who you'll work with

The role sits in our Product team, which is responsible for product direction, strategy and design. You'll join the product designer who owns design and UX today, and work closely with product, engineering and forward deployed engineers.

What we think it takes

Above all, we want someone who cares deeply about users, has great product taste and can explain it, moves fast while keeping quality high, leaves their ego at the door and welcomes feedback.

Likely a good fit if you 

- Have 5+ years of experience as a Product Designer at tech companies.

- Have excellent UX, UI and interaction design skills, and can make complex, technical flows, like building and running AI agent workflows, feel simple and intuitive.

- Have a portfolio that shows your latest work.

- Have hands-on experience running user tests and A/B tests.

- Know when a proven solution is good enough and when a problem deserves something new.

- Have designed complex data or ML/AI-driven products: you know how to make complex systems understandable and how to design for AI behaviour that isn't always predictable, building trust and keeping users in control.

- Are comfortable in technical discussions: you can dig into constraints and trade-offs with engineers and ramp up quickly on technical topics to discuss them with our researchers and more technical engineers.

- Are fluent in Figma.

- Can work within a design system and contribute to it.

Stronger still if you 

- Have designed platforms: complex B2B web or desktop software used by professionals, whether that's tools to build and run workflows, big data and analytics software, operational dashboards or other data-dense interfaces.

- Are curious about code and AI in your design workflow. Every design team is still figuring out how AI changes the way we work, and we're no different, so we'd love someone who has started experimenting, whether by prototyping in code, building small tools or bringing AI into their process, and who wants to keep exploring with us.

If you match most of this but not every point, apply anyway. We care far more about how you think, your curiosity and your care for users than a perfect match.

How we hire

Four stages: a 30-minute call with our Talent team, a 60-minute portfolio review, a 60-minute design interview in person at our Paris office, and a closing 30-minute conversation.

The portfolio review and design interview are built around your own work and how you design. Please apply with your CV and a link to your portfolio showing your latest work.

title: Junior AI Engineer
description:
Who we are

Lemrock builds the infrastructure of agentic commerce.

Tomorrow, consumers won't just buy on e-commerce websites. They will discover, compare and purchase directly inside conversational AI interfaces like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and a growing long tail of specialized AI assistants.

For brands, this is a major shift: if they are not present in these environments, they become invisible.

Our mission: enable any brand to exist, sell and distribute in this new channel.

Today, Lemrock is already:

- 100M+ conversations per month

- 150+ brand clients

- a $100B market structuring at high speed

The role

The product works, clients renew, and every month millions of people talk to AI agents running on our infrastructure before they buy. That traffic produces a unique dataset, and we want to get even more out of it: uncover the hidden patterns in how shoppers search, compare and decide, and use them to keep improving our recommendation algorithms and campaign performance.

As our Junior AI Engineer, this is applied work: you dig into the data, find what drives performance, ship the improvement to production and measure the result. You also maintain and improve our agents in production, and build the Claude Code skills that automate operational work and save time for the business team. You work directly with our Founding AI Engineer and the founders, alongside product and engineering.

Understand what drives performance 

- Explore our conversational and behavioural data, alongside campaign performance

- Track our key metrics, spot what moves, and find out why

- Surface the hidden patterns that make recommendations more relevant

Ship your findings to production 

- Turn your findings into improvements to our recommendation algorithms and agents, implemented in production

- Measure the impact directly with A/B tests, and feed the results into the next iteration

- Industrialise the analyses you run often into automated pipelines and monitoring, reviewed by the engineering team

Improve our agents in production 

- Maintain and improve our agents: prompts, tools, evaluation, and the code around them

- Turn client feedback into agent improvements: qualify what they ask for, and ship directly what can be handled at the agent level

Automate operations at scale 

- Build and maintain Claude Code skills that automate operational work at scale and free up time for the business team

Profile

Must-have 

- 0 to 3 years of experience, internships and work-study included. Fresh graduates are welcome.

- Personal projects where you built LLM agents end to end (prompts, tools, evaluation), or ran a serious data analysis on your own

- Hands-on prompt engineering: you write, test and iterate on prompts, and you measure whether a change actually made things better

- Solid SQL and Python for analysis

- The basics of statistics: you know how to read an A/B test and when not to trust a number

- You use AI coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor or similar) every day

- Rigorous and precise: you check your numbers before you share them

- Fluent French and professional English

A plus 

- A top engineering, business or data school, in France or abroad

- AI courses or certifications

- You have founded something, even small, and got real users or paying customers

- Hackathons, open source, or side projects that went further than a weekend

- TypeScript

- Recommender systems, ranking or applied ML experience

- E-commerce, advertising, growth or conversion experience

- BigQuery, dbt, PostHog

What we offer

- Competitive salary plus equity (BSPCE)

- You learn next to our Founding AI Engineer and the founders, two of them repeat YC founders

- A dataset very few people will ever see: 100M+ conversations a month between shoppers and AI agents

- An AI-first team: Claude Code and agents are part of everyone's daily work

- Ownership that grows fast: you start by taking real work off our plates, and take on more as you prove yourself

description:
ENSTA, établissement d’enseignement supérieur et de recherche sous tutelle du ministère des Armées, développe des activités de formation, de recherche et d’innovation dans les domaines de la défense et de la sécurité, des transports, de l'énergie, des activités maritimes, du numérique et de la santé.

L’école, présente sur deux campus, à Paris-Saclay et à Brest, est membre de l’Institut Polytechnique de Paris. Classée dans le Top 10 des meilleures écoles d’ingénieurs en France, elle a pour mission :

- la formation d’élèves ingénieurs civils et militaires, de cadres et docteurs pour les secteurs public et privé,

- la recherche et l’innovation de haut niveau en relation étroite avec l’industrie des grands secteurs de souveraineté au sein de 6 unités de formation et de recherche (UFR).

Le/la titulaire du poste sera affecté au sein de l’UFR S2I sur le Campus de Brest.

Projet FLOWATT 

Le projet FLOWATT, dans le cadre duquel s’inscrit cette étude, vise à déployer et exploiter six hydroliennes dans les forts courants marins du Raz Blanchard, en Normandie.

Au-delà de la production d’énergie, FLOWATT a pour objectif d’évaluer le potentiel du Raz Blanchard pour le déploiement de fermes hydroliennes à plus grande échelle. Cette évaluation repose notamment sur une caractérisation précise de la ressource, une estimation fine du productible et une meilleure compréhension des impacts environnementaux. Pour répondre à ces enjeux, le projet combine mesures in situ, modélisation numérique et essais expérimentaux afin de fournir les connaissances nécessaires à la préparation des futurs déploiements commerciaux, tout en contribuant à la réduction des coûts de production et à la limitation des impacts sur l’environnement marin.

Dans ce contexte, la caractérisation de l’état de mer constitue un enjeu important, notamment dans une zone soumise à des courants très intenses. La présente étude s’intéresse ainsi aux données de radar HF acquises depuis fin 2017, ainsi qu’à celles qui seront nouvellement enregistrées dans le cadre du projet TidalRace. Le système, de technologie WERA, est réparti sur deux sites distants d’environ 5 km au Cap de la Hague et fonctionne à deux fréquences, 13,5 MHz et 24,5 MHz. Les acquisitions sont réalisées en continu, à raison de quatre mesures par heure, 24 h/24 et 7 j/7, sur une emprise couvrant l’ensemble du Raz Blanchard. Cette couverture temporelle et spatiale offre ainsi une opportunité unique de suivre l’évolution des états de mer dans des conditions hydrodynamiques particulièrement contraintes.

L’exploitation de ces données nécessite toutefois d’adapter les méthodes de traitement aux conditions de forts courants. L’objectif des travaux est donc d’améliorer les algorithmes existants et, si nécessaire, d’en développer de nouveaux afin de restituer de manière fiable les spectres d’énergie des vagues en fréquence et en direction, ainsi que les paramètres moyens associés. Une première étape consistera à comprendre les limites des méthodes actuelles, qui ne permettent plus de restituer un état de mer cohérent avec les références disponibles lorsque la vitesse du courant dépasse 1 m/s, comme montré par Lopez et al. (2018). Les méthodes développées seront ensuite évaluées à partir des mesures in situ et des modélisations numériques. Le radar HF constitue ainsi un élément central de ce travail, dont l’amélioration doit permettre de mieux caractériser les états de mer dans les forts courants du Raz Blanchard . 

Missions / Activités principales : 

Le (la) titulaire du poste sera affecté à l’équipe M3 de l’UMR Lab-STICC et sera en charge des missions principales suivantes :

- Réaliser une étude bibliographique sur les modèles permettant de décrire l’effet des vagues sur le spectre Doppler mesuré par un radar HF

- Implémenter un code de simulation intégrant l’effet des vagues à partir d’une description de l’état de mer dans le spectre Doppler

- Analyser les simulations en les comparant aux mesures réelles pour comprendre l’influence du courant et plus particulièrement des forts courants sur la mesure d’états de mer

- Proposer et implémenter des évolutions des algorithmes permettant de s’adapter aux forts courants présents sur la zone du Raz Blanchard

title: Stage Assistant·e coordination de projet événementiel séminaire international
description:
Nous recherchons un.e stagiaire Assistant·e de coordination de projet événementiel pour le Séminaire international « Aides techniques et inclusion » (Dakar, juin 2027). 

Contexte : 

Titre de travail du séminaire : « Une offre de services de qualité en aides techniques : un pilier pour l’inclusion intersectorielle ». 

Le séminaire vise à construire et partager une approche commune de HI et de ses partenaires sur l’offre de services de qualité en aides techniques (identification, orientation, évaluation, adaptation, information et conseil aux usagers et aux aidants). Il couvre la mobilité, la vision, l’audition et la communication, et s’adresse aux secteurs de la réadaptation, de l’éducation inclusive et des moyens de subsistance.

Il s’inscrit dans l’accord-cadre (AC) 2023–2027, qui appuie 16 pays : en Afrique (Sénégal, Burkina Faso, Éthiopie, Mali, Niger, Madagascar, RDC, Rwanda) et hors Afrique (Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Cambodge, Laos, Myanmar, Népal, Palestine, Haïti). L’invitation pourra être ouverte à d’autres pays disposant de leurs propres sources de financement.

Il est organisé en articulation avec AT EXPO AFRICA 2027, premier dialogue international dédié à l’innovation, à la production et à l’accès aux aides techniques en Afrique, qui se tiendra sur le même site les 3–5 juin 2027 (Journée mondiale des aides techniques le 4 juin). Dates, agenda et logistique des deux événements sont à coordonner.

Cadre du stage : 

Le stage se déroulera à Lyon, avec un déplacement à Dakar (Sénégal). Vous êtes intégré à l'équipe de la Direction Réadaptation, composée de 12 personnes, incluant des spécialistes thématiques (dont 1 manager), des spécialistes de la réadaptation en urgence (dont 1 manager), une unité de reconditionnement de composants (avec 1 chef d’atelier), un adjoint à la direction et 1 assistante. 

Vos principaux interlocuteurs seront : 

• Le point focal en charge du contenu et de l’animation du séminaire (binôme de travail au quotidien)

• Les points focaux de HI Luxembourg et de HI Sénégal (logistique, finances, sécurité)

• Le point focal de la Division Résilience & Inclusion (éducation inclusive, moyens de subsistance)

• Les points focaux des pays de l’accord-cadre et le point focal de AT EXPO AFRICA 2027

• Les services communication, achats et finances de HI

Vos missions principales : 

Une phase d’intégration est prévue en début de stage : procédures HI, règles de sécurité, code de conduite et politiques de protection. 

Axe 1 – Coordination et pilotage opérationnel 

• Participer à la réunion de cadrage avec la tutrice, le point focal contenu et animation et les autres points focaux ; clarifier les rôles et les circuits de validation

• Reprendre et tenir à jour le rétroplanning et le plan d’action ; identifier les moyens nécessaires (budget, transport, salles, documentation, outils de présentation…)

• Assurer le secrétariat du comité d’organisation : préparation des réunions, comptes rendus, suivi des décisions

• Tenir un tableau de bord partagé (avancement, risques, points de blocage) et alerter rapidement la tutrice en cas de difficulté

Axe 2 – Participants et parties prenantes 

• Consolider la liste des participants (pays de l’AC, secteurs, partenaires, intervenants externes) à partir des premiers échanges déjà tenus avec les points focaux pays

• Préparer et envoyer les invitations et lettres d’invitation pour les visas ; gérer les inscriptions

• Mettre en place et tenir l’outil de suivi des participants (vols, visas, hébergement, contacts, besoins spécifiques), dans le respect de la protection des données personnelles

• Recenser les besoins d’accessibilité et organiser les aménagements raisonnables (accès des lieux, formats accessibles, accompagnants, interprétation)

• Recueillir les attentes des participants en amont ; concevoir, administrer et analyser l’évaluation du séminaire

Axe 3 – Logistique et achats 

En lien étroit avec les points focaux de HI Luxembourg et les équipes logistiques de HI Sénégal : 

• Finaliser le choix du lieu (déjà en discussion avec AT EXPO AFRICA 2027 et HI Sénégal), réserver les salles et l’hébergement ; négocier les tarifs et préparer avec le lieu tous les arrangements nécessaires

• Organiser les déplacements : billets d’avion des participants et intervenants, visas, transferts aéroport, transport local

• Organiser l’interprétation et les équipements techniques (sonorisation, connexion pour d’éventuels participants à distance)

• Sélectionner et suivre les fournisseurs selon les procédures d’achat HI ; commander le matériel, les impressions et les supports

• Préparer la logistique de la visite de terrain et des temps communs avec AT EXPO AFRICA 2027

• Pendant le séminaire : faire un point quotidien avec l’équipe d’organisation et le lieu, gérer les imprévus et remonter les problèmes

Axe 4 – Suivi budgétaire et administratif 

• Contribuer au budget prévisionnel détaillé ; suivre les engagements et les dépenses au regard du budget et des codes d’imputation

• Gérer les per diem, avances et remboursements des participants ; collecter les justificatifs

• Après le séminaire : clôturer les paiements fournisseurs, préparer les éléments financiers du rapport bailleur et transmettre les dossiers en cours

Axe 5 – Contenu, documentation et capitalisation 

En appui au point focal en charge du contenu et de l’animation du séminaire : 

• Contribuer à l’élaboration de l’agenda avec les parties prenantes et AT EXPO AFRICA 2027 (consolidation, gestion des versions, traductions)

• Appuyer les intervenants et facilitateurs dans la préparation des outils d’animation, des présentations et du matériel

• Produire le kit participant : agenda final, note logistique, informations pratiques sur Dakar, santé et sécurité, per diem, contacts

• Prendre des notes pendant les sessions et centraliser les ressources (présentations, documents) sur un espace partagé

• Rédiger le rapport du séminaire (plus spécifiquement le rapport au bailleur) avec le comité d’organisation ; contribuer à la compilation des outils et approches pour la note d’orientation

Axe 6 – Communication 

• Interne : informer les équipes via les canaux HI (Hinside, Teams, réseaux métiers)

• Externe : rédiger et/ou traduire en anglais des articles et publications (LinkedIn Rehabilitation), en lien avec le service communication et AT EXPO AFRICA 2027, en respectant les règles de visibilité du bailleur

• Assurer le lien avec les intervenants externes (experts, chercheurs, partenaires)

Et mettre en œuvre toute autre action nécessaire à la bonne organisation du séminaire. 

Calendrier indicatif : 

La préparation sera déjà engagée à l’arrivée du/de la stagiaire : lieu en discussion avec AT EXPO AFRICA 2027 et HI Sénégal, premiers échanges tenus avec les pays participants. Le/la stagiaire enclenchera directement l’achat des billets d’avion et les démarches de visas. 

• Janvier : intégration, reprise du rétroplanning et du budget, lancement des billets d’avion et des démarches de visas

• Février – mars : invitations et inscriptions, finalisation du lieu et choix des prestataires, suivi des visas, communication de lancement

• Avril – mai : contrats prestataires, recueil des attentes, agenda finalisé, kit participant et supports

• ~24 mai – 6 juin : à Dakar : installation et briefing, séminaire (31 mai ou 1er juin – 5 juin), AT EXPO AFRICA 2027 (3–5 juin), débriefing

8 – 25 juin : clôture financière, analyse de l’évaluation, rapport, passation

Contraintes particulières liées au stage : 

• Déplacement terrain : Dakar, Sénégal, environ deux semaines (~24 mai – 6 juin 2027). L’établissement d’enseignement doit valider ce déplacement en amont. Passeport valide et vaccinations à jour requis ; respect des règles de sécurité HI.

• Pic d’activité dans les semaines précédant le séminaire et pendant celui-ci : horaires pouvant être décalés, dans le respect du cadre légal des stages.

• Environnement multi-site et multilingue : Lyon, Bruxelles, Luxembourg, Dakar et 16 pays ; nombreux échanges à distance.

Engagement à respecter le code de conduite de HI et ses politiques de protection (exploitation et abus sexuels, protection de l’enfance, anti-fraude et anti-corruption, protection des données).

Requirements 

Vous êtes issu d'une formation Master en gestion de projets de solidarité internationale, action humanitaire et développement, affaires internationales, management d’événements ou logistique, ou équivalent.

Une première expérience en organisation d’événements (séminaires, conférences, formations), idéalement à dimension internationale, est un atout (stage, emploi ou engagement associatif)

Une expérience dans le secteur des ONG et/ou en Afrique de l’Ouest est appréciée

Une connaissance ou une expérience du milieu de la santé et du handicap est appréciée. 

Planification et suivi de projet : 

• Organisation logistique et suivi budgétaire de base (rétroplanning, tableaux de suivi)

• Très bonnes capacités de communication et de rédaction en français et en anglais (comptes rendus, rapports, articles)

• Capacité de synthèse et prise de notes

Savoir-être : 

• Rigueur, sens de l’organisation et des priorités

• Autonomie, esprit d’initiative, capacité à résoudre les problèmes

• Aisance relationnelle, diplomatie et goût pour le travail en équipe multiculturelle, y compris à distance

• Réactivité, sang-froid et adaptabilité face aux imprévus

Environnement informatique : 

• Maîtrise du pack Office, notamment Excel (tableaux de suivi, budget)

• Outils collaboratifs Microsoft 365 (Teams, SharePoint) et visioconférence

• Formulaires et enquêtes en ligne (MS Forms, KoboToolbox…)

• Usage raisonné des outils d’IA générative (traduction, synthèse, rédaction), dans le respect des règles de confidentialité de HI

• Outils de création graphique simples (Canva…) : un plus

Les participants seront francophones et anglophones, voire hispanophones. Toutes les communications orales et écrites se feront au minimum en français et en anglais.

Benefits 

Durée: 6 mois à temps-plein

Date de démarrage : à partir du 04/01/2027

Type de contrat: Stage 

Salaire: - Gratification mensuelle de 693€ 

- Tickets restaurant d’une valeur faciale de 8,96 euros (60 % à la charge de l’employeur, 40% à votre charge) 

- Participation de 50% à votre abonnement au titre des transports 

Vous devez disposer d’une convention de stage obligatoire délivrée par un établissement d’enseignement ou de formation français.

Les stages proposés chez HI donnent l’occasion aux étudiants d’évoluer dans une organisation internationale et de prendre part à l’action d’Humanité & Inclusion. Nous considérons que les stagiaires pour qui l’expérience s’est bien passée sont nos talents de demain !

title: Data Scientist & Analytics Engineer
description:
We’re a team of experts pushing the limits of what’s possible, united by our common goal to unlock true freedom through digital ownership, making technology accessible for all. We believe in a world where users, creators and enterprises manage their value with ownership and freedom. Our curiosity drives us to innovate, empowering individuals on a global scale. We believe change is constant and our team moves forward as one, with a culture of problem-solving where every employee is empowered and supported to challenge tradition and create solutions. Our mission is simple: to make self-custody accessible and give people the keys to their own financial futures. If you want to make a true impact, we want you to join us at Ledger.

At Ledger, we’re proud to be the global platform for digital assets and Web3, with over 20% of the world’s crypto assets secured through our Ledger devices. With our headquarters in Paris, and offices in Vierzon, Grenoble, Montpellier, London, Portland, Geneva, Zurich and Central Singapore, we have a team of around 600 professionals developing a variety of products and services to enable individuals and companies to securely buy, store, swap, grow and manage crypto assets – including the Ledger hardware wallets line with more than 7.5 millions units already sold in 200 countries. 

The team: 

You'll join the Data Team, responsible for turning data into actionable insights and recommendations for our consumer sales and marketing operations across all channels.

What you’ll be doing: 

- Own consumer sales analytics end to end: Ledger.com , Amazon, wholesale and resellers, from sell-in to sell-out, with one consistent view of revenue, units and margin

- Measure the true incremental impact of pricing, promotions and marketing campaigns with rigorous causal methods and experiments, and turn the results into budget recommendations for the Growth team

- Develop and improve data models (dbt/Snowflake) across varied data sources (sales, sell-out, marketing, web analytics) with the support of the data engineering team; co-own data quality alerting

- Own performance marketing measurement (attribution, ROAS, CAC), reconciling ad platforms, GA4 and internal sales data into a single source of truth

- Build and maintain Tableau dashboards that give business teams a clear, reliable view of their performance

- Model customer value (LTV, repurchase behavior, services attach) and feed it back into marketing ROI decisions

- Work as part of an AI-augmented team: use LLM-based workflows and AI agents daily to automate analyses and accelerate delivery

- Create and deliver presentations that turn complex analyses into clear recommendations for stakeholders up to ExCom level

What we’re looking for: 

- Proven hands-on data science experience applied to business decisions: you have run causal inference studies (CausalImpact, difference-in-differences, synthetic control, geo-experiments) and/or built predictive models (LTV, repurchase, propensity) whose results changed a budget or pricing decision

- Strong statistical rigor: comfortable with experiment design, confidence intervals and power, and able to clearly say when a result shows no detectable effect

- 2 to 4 years of experience in data analytics, analytics engineering or data science

- Strong SQL

- dbt skills are a plus

- Tableau skills are a strong plus

- Data driven and business oriented; able to challenge stakeholders' methodology

- Familiarity with marketing/web analytics data: GA4, ad platforms (Google Ads, Amazon Ads), affiliation networks are a strong plus

At Ledger, we are dedicated to continually investing in our employees which is why we offer more than just salaries; we provide comprehensive compensation packages that include a wide range of benefits. Here are some of the benefits you can look forward to:

- Flexible work options - Our hybrid policy allows employees to work from home up to 3 times per week

- Health & Wellness support - Health and Life Insurance.

- Financial growth opportunities - Employees can become shareholders in Ledger as well as other financial benefits depending on your country of work.

- Commuter allowance - Ledger offers a commuter allowance to contribute to your preferred means of transportation.

- Learning & Development - A comprehensive suite of training solutions providing a personalised learning experience for every employee.

For regionally specific benefits, your Talent Acquisition contact will be able to provide you with more information.

We’re committed to building an inclusive hiring process. If you need any adjustments or accommodations, just let us know, we’ll do our best to support you.

title: Embedded Software Engineer – Wireless Systems

title: Software Engineer, Robot Autonomy (Planning & Navigation)
description:
Our Mission

At Laelaps AI, we believe robotics is entering a transformative decade, much like the arrival of the internet. Advances in AI, cloud computing, and hardware are reshaping what autonomous systems can do. Our mission is to build the intelligent software that powers physical security in the real world - enabling robots and sensors to handle dangerous and critical tasks that humans shouldn't have to. By engineering the orchestration layer for intelligent security, we aim to create a world that is safer, more secure, and more resilient.

We're a strong founding team based in Zurich, backed by visionary investors and advisors. We are engineering the future of security today!

The Role

As a Software Engineer on Robot Autonomy, you will make our robots navigate dependably across real customer sites. Our stack works. The gap between working and dependable is the whole job. Every new site tests how a robot understands its surroundings and chooses where to go: a ramp the planner avoids, a narrow passage that exposes a poor route, a gate that changes the map, a person who steps into the robot's path, or localization drift that builds over a long patrol. You treat those cases as the real navigation problem to solve, not as edge cases.

You'll shape the technical choices behind reliable navigation, from sensor selection, ground segmentation, and traversability estimation to predicting how people and vehicles move and planning safe, efficient routes around them. The system has to work day and night, in challenging weather, across different embodiments and changing site conditions. We measure success by whether the robot completes its patrol on a live site, not by how it performs in simulation.

What You'll Work On

- Navigation and path-planning design: how robots represent traversable space, select routes, avoid obstacles, and reach goals across complex sites.

- Sensor integration driven by navigation requirements, including what ground segmentation and traversability estimation need in day, night, and challenging weather.

- Environment understanding: how the robot distinguishes ground from obstacles and estimates which terrain is safe and practical to traverse.

- Behavior prediction: anticipate how people, vehicles, and other dynamic obstacles will move, and plan routes that stay safe and efficient around them.

- Field reliability: reproduce failures from deployments, find the root cause, and fix it at the right layer, from sensor data and maps to costmaps, planners, and recovery behaviors.

- Planning under imperfect localization: plans that stay useful when the state estimate drifts and the robot must execute routes in tight or dynamic environments, working with the rest of Robot Autonomy on localization and control.

- Validation on real robots: logs, simulation, and repeatable field tests to verify that design choices and changes hold across routes, lighting, weather, and site layouts.

- New autonomy capabilities: work with the engineers building the operator application and backend so operator requests and new robot capabilities rest on a sound navigation design.

- The field feedback loop: work closely with forward-deployed engineers to turn site issues into bugs, design changes, and improvements to the navigation stack.

- Regular site visits to build a practical understanding of how robots and sensors behave in real operating conditions.

Who We're Looking For

We're looking for an engineer who has taken a robotics system from unreliable to dependable and takes ownership beyond individual tickets. You can explain why you made a navigation design choice and what it costs. When a robot takes a bad route, you can tell whether the planner, the map, the state estimate, or the robot's behavior is at fault, and you fix the right one. You are comfortable in the field and want to understand how robots behave in real customer environments.

Your Background

- A Master's degree or PhD in mechanical engineering, computer science, robotics, electrical engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

- Proven track record building and deploying navigation on ground mobile robots in the real world (3+ years or equivalent depth).

- Hands-on experience with mobile robot navigation and path planning: route or local planning, static and dynamic obstacle avoidance, costmaps, or recovery behaviors.

- Understanding of how mapping and localization affect navigation, and the ability to diagnose when a planning issue is actually caused by the map, the state estimate, or robot behavior.

- Understanding of how lighting, weather, terrain, and sensor limitations affect perception and navigation, with experience developing or validating systems for demanding real-world conditions.

- Hands-on experience with robotics sensors and hardware, especially LiDAR, IMUs, and cameras. You can investigate issues across software, networking, and hardware boundaries.

- Experience testing and debugging navigation on physical robots using logs, visualization, simulation, and repeatable field tests.

- Strong ROS 2, C++, and Python skills.

- Clear communication of navigation and path-planning design choices and their trade-offs.

- Willingness to visit customer sites regularly.

Nice to Have

- Experience with legged robots or with more than one robot embodiment.

- Experience with Nav2 or a comparable navigation framework.

- Motion prediction or planning among people and vehicles, such as trajectory forecasting or socially aware navigation.

- Terrain mapping and traversability methods: elevation mapping, learned traversability, or semantic segmentation for navigation.

- Experience with night-time or all-weather sensing, such as thermal cameras or LiDAR in rain and fog.

- Background in security, defence, or other safety-critical robotics deployments.

What We Offer

- Ownership: you are able to ship products and deliver project end-to-end.

- Mission: autonomous security that keeps people and critical sites safe, including in defence.

- Career path: a ground-floor seat with real runway. Prove your value and you will not have barriers to grow.

- Team: work directly with PhD-level co-founders in AI, Robotics, and Physics, alongside a strong (and fun) founding team.

- Compensation: Competitive equity/salary package

- Culture: International founding team that is serious about building but does not take itself too seriously.

title: FPGA Engineer Intern
description:
About Us 

Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces.

Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected.

About the Role 

As an FPGA Engineer Intern on Harmattan AI’s compute module team, you will take camera aggregation from concept to real hardware for the first time. Our drones carry more cameras than a single processor can take in, and your job is to show how an FPGA can close that gap. You will own the work end to end, from first design to a demonstrator on the bench. Your results will set how cameras are connected in our next hardware generation.

Responsibilities 

- Integrate existing IP cores, write HDL wrappers, simulate and validate FPGA logic that merges multiple camera streams into one.

- Investigate the system’s limits in camera count, resolution and frame rate.

- Build the processor-side pipeline that splits the merged stream so each camera stays independently usable.

- Debug the full chain, from cables and connectors to FPGA logic and camera software on the processor.

- Deliver a complete demonstrator and documentation that guide our next hardware design.

Candidate Requirements 

- Final-year Master’s or engineering school student in electrical engineering, electronics or embedded systems.

- Previous hands-on experience with FPGAs and digital board design and debugging.

- Experience writing software that runs close to the hardware; embedded Linux is a plus.

- Ideally, previous exposure to video or camera interfaces.

- Hands-on in the lab and comfortable reworking wiring, connectors and test setups to get a system running.

- Curious, autonomous and persistent when hardware refuses to behave.

- Full commitment to Harmattan AI’s mission, with the drive to go the extra mile.

We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of autonomous defense systems at Harmattan AI.

title: Composite Technician - Airframe
description:
About Us 

Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces.

Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected.

About the role 

As the composite technician on the Airframe team, your core mission is to prototype carbon structures fast, in-house — from mould to finished, quality-checked part — and to bring innovative solutions that make assembly and prototyping easier . A true hands-on professional, you combine technical skills, initiative, and a maker mindset. You build tooling, lay up and finish composite parts (carbon / glass fibre), and turn the engineers' CAD into flight-worthy structures on short cycles. You are also the owner of technical drawings and supplier quotations for the parts you handle, and the one who trains production operators when a design moves to series. You thrive with minimal supervision, favour pragmatic, quick-result approaches over perfect-but-slow tooling, and are equally comfortable laying up a part, machining or printing a mould, and reading a technical drawing.

Technical skills 

Key responsibilities 

Rapid in-house prototyping (core) 

- Produce carbon prototype structures quickly in-house, choosing the fastest viable route rather than heavy tooling when a proto is the goal.

- Propose innovative, simple solutions to speed up assembly and prototyping.

- Design certain parts and prototyping tools yourself (fixtures, adapters, simple structural parts) when it is faster than going through the design loop.

- Iterate fast with the design engineers: short loops between concept, part and feedback, flagging manufacturability issues before they cost a mould.

Tooling & moulds 

- Build and maintain moulds and tooling, in coordination with the design team; machine or 3D-print mould masters, prepare and polish mould surfaces.

- Design and build layup jigs, trimming templates, bonding and assembly fixtures.

- Manage the composite workshop consumables and material inventory (fabrics, resins, cores, vacuum consumables) including storage and shelf-life follow-up.

Design & documentation 

- Read and interpret 2D/3D drawings and ply books; model simple parts and tooling in CAD when needed; give manufacturability feedback early.

- Own the technical drawings: produce and keep up to date the manufacturing drawings for the parts and tooling you handle.

- Write and maintain clear, accessible fabrication procedures, ply books and cure logs on Confluence so processes are repeatable by others.

- Optimise part designs for their manufacturing process: adapt geometries for plastic injection (wall thickness, draft angles, ribs) or for composite / 3D-printed fabrication (layup feasibility, demoulding, printability), in collaboration with the design engineers.

Support & improvement 

- Support assembly and mechanical testing, including preparing test coupons and samples for structural analysis.

- Identify and propose process and quality improvements; help run the composite workshop safely (dust extraction, PPE, resin handling and waste management).

- Own the knowledge transfer to production: train the production operators on fabrication and assembly processes, and validate that a process is repeatable by others before handover.

Candidate profile 

- Technical diploma or degree in composite materials, mechanical / aerospace manufacturing, industrial technology, or equivalent hands-on experience.

- Proven experience in rapid in-house composite prototyping (carbon / glass fibre): hand layup, vacuum bagging, infusion and/or prepreg; mould making and surface preparation a strong plus.

- Track record of quick, pragmatic solutions — getting a functional carbon part out fast, with sound trade-offs, rather than perfect parts requiring heavy tooling.

- Ability to read technical drawings and ply books, and to control layup orientation, resin ratios, debulking and cure cycles with rigour and traceability.

- Ability to produce manufacturing drawings (2D plans) 

- Understanding of design-for-manufacturing basics for plastic injection (wall thickness, draft angles) and composite / 3D-printed parts, to optimise geometries with the design engineers.

- Hands-on finishing skills: trimming, sanding, drilling composites, structural bonding, insert fitting, and basic defect detection (porosity, delamination).

- Proficiency with common fabrication tools (hand tools, bench equipment, 3D printer; basic machining appreciated); CAD literacy (Fusion 360, SolidWorks, FreeCAD or similar) to adapt tooling and jigs.

- Highly autonomous — able to take ownership of tasks and drive them to completion with minimal supervision; resourceful and solution-oriented, comfortable improvising with available means.

- Pedagogy and communication : able to write clear, accessible procedures and to train production operators so processes remain repeatable without you; rigorous on process, safety and documentation.

We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of autonomous defense systems at Harmattan AI.

title: Senior Consultant (Strategy & Data/AI Transformation)
description:
Who is Artefact?

Artefact is a next-generation strategy and data consulting firm dedicated to transforming organisations through data and AI. We combine the rigour of top-tier strategy consulting with deep expertise in data, digital and analytics to help clients achieve tangible business impact.

With 2,500+ consultants, data scientists and engineers, we work with global leaders such as Samsung, L’Oréal, Orange and Sanofi. Our Swiss offices are at the heart of Artefact’s growth, advising clients on their most pressing strategic challenges — from AI strategy and governance to digital transformation roadmaps and new business model design.

Main Responsibilities

As a Senior Consultant in our Zurich/Lausanne office, you will work at the intersection of strategy consulting and data and AI delivery. You will:

- Strategy Development: Work with client leadership teams to address high-stakes questions. How can AI reshape our business model? How should we govern and organise for data? Which strategic programmes deliver the most impact?

- Structured Problem-Solving: Break complex challenges down into decisions a client can act on, combining consulting rigour with a working knowledge of what current AI can and cannot actually do.

- Solution Design: Turn a business question into a solution shape — what data it depends on, what kind of platform or product it should sit on, and what “good” looks like once it is built. You will do this alongside our data scientists and engineers.

- Project Delivery: Support engagements end to end, from hypothesis framing and market and competitor analysis through to data maturity assessments, client workshops, governance design and implementation roadmaps.

- Client Engagement: Work closely with C-level stakeholders and business unit leaders. You will build trusted relationships, communicate recommendations with clarity, and keep the work aligned to what the client is actually trying to decide.

- Knowledge & Practice Building: Contribute to the growth of Artefact's Zurich office by shaping new offerings, creating intellectual capital - frameworks, thought pieces, benchmarks - and taking part in business development.

Candidate Profile

We are looking for someone who can hold a technical position and a commercial one at the same time. The strongest candidates meet most of the following.

- Education: A degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, Business, Economics or a related field.

- Work Experience: Around three to five years in consulting, or in a technical/date-focussed role with client-facing responsibility. 

- Business Acumen & AI Fluency: A genuine dual affinity for business and technology. You are comfortable with modern data and AI concepts - generative AI and LLMs, retrieval, predictive machine learning, cloud platforms - and with what they cost and where they fail, not only with what they are called.

- Technical Depth: You have built AI or data products, not only advised on them. You can explain why you chose which model you put on which part of the work, and what that choice did to both output quality and cost. You will not be writing production code in this role, but you should have the basic understanding.

- Analytical & Problem-Solving Skills: Strong quantitative and analytical skills, and the judgement to know which number actually decides the question. You are comfortable getting to a defensible estimate with your assumptions stated out loud.

- Communication & Interpersonal Skills: Excellent written and verbal communication. You enjoy working in teams and in front of clients.

- Languages: Fluency in German/French and English, written and spoken, is strongly preferred.. 

- Work Eligibility: You must be eligible to work in Switzerland.

Why Join Us

- Strategy and the Build: Artefact is neither a traditional strategy consultancy nor a pure technology player. You will move between the boardroom and the build, and be expected to be credible in both.

- Engineers, not hand-offs: Our 2,500 people include the data scientists and engineers you will work beside on the same engagement - not a delivery organisation you hand a slide deck to.

- Zurich Office Impact: As part of a growing Swiss team you will have visibility and impact from the first day. You will help shape Artefact's footprint in the region and work directly with senior leadership.

- Learning & Growth: Regular training in both consulting method and AI and data capability, combined with international exposure.

- Culture of Doers: Innovation, action, collaboration. We are entrepreneurial and fast-moving, committed to delivering impact while supporting each other's growth.

This position is based in Zürich or Lausanne .

Medior/Senior Java & Angular Developer 

Delft | 32–40 uur per week | 

Wil jij met jouw skills écht impact maken in de zorg? Bij CHA bouw je niet zomaar software – je bouwt systemen waar honderden apotheken en uiteindelijk miljoenen inwoners in Nederland dagelijks op vertrouwen. Wat ga je doen als Java & Angular Developer? 

Voor jou begint software pas écht te leven als het draait in productie, veilig, snel en in handen van gebruikers. Je bent niet alleen een bouwer, maar ook een meedenker: van functioneel ontwerp tot technische architectuur. Samen met je collega’s zorg je dat onze applicaties future-proof zijn en optimaal draaien. 

De komende tijd werken we aan het moderniseren en modulariseren van ons applicatielandschap. Dat betekent: veel ruimte om jouw ideeën en expertise toe te passen. Samen met je collega’s ontwikkel je nieuwe features, verbeter je bestaande functionaliteiten en zorg je ervoor dat zorgverleners minder tijd kwijt zijn aan administratie, zodat zij zich kunnen richten op hun verdere bedrijfsvoering.

We zoeken geen alleskunner die elk vinkje af kan kruisen, maar een enthousiaste developer die zich wil verdiepen én verbreden. Of je nu uit de Java/Spring-hoek komt en je kennis van Angular wilt versterken, of juist andersom: je krijgt bij ons de kans om beide kanten uit te bouwen. 

Wat zijn je belangrijkste taken/verantwoordelijkheden? 

- Meedenken over software-ontwerpen en deze vertalen naar robuuste oplossingen. 

- Nieuwe features ontwikkelen én bestaande functionaliteit verbeteren. 

- Clean code schrijven, mét geautomatiseerde (unit) tests. 

- 2e-lijns support leveren bij gebruikersvragen en incidenten. 

- Technisch aanspreekpunt zijn voor externe softwareleveranciers. 

- Werken aan diverse applicaties die het verschil maken in de dagelijkse zorg. 

Wie ben jij, en wat breng je mee? 

Java 

- Diepgaande kennis van Java & Spring (Boot, MVC, Batch). 

- Bedreven met Hibernate en SQL. 

- Ervaring met CI/CD-tooling en testing frameworks, zoals JUnit en Mockito. 

- Basiskennis van Angular is mooi meegenomen. 

Angular 

- Up-to-date kennis van Angular. 

- Skills in HTML, CSS, JavaScript/TypeScript & RxJS. 

- Ervaring met CI/CD-tooling en testing frameworks, zoals Jasmine. 

- Basiskennis Java & Spring Framework 

Soft skills 

- Je bent zelfstandig, neemt initiatief en werkt oplossingsgericht. 

- Je voelt je verantwoordelijk voor je werk én dat van je team. 

- Je durft fouten te maken, leert ervan en helpt je collega’s vooruit. 

- Je deelt je kennis graag en staat open om ook van anderen te leren. 

- Je hebt affiniteit met de farmacie en interesse in declaratieverwerking in de zorg. 

- Samenwerken met je collega’s geeft jou energie. 

Wat bieden wij jou? 

- Een dynamische werkomgeving met korte communicatielijnen en een informele cultuur; 

- Een salaris tussen €5000,- en €6250,- bruto per maand (o.b.v. 40 uur), afhankelijk van ervaring en achtergrond. Dit is geen absolute range, wel een goede indicatie; 

- Jaarlijkse bonus (bij goede resultaten) ter hoogte van een maandsalaris. 

- Reiskostenvergoeding (€ 0,23 per km) of een NS Business Card met volledige OV-vergoeding; 

- Thuiswerkvergoeding en flexibele werkmogelijkheden; 

- Een aantrekkelijke pensioenregeling met een lage werknemersbijdrage; 

- Minimaal 26 vakantiedagen op basis van een 40-urige werkweek, met de mogelijkheid om feestdagen flexibel in te zetten; 

- Diverse secundaire arbeidsvoorwaarden zoals korting op sportabonnementen via Bedrijfsfitness NL, een fietsleaseplan, workation-mogelijkheden, sabbaticalopties en mantelzorgverlof; 

- Tijd en ruimte voor vrijwilligerswerk onder werktijd. 

- Een inspirerende werkomgeving met een een gezellig, hecht team. 

Wie zijn wij? 

Clearing House Apothekers (CHA) is onderdeel van MSPS Groep B.V. – Medical Software & Processing Services . Samen met verschillende bedrijven binnen de groep (o.a. Infomedics en Vertimart) zetten wij ons in om de zorg slimmer, efficiënter en menselijker te maken.

title: Senior Data Scientist BI
description:
Data Scientist BI - Senior
Almere | 32–40 uur | Hybride | €4.500–€6.800 bruto per maand 

Als Senior Data Scientist BI help je de organisatie maximaal waarde uit data te halen. Je vertaalt complexe vraagstukken naar concrete inzichten, dashboards, voorspellende modellen en AI-toepassingen die bijdragen aan betere processen, besluitvorming en aantoonbare businesswaarde. 

Als Data Scientist maak je onderdeel uit van het Business Intelligence team. Het BI-team ondersteunt alle labels binnen de MSPS Groep. Hierdoor krijg je te maken met uiteenlopende vraagstukken en draag je bij aan organisatiebrede besluitvorming, KPI's en strategische inzichten. Je werkt nauw samen met stakeholders om datagedreven werken verder te ontwikkelen en de organisatie te ondersteunen met data- en AI oplossingen. - Analyseren van informatiebehoeften en businessvraagstukken en het vertalen naar passende BI- en data science oplossingen voor stuurinformatie. 

- Leveren van organisatiebrede stuurinformatie, analyses, voorspellende modellen en AI-oplossingen ter ondersteuning van tactische en strategische besluitvorming. 

- Identificeren van kansen om meer waarde uit beschikbare data te halen, waaronder AI- en advanced analytics-toepassingen. 

- Verbeteren en borgen van de kwaliteit, integriteit, betrouwbaarheid en adoptie van data- en BI-oplossingen. 

- Mede vormgeven van de roadmap, architectuur en lifecycle van het Data & BI-product en bijdragen aan een toekomstbestendig data- en BI-landschap. 

- Coachen van collega's, uitvoeren van peer reviews en actief bijdragen aan kennisdeling binnen het team. 

- Actief bijdragen aan de ontwikkeling van het BI-team naar een high-performing team met een sterke data-, innovatie- en verbetercultuur. 

Wat breng je mee?

- Minimaal 5 jaar ervaring binnen Data Science, Business Intelligence, Analytics of een vergelijkbaar vakgebied. 

- Ervaring met het ontwikkelen van datamodellen, dashboards, stuurinformatie en geavanceerde analyses. 

- Ervaring met AI-, machine learning- en/of voorspellende modellen. 

- Kennis van data-architectuur, datamanagement en lifecycle management. 

- Het vermogen om complexe vraagstukken te vertalen naar begrijpelijke inzichten en concrete aanbevelingen. 

- Ervaring met het samenwerken met business stakeholders, productteams en technische teams binnen een complexe en dynamische organisatie. 

- Een proactieve houding waarbij je kansen signaleert en initiatief neemt om meer waarde uit data te halen.

- Sterke communicatieve vaardigheden en het vermogen om stakeholders op verschillende niveaus mee te nemen in datagedreven besluitvorming. 

Over het team 

Het huidige BI team bestaat uit drie BI-specialisten, een Data Scientist en een Product Owner. Het BI team maakt onderdeel uit van de afdeling Finance en wordt samen met de afdeling Business Control aangestuurd door de manager Business Control & Business Intelligence. We zijn een ambitieus team met ervaren professionals dat continu wil leren en verbeteren. We werken in een dynamische omgeving waarin niet alles vooraf vaststaat. Juist daarom zoeken we continu naar de juiste balans tussen flexibiliteit, voorspelbaarheid en het leveren van maximale businesswaarde. 

Daarnaast werken we aan een ambitieuze transformatieroadmap waarmee we ons Data & BI-landschap verder ontwikkelen tot een toonaangevende, AI-gedreven dataorganisatie. 

Onze groeifocus 

Jij speelt een sleutelrol in:

- Kennisdeling en coaching dragen zichtbaar bij aan de ontwikkeling van het team naar een high-performing team. 

Wat bieden wij jou? 

- Een dynamische werkomgeving met korte communicatielijnen en een informele cultuur;

- Een inspirerende werkomgeving, een gezellig team en een dagelijkse verzorgde lunch. 

Wie zijn wij? 

Infomedics is gevestigd in Almere waar bijna 300 mensen werken. Wij streven ernaar de administratieve druk van de zorg zoveel mogelijk bij zorgverleners weg te halen zodat ze zich volledig op hun patiënten en cliënten kunnen richten. Declaratieverwerking en factoring, dat is waar Infomedics goed in is. Door de volledige declaratieverwerking en het debiteurenbeheer uit handen te nemen, besparen zorgverleners tijd en geld. Infomedics is onderdeel van het ecosysteem van MSPS, lees hier meer. 

Binnen Infomedics bieden wij een financieel sterke en stabiele werkomgeving, met volop kansen voor onze medewerkers om door te groeien. Je werkt in een open en vertrouwde omgeving waar samenwerking en ontwikkeling centraal staan. 

De sollicitatieprocedure

description:

title: Product Manager (Web & App)
description:
Shape how tens of thousands of patients experience Wellis digitally, from first website visit to long-term treatment. Own the roadmap for our web platform and mobile app, and drive experiments that improve conversion, retention, and satisfaction.

Introduction 

The digital patient journey at Wellis is growing rapidly and becoming more complex. To take it to the next level, we're looking for a Product Manager Web & App. You will own the product roadmap and prioritization across our web platform and mobile app-from first visit and prescription flow through onboarding, subscriptions, and long-term engagement. Working closely with engineering, UX/UI, data, and key stakeholders across medical operations, marketing, and customer care, you'll turn insights into shipped improvements and experiments that lift conversion, retention, and satisfaction. This is a hands-on role with real ownership for an experienced product builder who wants to make Wellis' digital experience the benchmark in healthcare.

About Wellis 

Wellis is a fast-growing healthtech scale-up that is reinventing one of the most traditional sectors: healthcare. What started just three years ago has already grown into a company with tens of thousands of customers, and we are only at the beginning. By combining medical expertise with technology and data, we make healthcare smarter, more efficient, and more personal.

Our mission is to improve everyday lives by making care accessible, personal, and seamless. Through our platform, people can take control of their health journey with trusted medical support, smart digital tools, and tailored programs. We move fast, challenge conventions, and build solutions that truly make an impact, because we believe better healthcare should be within everyone's reach.

About the Role 

As a Product Manager Web & App, you'll own the product direction for Wellis's web platform and mobile app across the full digital patient journey - from first visit through long-term treatment. You'll translate business goals, user needs, and medical requirements into a clear roadmap, and partner closely with design and engineering to ship improvements that drive conversion, retention, and satisfaction. With a strong eye for data and user insight, you'll identify friction points, run experiments with our CRO specialist, and align stakeholders across the business to keep the product vision sharp and execution moving fast.

You will start by owning the web platform and the mobile app together across the full digital patient journey. Both are first-class products. As the team grows, ownership may concentrate more on the app. We want someone who thrives owning both at the start and can adapt if focus deepens into mobile later.

Key Responsibilities 

- Own the product roadmap and prioritization for Wellis's web platform and mobile app, translating business goals and user needs into clear features and improvements.

- Define, scope, and deliver product initiatives across the full digital patient journey - from first visit to long-term treatment and subscription management.

- Run product experiments together with our CRO specialist (A/B tests, feature releases) to improve conversion, retention, and user experience.

- Work closely with UX/UI and engineering to ship high-quality features that support weight management treatments, subscriptions, and the broader wellness platform.

- Analyze user behavior data, customer feedback (e.g., via Intercom), and medical team insights to identify friction points and opportunities for innovation.

- Set clear product objectives and success metrics, and continuously track outcomes (including conversion, app/feature adoption, and NPS for the digital experience).

- Align and manage stakeholders across medical operations, customer care, marketing, and leadership, while maintaining a clear product vision.

- Communicate roadmap progress, trade-offs, and learnings clearly, and help the organization make data-informed product decisions.

About the Team 

In this role, you'll work day-to-day with Engineering and UX/UI to define, prioritize, and ship improvements across our web platform and mobile app. You'll also partner closely with colleagues in marketing & growth, data & analytics, medical operations, and customer care to translate business goals and patient needs into a clear roadmap and to validate decisions through research and experimentation. As our digital domain is growing fast, you'll have a key role in shaping how we build product at Wellis and how teams collaborate across the full digital patient journey.

Who You Are 

- Extremely entrepreneurial and resourceful . You invent paths when playbooks do not exist, and you ship without waiting for perfect conditions. 

- Strong product instincts. You have a clear sense for what patients and the business need next, including when the data is incomplete.

- This role is 100% AI- and agent-enabled . You are comfortable with an agentic product development process and with working with agents as part of how you build. You have clearly shown proficient use of agentic systems such as Claude, Codex, ChatGPT, Grok, or Cursor. Bring specific instances. Examples include shipping a feature end to end with agents, turning a backlog into agent-runnable specs, or cutting cycle time by pairing with coding agents. We will ask for those examples in the process.

- Bachelor's or Master's level education.

- 5+ years of experience as a Product Manager or Product Owner for web platforms and mobile apps.

- Experienced in a start-up/scale-up environment , comfortable with speed, ambiguity, and pragmatism.

- Strong at translating business goals and user needs into a clear roadmap, priorities, and well-defined product requirements.

- Data-informed and outcome-driven; able to define and track product KPIs like conversion, adoption, retention, and NPS.

- Comfortable running experiments (e.g., A/B tests, feature releases) and collaborating with a CRO specialist on hypotheses and success criteria.

- Confident partnering daily with engineering and UX/UI to ship intuitive, high-quality experiences across the digital patient journey.

- Strong stakeholder management skills and the ability to influence without formal authority across medical, operations, marketing, and leadership.

- Curious and customer-focused; skilled at turning feedback and insights into concrete product improvements.

- Fluent in English;

- Experience in healthcare, subscriptions, or marketplace/e-commerce environments is a plus.

What We Offer 

- The opportunity to help build a fast-growing healthtech scale-up from the inside.

- A hands-on Product Manager role with real ownership of the web platform and mobile app roadmap.

- Close collaboration with engineering, design, medical operations, marketing, customer care, data, and leadership.

- The chance to make our web platform and mobile app the envy of everyone else - improving conversion, retention, and the end-to-end patient journey.

- A culture of short lines, speed, pragmatism, and continuous improvement - where impact matters.

- Hybrid working: partly from our new office in central Rotterdam, partly remote (We are flexible on that so dont hesitate to apply)

Hiring Process 

- Introductory chat with Georgios (Recruitment Lead) – an informal online call to get to know you and answer your questions.

- Interview with the CTO – a deep-dive conversation about the role, your experience, and Wellis' ambitions.

- Case & presentation – you'll prepare a case on site and present it to at least 2 stakeholders. This way, you get to know us better, and we get to know you.

- Final conversation with the founders – a closing meeting where you'll hear more about the bigger Wellis story and feel whether this is the right place for you.

We keep the process compact and clear: you'll always know what to expect and truly get to know our team before making your decision.

title: DevOps/Platform Engineer
description:
Do you want to own the infrastructure under a health-tech operation that touches hundreds of thousands of lives? This is a dedicated infrastructure, security, and platform role, and there's a lot of ground to claim. Right now a handful of engineers keep the whole stack running between them. Your job is to turn that into something that runs and scales on purpose, and to make it more secure while you do. The more reliable we are, the more people we help lead healthier, happier lives.

About Wellis 

Wellis is a fast-growing healthtech scale-up reinventing healthcare. We are building the first truly integrated health platform in the Netherlands, offering on-demand care for everyday health needs such as weight loss, hair loss, sexual health, and more. Our platform covers the full journey: from diagnosis and medical assessment to prescription and delivery at home. By combining medical expertise, technology, and data, we make healthcare smarter, more accessible, more personal, and easier to use. We are growing quickly, which means we are building the structures, teams, products, and processes that will help us scale responsibly. You will join an ambitious, international team where ownership is encouraged, collaboration is key, and impact is visible from day one.

The Role 

You won't inherit a mature platform team here. You'll help build one. Our services already run across more than one cloud, most provisioning still happens by hand, and we have very little visibility into what's actually going on in production. Fixing that is the job: bringing order, portability, and security to all of it, and doing it the way our engineering team already works, which is agent-first.

The role covers three areas, and we mean all three. On infrastructure, you'll own how and where we run. We want managed services that stay portable, so we can pick up a workload and move it between GCP, AWS, or anywhere else without rewriting it. On security, you'll own access provisioning, database security, secrets, and the controls a company handling patient data has to get right. On IT and platform admin, you'll own onboarding, offboarding, team access, and tooling: the unglamorous plumbing that keeps a growing team moving.

What ties the three together is automation. We're not looking for someone to click through consoles all day. We're looking for someone who builds the systems and agents that make provisioning, deployment, and access self-serve.

We're an AI-native engineering team. Agentic coding tools are how we work, and infrastructure is no exception. Think Terraform written and reviewed with an agent, runbooks that are actually scripts, an access request that a workflow fulfills on its own. You'll bring that habit to a corner of the company that usually gets it last.

What You'll Own 

- Provider-agnostic infrastructure. Define our infra as code so it's reproducible and portable. Containerize workloads, standardize how services get deployed, and keep us free to move between clouds instead of locked into one. Today we run across more than one provider mostly by accident. You'll make it a choice. 

- CI/CD and release engineering. Build the pipelines that take code from merge to production safely: automated, repeatable, with the guardrails that let a small team ship often without breaking things.

- Observability and reliability. We have almost no monitoring, alerting, or error tracking today. You'll build the visibility layer from scratch, from metrics and logs through tracing, uptime, and the basics of on-call, so we catch problems before customers do.

- Security and access. Own IAM and least-privilege access across our systems, plus database hardening, secrets management, and the audit trails a regulated healthcare business needs. Access for people and services should be controlled and reviewable, never handed out ad hoc.

- Team provisioning and IT admin, automated. Onboarding, offboarding, accounts, and tooling access, built as workflows and agents rather than a ticket queue. When someone joins or leaves, the right things should happen without a person doing them by hand.

- Infrastructure agents and tooling. Build the skills, scripts, and agent workflows that let the whole team self-serve infra and access. This is the leverage that lets a small team run like a bigger one.

What we offer 

- Salary range €5,500 – €8,000 gross per month, depending on experience, plus 8% holiday allowance

- Pension plan

- Learning budget

- Monthly personal budget (Alleo)

- Hybrid working: partly from our new office in central Rotterdam (2 days)

- 20 days of remote working per year

- Working from home allowance (2 days a week)

- 25 holidays

- A culture of short lines, speed, and continuous improvement, where pragmatism and impact matter

- The chance to build a healthtech scale-up's entire infrastructure and security foundation from the ground up

Essential 

- 3+ years of professional DevOps, platform, SRE, or infrastructure engineering. You've owned production infrastructure, not just touched it. Fundamentals matter more than years here: what happens on deploy, how to recover, how to keep it running.

- Infrastructure as code, done properly. Terraform, Pulumi, OpenTofu, or equivalent. You provision through version control, not a console, and you know why that discipline matters.

- Cloud, with an eye on portability. Real experience with at least one major cloud (GCP, AWS, or Azure) and the container tooling (Docker, plus Kubernetes or a managed equivalent) that keeps workloads movable. You've thought about lock-in and how to avoid it.

- CI/CD ownership. You've built and maintained pipelines that other engineers depend on, with the automated checks and rollbacks that make frequent deploys safe.

- Security fundamentals. IAM and access control, secrets management, network basics, and database security. You know how to give people and services exactly the access they need and nothing more.

- Agentic AI development is how you work. You spend a real part of your day in tools like Claude Code, Cursor, Pi, or opencode, and you point them at infrastructure and ops, not just app code. Given a repetitive task, your instinct is to automate it. 

- You've felt the pain. A migration that locked a table, a deploy that took down an endpoint, an access mistake you had to clean up at 2am. You owned it, fixed it, and built the guardrail so it couldn't happen twice.

Nice to Have 

- Building agents and agentic workflows, not just using them: plugins, skills, or custom automations that made infra or ops better for a team.

- Experience with regulated or sensitive data (healthcare, financial services, government). You know why 'move fast and break things' has no place near patient data.

- Observability tooling stood up from scratch: Sentry, Prometheus and Grafana, Datadog, OpenTelemetry, or similar.

- IT administration at a growing company: SSO and identity providers, device and access lifecycle, automated on and offboarding.

- Audit logging and compliance in regulated environments (NEN 7513, GDPR, ISO 27001, SOC 2, or similar).

- Running Supabase, Postgres, or serverless and edge platforms (Cloud Run, edge functions) in production.

- Multi-cloud or cloud-migration experience, meaning you've moved real workloads between providers.

- Dutch and/or German (business English is the working language).

Who You Are 

- You take ownership from provisioning through deployment through monitoring, right up to the 2am page.

- You automate by instinct. Do something twice by hand and you're already writing the thing that does it for you.

- You're comfortable being the first and only person in your domain, making decisions that carry weight, with no team to hide behind yet.

- You treat security as the default. You handle access and data like someone's health depends on it, because it does.

- You work fast and stay careful.

With Your Application 

Alongside your CV, share a transcript or a detailed walkthrough of the most interesting agentic session you've had recently, one where the agent did real infrastructure, ops, or automation work. Provisioning, a pipeline, a migration, an access workflow, whatever it was. Tell us what you were building, how you steered the agent, and what you'd do differently. We'd rather read that than a cover letter.
