Sayari’s largest customers, the biggest government agencies and Fortune 100 companies, are moving from data products to an agentic platform that runs their investigation and risk workflows end to end. As a Forward Deployed Engineer II, you are dedicated to those accounts. You own the technical win (demo, proof of concept, trial), then the deployment, then what comes after. The same engineer scopes the problem and ships it.

You are equal parts engineer, strategist, and operator. You embed in the customer’s environment, build on Sayari’s agentic platform against their data and their workflows, and solve high-stakes problems that have no textbook answers. You are the conduit between the front lines and core engineering: what you learn in the field becomes what the platform does next.

What You’ll Do 

- Win the technical evaluation: design and run demos, proofs of concept, and trials that prove the platform on the customer’s own data. Define success criteria with the customer and hit them.

- Deploy the agentic platform: build agents, tools, and integrations on Sayari’s agentic platform inside the customer’s environment, and take them from trial to production.

- Embed and build: ship production Python, SQL, and integrations into customer persistence layers and analytics stacks.

- Own the relationship: serve as the primary technical authority for the account. Brief executives, analysts, and mission owners on outcomes.

- Triage and feed engineering: decide what is bespoke, what is reusable, and what belongs in the platform. Document capability gaps and drive them into the roadmap.

- Raise the bar: set delivery standards and review work for other engineers on your accounts.

What We’re Looking For 

Required 

- 5+ years in a client-facing technical role (forward deployed engineering, sales engineering, or technical consulting).

- 7-8+ total years of experience working in software engineering and/or solutions consulting

- A record of owning strategic deployments end to end, from technical win to production.

- Production Python, including the data manipulation ecosystem (Pandas). Deep experience having worked with SQL. Hands-on experience integrating and reasoning about REST APIs.

- Building and deploying on cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, or Azure) with containers (Docker, Kubernetes).

- You are a technology polyglot, you have worked across multiple tech stacks and enjoy getting the opportunity to navigate different coding languages, frameworks, and systems. 

- AI-assisted coding tools (Cursor, Claude, or similar) as a daily part of how you work.

- Executive communication. You articulate technical concepts with clarity and conviction to engineers, analysts, and senior leaders alike.

Desired

- Sovereign, air-gapped, or government cloud deployments.

- Modern data stack (Snowflake, Databricks) and workflow orchestrators (Airflow, Prefect).

- Graph data technologies and their query languages.

- Exposure to ML, NLP, or entity resolution.

- Experience in high-stakes domains: AML and financial crime, supply chain risk, or national security.

title: Staff Software Engineer, AI-Native Systems
description:
Staff Software Engineer, AI-Native Systems 

Location: Remote (US)

We are 

Virtual care only works if the infrastructure behind it does. Wheel builds that infrastructure: the systems that let telehealth run at scale for the patients, clinicians, and companies that depend on it. We're not bolting AI onto old workflows; we're rebuilding how care gets delivered, with AI in the product and in how we build it.

We do this in a live, regulated healthcare environment where getting it right matters. This is the next architecture of virtual care, and we're building it now.

You are 

A staff-level engineer who has built software in a regulated, high-stakes domain (ideally health tech; fintech and insurtech count too) and knows what that demands: sensitive data, regulatory constraints, and the cost of getting it wrong. You've designed and shipped AI and agentic systems in production, you know where they break, and you have opinions, held loosely and argued well, about building them safely.

You're a builder first, and you've done real work in small, scrappy teams. You still write the hard parts of the code yourself, and you've done it recently. You don't need a platform org, TPMs, or layers of review to move.

You operate as a domain owner, not a task owner. You take a problem that isn't well-formed, define it, tie it to what the business has committed to, and lead a group of engineers to a shipped, measured outcome. Your impact shows up in other people's work: the patterns they reuse and the ambiguity you removed before it cost the team a quarter.

You get things done. You have sharp judgment about what actually moves the outcome, you'd rather ship something useful this week than something perfect next quarter, and you know when good enough is good enough (and when, in healthcare, it isn't).

And you're good to work with. You're curious, generous with your time, quick to give credit, and you can disagree hard without making it personal. Smart matters here; kind matters just as much. Bonus points if people genuinely enjoy being on a team with you.

The Work 

Technical Leadership & Direction 

- 
Own the technical direction for a significant AI-native area of the platform, such as patient and clinician experiences, care delivery, or the AI platform layer other teams build on.

- 
Act as tech lead for a team or cross-team initiative: break down ambiguous problems, sequence delivery, clear blockers, and keep the team pointed at the outcome rather than the ticket.

- 
Connect day-to-day engineering to quarterly commitments and company goals, and make those links visible to the team.

- 
Write and review design docs. Make and document the load-bearing calls, including "not yet" and "buy, don't build."

AI & Agent Engineering 

- 
Design and build production AI features and agents: retrieval, orchestration, tool calling, guardrails, evaluation, and observability.

- 
Define what "production-ready" means for AI here (testability, rollback safety, cost ceilings, failure modes, human-in-the-loop boundaries) and hold the bar in review.

- 
Take on the hardest parts of the build yourself. This is a hands-on role; you are expected to be in the code every day.

Healthcare-Grade Engineering 

- 
Treat privacy, security, and responsible AI use on sensitive health data as hard engineering requirements, and turn compliance constraints into concrete architecture.

- 
Partner with clinical, compliance, and legal stakeholders early, so safety and review are designed in rather than bolted on.

- 
Build for the realities of healthcare: integrations with clinical systems, auditability, and high-reliability workflows.

Cloud-Native Delivery 

- 
Own full-stack delivery in TypeScript/Node.js and Python: services, APIs, data jobs, and the interfaces on top.

- 
Own deployment, monitoring, and troubleshooting in production, including on-call, and improve the operational posture of what you inherit.

Measure & Improve 

- 
Own the evaluation strategy for your area: metrics, test harnesses, and plans for accuracy, latency, safety, and cost.

- 
Instrument systems so their behavior is legible after the fact, not just at demo time.

- 
Kill approaches that aren't working, early and visibly.

Stakeholders & The Org 

- 
Work directly with product, operations, clinical, and business leaders to decide which use cases are worth building.

- 
Explain trade-offs and risks clearly to technical and non-technical audiences, up to the executive team.

- 
Mentor engineers through code review, design review, and pairing, and build reusable patterns that raise the bar beyond your own team.

What success looks like 

- 
First 30 days: you've shipped something to production, met the people you'll build with, and know where the sharp edges are.

- 
First 90 days: you own an area, set its technical direction, and have shipped AI features with an evaluation story behind them.

- 
First 6 months: patterns you established are used by teams you don't sit on, the business can point to outcomes you drove, and engineers say their work got better (and more fun) because you're here.

What we're looking for 

- 
8+ years building and operating production software, with full-stack depth in TypeScript/Node.js and at least one other language (Python strongly preferred).

- 
3+ years building software in health tech, fintech, or insurtech, including work with sensitive data under HIPAA, PCI, SOC 2, or similar requirements.

- 
Hands-on experience designing and shipping AI or agentic systems in production (retrieval, orchestration, tool calling, evaluation), with a clear view of where LLMs work and where they don't.

- 
A record of shipping outcomes, not just output: you can point to what you delivered, why it mattered, and the judgment calls you made to get it out the door.

- 
Recent hands-on output: in the last two years you've personally built and debugged significant production systems, not only directed others.

- 
Meaningful time at a startup or growth-stage company where you owned what platform, release, or infrastructure teams would handle elsewhere.

- 
A track record of technical leadership as an IC: owning a domain, leading multi-engineer efforts to completion, and driving decisions across teams without positional authority.

- 
A collaborative, low-ego style: you raise the people around you and make hard conversations easier, not harder.

- 
Fluent use of AI development tools as a force multiplier, with judgment about when to trust, verify, or override them.

- 
Strong cloud-native fundamentals: CI/CD, observability, and running what you build. Fluency with relational data and SQL.

- 
Clear written and verbal communication, including design docs that change minds. This is a remote, cross-functional role.

Strongly desired 

- 
Health tech experience specifically: telehealth, EHR/EMR, digital health, payer/provider, or pharmacy.

- 
Experience with clinical workflows or integrations with clinical systems (EHRs, e-prescribing, labs, HL7/FHIR).

- 
Model evaluation and guardrail infrastructure: measuring output quality, catching regressions, and keeping AI inside safe bounds.

- 
Patient-, clinician-, or customer-facing AI products shipped to real users.

- 
Experience building platform capabilities consumed by other engineering teams.

- 
Experience as a formal tech lead or mentoring engineers.

What's hard about this role 

We'd rather you hear it now: 

- 
Ambiguity is the job. Problems often arrive half-formed, and priorities can shift as the business and market change.

- 
You'll build, not just direct. There's no large platform org; you'll write code, run what you ship, and take on-call.

- 
Healthcare raises the bar. Clinical safety, privacy, and compliance review are part of shipping, and they take real time.

If that sounds energizing rather than draining, we'd love to talk.

How we work 

Remote-first (US), fast-moving, with tight loops between engineering, product, clinical, and the business. We're an AI-forward engineering org: we expect AI in the toolchain and in the product, and we measure outcomes over activity. We handle sensitive healthcare data under strict controls; privacy, security, and responsible AI are engineering requirements, not afterthoughts.

We take the work seriously, not ourselves. We're direct and kind, we help each other out, and we have fun doing it.

Salary and Perks 

Pay Range: $185,725-$264,500 USD

Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors including, but not limited to, the scope and responsibilities of the role, the selected candidate’s work experience, education and training, the work location as well as market and business considerations. 

As an employee of Wheel, you’ll enjoy our Total Rewards Program to help secure your financial future and preserve your health and well-being, including:

- 
Medical, Dental and Vision

- 
Ancillary: Life, Short and Long Term Disability

- 
401K match

- 
Flexible PTO

- 
Parental Leave

- 
Stock options

- 
Additional programs and perks

Wheel is committed to equal employment opportunities for all team members. Every decision we make regarding employment is solely based on merit, competence, and performance. We are committed to building a team that represents a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills. 

Research shows that underrepresented groups typically apply only if they meet 100% of the criteria listed. At Wheel, we encourage women, people of color, and LGBTQ+ job seekers to apply for positions even if they don’t check every box for the role.

We are looking for applied AI engineers to build AI-native systems for BJAK's AI Finance Agent.

This is not a research-only role. We need builders who can use AI to automate real workflows, improve products, reduce manual work and make financial services easier for users and teams.

What You'll Own 

- 
Build AI-powered workflows, assistants, agents and automation systems.

- 
Apply AI across customer support, CRM, onboarding, claims, renewals, payments, operations and internal tools.

- 
Work with product and engineering teams to turn manual processes into scalable AI-native systems.

Build integrations with LLMs, internal data, APIs, documents, knowledge bases and business systems.

- 
Design evaluation, monitoring and fallback flows so AI outputs are useful, safe and reliable.

- 
Prototype quickly, test with users or operators, then productionize what works.

- 
Improve speed, quality and consistency across workflows using AI where it creates real business value.

What We're Looking For 

- 
Strong software engineering foundation, preferably with Python and backend systems.

- 
Hands-on experience building with LLM APIs, agents, RAG, workflow automation or AI tools.

- 
Able to connect AI systems with real product, data and operational workflows.

- 
Good judgement on where AI helps and where rule-based systems or human review are better.

- 
Understands evaluation, accuracy, latency, cost, privacy and failure modes.

- 
Fast builder who can prototype, test and ship practical systems.

- 
Experience in fintech, insurance, support automation, CRM or operations automation is a strong advantage.

The Kind of Builder We Want 

- 
Practical AI builder, not just a prompt experimenter.

- 
Thinks in workflows, systems and measurable quality.

- 
Can build quickly but still cares about guardrails and reliability.

- 
Comfortable working with messy real-world data and processes.

- 
Honest about what AI can and cannot do.

This Role Is Not For 

- 
People who only want research projects with no production ownership.

- 
Candidates who treat AI as demos instead of working systems.

- 
Engineers who do not care about evaluation, reliability or user impact.

- 
People who overclaim AI impact without evidence.

- 
Builders who cannot work with product, ops and business teams.

Location 

This role is remote, but candidates must be based in Netherlands . We are hiring specifically for this market, so applicants should already be based in Netherlands. 

Language 

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview Process 

Our process is designed to move fast:

- 
Online assessment or practical task

- 
Technical interview

- 
CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

title: Principal Software Engineer, Data Lakes
description:
From Fivetran ’s founding until now, our mission has remained the same: to make access to data as simple and reliable as electricity. With Fivetran, customer data arrives in their warehouses, canonical and ready to query, with no engineering or maintenance required. We’re proud that more organizations continue to leverage our technology every day to become truly data-driven.

About Us

Fivetran and dbt Labs are bringing together two industry-leading companies with a shared mission: helping organizations unlock the full value of their data.
Together, we’re delivering the data infrastructure layer that helps organizations move, transform, and trust their data — from the moment data moves, through every transformation, to the context teams and AI systems rely on.
Fivetran helps organizations automate data movement across the systems, clouds, engines, and tools they rely on. dbt Labs pioneered analytics engineering, helping teams transform data into reliable, governed insights. Together, we support thousands of organizations as they build a trusted foundation for analytics, AI, and better business decisions.
As we bring our teams and technology together, we’re building on the strengths of both companies while continuing to deliver the products and experiences our customers know and trust. It’s an exciting time to join us: we’re creating a company with the scale, talent, and technology to help more organizations put their data to work with greater speed, confidence, and impact.
During this transition period, you may see references to both Fivetran and dbt Labs throughout our recruiting process as we integrate our teams, systems, and career sites.

About the Role 

Fivetran is building data pipelines to power the modern data stack for thousands of companies.

We’re seeking a Principal Software Engineer to contribute to the technical architecture, design and development of Fivetran’s Managed Data Lake product offering. As part of a senior engineering team, you’ll partner with product and engineering teams to build scalable, high-performance systems, advance open-source technologies, and set technical standards that raise the bar across the organization. 

This is a full-time remote position based out of Germany.

description:

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.

How we work

- 
High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

- 
Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

- 
AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

- 
Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.

What we offer

- 
Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

Learning & development : ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

ElevenMusic is a consumer music app where music is the core product: a place to listen, create, remix and stream. The team works in its own environment, separate from the main org, and is agent-first with fast CI, so ideas reach users within a day or two.

title: Staff Performance Engineer, JavaScript Engine (SpiderMonkey)
description:
Why Mozilla ? 

Mozilla Corporation is the non-profit-backed technology company that has shaped the internet for the better over the last 25 years. We make pioneering brands like Firefox, the privacy-minded web browser. Now, with more than 225 million people around the world using our products each month, we’re shaping the next 25 years of technology and helping to reclaim an internet built for people, not companies. Our work focuses on diverse areas including AI, social media, security and more. And we’re doing this while never losing our focus on our core mission – to make the internet better for people. 

The Mozilla Corporation is wholly owned by the non-profit 501(c) Mozilla Foundation. This means we aren’t beholden to any shareholders — only to our mission. Along with thousands of volunteer contributors and collaborators all over the world, Mozillians design, build and distribute open-source software that enables people to enjoy the internet on their terms. 

About this team and role: 

The JavaScript team at Mozilla works to make Firefox's industry-leading JavaScript engine SpiderMonkey even more performant. We push the boundaries of what the web is capable of, shaping the future of the JavaScript language through standardization at TC39, while keeping in mind the fundamental principle of “don’t break the web.”

As a Staff Software Engineer on the SpiderMonkey team, you'll be a domain expert who drives the engine's runtime performance forward, from the interpreter and JITs to the garbage collector, while also helping maintain and advance the health of a large, mature C++ codebase. You'll typically lead performance projects within the team, planning the work and mitigating the risk yourself, and you'll mentor other engineers as you take on increasingly ambiguous, high-impact problems.

What you’ll do: 

- Lead runtime performance initiatives: Own projects to improve SpiderMonkey's runtime performance, from profiling and identifying bottlenecks to designing and landing optimizations across the interpreter, JITs, and garbage collector.

- Provide technical leadership to the team: Mitigate risk for the performance projects you own, planning work that may start out ambiguous and require significant up-front design and prototyping.

- Maintain and advance the codebase: Help preserve the correctness and stability of a large, mature C++ codebase while improving its architecture and maintainability as the JavaScript language and the engine continue to evolve.

- Track and shape the JavaScript standard: Work with the JavaScript team to keep up with the evolving TC39 standard, and help evaluate proposals where performance or implementation tradeoffs are involved.

- Strengthen engine security: Collaborate with the Fuzzing team to identify and close security issues in the JavaScript engine.

- Mentor and elevate the team: Mentor other engineers by stewarding some of your existing responsibilities to more junior team members as you take on new, larger initiatives, and help the team build stronger performance-analysis and benchmarking practices.

- Communicate clearly: Turn team strategy and goals into concrete action for the projects you lead, and communicate progress, tradeoffs, and technical decisions clearly to your team and to partner teams.

- Use AI tools day to day: Incorporate AI-assisted tools into your workflow for debugging, prototyping, code analysis, and development.

What you’ll bring: 

- 5+ years developing C++ applications

- Demonstrated expertise in systems programming, including direct experience with one or more of: compilers, garbage collectors, interpreters, and virtual machines

- Strong background in performance analysis, profiling, and benchmarking on large and complex software

- Experience with general systems architecture (x86, x64, ARM, ARM64, etc.)

- A track record of technical leadership: planning ambiguous projects, sequencing project work, and mitigating risk with minimal help

- Experience mentoring other engineers and helping raise a team's technical standards

- Creative problem solver with strong debugging skills and a detailed approach to code review

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills; comfortable turning team strategy into action and communicating tradeoffs to peers

- Comfortable incorporating AI assisted tools into your day-to-day engineering workflow

- Rich medical, dental, and vision coverage

- Generous retirement contributions with 100% immediate vesting (regardless of whether you contribute)

- Quarterly all-company wellness days when everyone takes a pause together

- Annual professional development budget

- Quarterly well-being stipend

- Considerable paid parental leave

- Employee referral bonus program

Mozilla exists to build the Internet as a public resource accessible to all because we believe that open and free is better than closed and controlled. When you work at Mozilla, you give yourself a chance to make a difference in the lives of Web users everywhere. And you give us a chance to make a difference in your life every single day. title: Product Engineer, Nino
description:
Overview 

CoinTracker is on a mission to unlock everyone's financial potential so they can build the life they want. We started with crypto, building the tax and portfolio tools that millions of users trust to trade digital assets with peace of mind. Nino builds the next layer of financial fluency for our users. Nino is an AI-powered financial operating system that makes comprehensive, expert-level tax and financial planning advice accessible.

More on Nino: Comprehensive tax and financial planning strategies are currently locked behind high AUM fees or require enough wealth to have a family office. We are turning expert judgment into software so we can serve millions. AI is going to redefine how people understand their finances and how tax advice gets delivered. Not in ten years, in 2026. You can help define that, or spend the next few years adapting to rules someone else wrote. Nino sits inside CoinTracker ($100M raised, partnered with Coinbase, TurboTax, H&R Block, and Thomson Reuters) with the autonomy of an early-stage startup and the reach of an established platform.

Your mission 

As Product Engineer, you'll own customer problems from the first conversation to a working product. You'll talk to users, shape the idea, design the experience, and build it across the stack. You'll work closely with engineers, design, and our CPAs and Financial Planners to turn complicated financial work into software people can understand and trust.

Your one-year outcomes

- 
Customers rely on what you build. You've shipped meaningful features end to end, with evidence that customers use them and find them valuable.

- 
More financial work gets done. Workflows you own help households and advisors complete tasks with less manual effort, fewer handoffs, and clearer next steps.

- 
The experience holds up. Your features are easy to use and reliable in practice, including when information is missing, an integration fails, or a person needs to step in.

- 
We learn and ship faster. You turn ambiguous problems into focused releases, learn from real usage, and use that evidence to decide what to improve next.

What you will do 

- 
Examples of what you could build:

- 
Trading: Help users go from an investment idea to a reviewed trade, with clear approvals, execution status, and visibility into what happened.

- 
Strategies: Build ways to discover financial ideas, understand their upside and tradeoffs, explore how they fit a household's situation, and turn a saved strategy into a plan of action.

- 
Tax filing: Bring document collection, missing-information requests, CPA review, and filing progress into one clear experience for households and their tax team.

Across these features, you'll:

- 
Own problems from discovery to launch. Talk with customers and financial experts, identify what matters, and decide what to build first.

- 
Design the experience. Sketch, prototype, and refine interfaces with our designer. Make complex decisions and workflows feel clear.

- 
Build across the stack. Ship interfaces, backend services, integrations, and AI workflows. Follow the problem wherever the implementation takes you.

- 
Turn agents into useful products. Build ways for people to understand, review, and approve an agent's work, including workflows that span external tools and websites.

- 
Make the whole flow work. Handle incomplete information, interruptions, retries, and human handoffs. Verify that the task actually finished correctly.

- 
Use AI tools to ship and iterate. Move quickly, understand and check what you ship, and keep improving it through customer feedback and usage.

What we look for

- 
Role-agnostic

- 
Opportunity alignment: You want to help households manage complex finances and bring expert tax and financial planning to more people. You're excited to shape a product on a small, early team.

- 
High agency: You see what needs doing and take responsibility for it. You can start with an incomplete brief, find the missing information, and make progress.

- 
Exceptional collaboration: You make the people around you better: engineers, designers, CPAs, and Financial Planners. You seek feedback, say what you think, and follow through.

- 
First-principles thinking: You start with the customer's problem, question assumptions, and can explain why your approach makes sense. You change your mind when the evidence changes.

- 
Role-specific

- 
Strong engineering fundamentals. You've built and shipped working software, can reason through unfamiliar systems, and care about correctness and maintainability.

- 
Product judgment. You can turn an open-ended problem into a useful first release, explain what you left out, and define how you'll know it helped.

- 
Design taste. You notice confusing interactions, care about the details, and can explain how your changes improve the experience.

- 
You ship your own work. You're comfortable moving between the interface and backend, using AI coding tools thoughtfully, and verifying the result.

- 
Bonus: startup, agent, or integration experience. You've built directly with users, worked with browser automation or AI agents, or connected systems that don't fit neatly together.

Prior experience with finance, AI or ML products, or our exact tech stack isn't required. Neither is a particular degree or school. We're interested in what you've built and how you think.

title: Lead AI Engineer, LLM Systems
description:
Company Overview 

hermeneutic research is a best-in-class proprietary trading firm. It deploys research-driven discretionary and systematic strategies as well as makes strategic long-term investments. The partners' decade-long history of success in trading and business building and a firm-wide cultural emphasis on alpha generation, open debate, relentless iteration, and teamwork are key to the firm's continued expansion in a challenging market environment that has hamstrung competitors. A hard-wired emphasis on risk management and opportunistic market participation ensures that hermeneutic research will continue its growth trajectory in the coming decades.

Job Overview 

You will own a multi-agent research system as production infrastructure: make it faster, cheaper, measurably better and efficient.

hermeneutic Research Labs is the firm’s applied research and engineering unit. Its first product is a research intelligence platform for both traditional and digital-asset markets, built with our researchers and traders and used by them every day. The platform turns market, on-chain, macro and news data into event-driven research that trading decisions rely on. The platform is held to the standard we apply to our own trading: rigorous, falsifiable and measured on outcomes.

The Labs is making a multi-year investment to turn the platform into production infrastructure that a growing set of internal users can depend on. As part of that investment, it is hiring a Lead AI Engineer.

The LLM layer is yours for years. A research query runs through multiple agent stages across several model providers and our own self-hosted models. You start with your hands on the system, writing code and running experiments. As the function grows, you will hire and lead its engineers. The role is built to grow into Head of AI Engineering.

Key Responsibilities

- Keep the LLM layer reliable: latency budgets, concurrency and queueing, declared degradation modes, structured-output validation and provider failover.

- Build evaluation tied to research outcomes: offline sets from real queries with outcome labels, online experiments, regression gates on every change, and model-generated confidence calibrated with quantitative research before it reaches a decision.

- Control cost and routing: per-workload cost attribution, difficulty-based routing between small and frontier models, caching and batching, and the economics of self-hosted serving and GPU capacity.

- Run model strategy and lifecycle: pinned model versions, replayable test batteries before any change, one-step rollback, provider diversification, and fine-tuning or adapters where they pay.

- Shape the agent architecture with evidence: ablate and retire components that do not earn their keep, and improve tool use, memory and retrieval only where they move research outcomes.

- Ground and trace outputs: citation, hallucination controls, audit trails, and the boundary between what a model may assert and what it may only suggest.

- Build the team: review and mentor engineers now, and hire and lead an AI engineering group as the function grows.

Requirements

Must-Haves 

- 7+ years of software or ML engineering, including 3+ years shipping LLM-backed systems to real users in production, where you owned latency, cost and quality, and 2+ years leading other engineers while still shipping.

- A track record of building a function from nothing.

- Command of inference economics: tokens, caching, routing, structured outputs, tool use and quantisation, with cost-per-request figures for the systems you ran.

- Measurement discipline: you instrument before changing anything, evaluate against outcomes rather than model judges, have built an eval that caught what a vibe check missed, and have retired a component with data.

- Strong Python, including async concurrency.

- Experience with self-hosted serving (vLLM or similar), adapters and GPU capacity planning, or an end-to-end provider migration.

- Depth in vector and graph retrieval, built and measured, with an informed view on when retrieval is the wrong fix.

Technologies named here are what we run today, not a filter. We hire for depth and judgement.

Desired Attributes

- Directness: you tell the author when their component does not earn its keep.

- Sound judgement working alongside AI coding agents on a largely AI-written codebase, keeping ownership of what ships.

- Initiative: you take on the hard, unowned problem first, and bring the profiling data and a first fix.

- Bonus: fine-tuning and preference optimisation in production, and an informed view on when multi-agent frameworks are over-built.

- Bonus: finance or trading exposure, and experience hiring engineers.

Interview Process 

- 
CV Screening – We will review your application based on the qualifications and experience outlined above.

- 
Hiring Manager Screen – A conversation about the LLM systems you have run in production.

- 
Systems Deep-Dive – A whiteboard session on LLM systems design.

- 
Hands-On Round – A take-home on a synthetic trace set with a review, or a live debugging session.

- 
Reliability and Measurement Scenarios – A scenario discussion with peers from research or risk.

- 
Collaboration and AI-Assisted Work – A conversation on how you work with teammates and AI coding agents.

- 
Co-Founder Interview – A concluding discussion to assess your capabilities, strategic thinking, and cultural fit.

Company Values 

Throughout the process, you'll be assessed for cultural fit through our company values:

- 
Drive – We believe the best team members are deeply passionate about what they do. That passion fuels their growth, drives them to seek out the best teams, and leads them to hold high expectations of themselves in pursuit of excellence.

- 
Ownership – We aim to extend ownership as broadly as possible across the firm. In return, we value people who take initiative, step up when needed, and treat the company’s goals as their own.

- 
Judgment – We value those who see the big picture and focus on what truly drives impact and results. They use time wisely, adapt across domains, and always prioritize outcomes over comfort zones.

- 
Openness – We foster a culture of open communication, mutual challenge, and shared growth. We believe constructive debate and proactive knowledge sharing lead us closer to the truth—and better decisions.

- 
Competence – We work with people who bring exceptional intellectual strength. What sets them apart isn’t just what they know—it’s how they use what they know to navigate change, adapt quickly, and contribute meaningfully in fast-changing environments.

description:
About the Role

The Coding Specialist is responsible for independently reviewing, analyzing, and resolving all assigned front-end scrubs and denied claims to ensure accurate and timely claim payment. This position focuses on identifying and correcting coding-related issues prior to claim submission, resubmitting corrected claims or appealing denied claims, applying established coding guidelines, payer requirements, and organizational policies. The Coding Specialist works closely with revenue cycle partners to prevent claim rejections, support clean claim rates, and promote efficient reimbursement processes. This role requires strong attention to detail, foundational coding knowledge, and the ability to work independently in a fast-paced environment.

A Day in the Life

- Averages 10 front-end holds/denials per hour

- Reviews coding and resubmits corrected claims to insurance

- Creates appeal letters/forms with medical documentation

- Maintains a minimum of 92% coding accuracy.

- Assigns ICD-10-CM and CPT codes with appropriate modifiers for services provided in the professional fee environment.

- Reviews medical records and all applicable documentation to determine appropriate codes for documented services and diagnoses.

- Ensures all diagnosis codes meet local and national medical necessity guidelines.

- Utilizes internal coding resources, payer guidelines, and other reference materials to ensure accurate and compliant coding for all assigned services.

- Follows all HIPAA regulations and upholds the highest standards of privacy and confidentiality.

- Maintains current knowledge of laws, regulations, payer policies, and industry guidance impacting compliant coding practices.

- Independently reviews and resolves all assigned front-end claim holds.

- Actively participates in department meetings, one-on-one meetings, and mentorship meetings with the assigned Coding Team Lead.

- Escalates identified client trends to the assigned Coding Manager.

- Escalates all coding-related questions to the assigned Coding manager for guidance and clarification.

- Maintains and completes all CEU requirements.

- Performs other duties or tasks as assigned

What You Need

- Must hold a current AAPC or AHIMA Coding Certification for a minimum of 3 years.

- Minimum of 3+ years of professional coding experience.

- Strong working knowledge of CPT, ICD-10-CM, medical terminology, anatomy and physiology, and state and federal Medicare reimbursement guidelines.

- Prior experience in reviewing front end coding errors before submitting to insurance

- Prior experience in reviewing and correcting coding from insurance denials. 

- Prior experience in submitting corrected claims and appeals.

- Prior experience with insurance guidelines and EOBs.

- Familiarity with proper English grammar, usage, and professional documentation standards.

- Ability to research and analyze data, draw logical conclusions, and resolve coding or documentation issues.

- Ability to read, interpret, and apply policies, procedures, laws, and regulations.

- Ability to accurately read and interpret medical documentation, clinical terminology, and documented procedures.

- Demonstrated ability to exercise independent judgment in coding and claim resolution.

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare reports, clarify documentation needs, and maintain collaborative working relationships with physicians and staff.

- Strong commitment to maintaining confidentiality and safeguarding protected health information.

- Prior experience working in a medical billing environment with strict adherence to HIPAA compliance requirements.

- Demonstrated proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook, Teams).

title: Principal Product Management, Growth
description:
Headquarters: Remote

ZoomInfo is where careers accelerate. We move fast, think boldly, and empower you to do the best work of your life. You’ll be surrounded by teammates who care deeply, challenge each other, and celebrate wins. With tools that amplify your impact and a culture that backs your ambition, you won’t just contribute. You’ll make things happen fast.

Principal Product Manager, Growth

About ZoomInfo

ZoomInfo is where careers accelerate. We move fast, think boldly, and empower you to do the best work of your life. You'll be surrounded by teammates who care deeply, challenge each other, and celebrate wins. With tools that amplify your impact and a culture that backs your ambition, you won't just contribute — you'll make things happen, fast.

The Opportunity

Own a Growth Portfolio and Set the Pattern the Rest of the Team Inherits

ZoomInfo built the industry's most sophisticated GTM data platform. The next frontier is turning every visitor into revenue without waiting on a human handoff — a coherent self-serve journey that activates a non-customer in minutes, converts consumption into upgrade, and routes high-intent signals back to sales when a human will close more than they distract.

You'll define the multi-quarter thesis on which channels compound, the operating rhythm the rest of the growth PM team inherits, and the ZoomInfo POV on how buyers discover us in an AI-first world.

The impact is immediate and compounding. Every signup you activate, every credit you cause to be consumed, every transaction, every PQL you route, every "buy more" event you trigger is revenue — and every operating pattern you set multiplies across the growth PM group. We've adopted a consumption-first monetization model and a unified entry-point thesis across the company, and we run weekly: if your hypothesis can't be falsified inside a sprint, it isn't a hypothesis. This is a rare opportunity to own a P&L-shaped surface with full air cover to ship fast, learn in public, re-pivot when the data turns — and to define the growth PM craft as ZoomInfo scales it.

What You'll Do

Own the Portfolio End-to-End

Take a portfolio-scope growth surface — and own it from first impression to revenue. Define the entry points, the activation milestones, the monetization moments, and the sales-assist signals across the channels that make up the portfolio. Drive the user experience across surfaces: landing, signup, in-product onboarding, empty states, upgrade modals, paywalls, lifecycle communication, and the agent-readable / LLM-discovery surfaces that are becoming primary. You own the funnel chart; you own the why behind every drop.

Set the Multi-Quarter Growth Thesis

Beyond weekly experiments, own 4-8 quarter bets on which channels compound and which retire. Publish a written POV on where PLG distribution is heading (LLM-first discovery, MCP-as-channel, agent-readable onboarding, partner-driven trials) and defend the sequencing to the exec team. Rebalance investment across the portfolio quarterly based on unit economics, not the loudest channel.

Run Experimentation as the Operating Rhythm — and Set the Rhythm for the Team

Ship 8-10 experiments per sprint. Pre-register the hypothesis, the metric, the success threshold, and — critically — the invalidation signal. Read results weekly, kill what doesn't work, double down on what does, and keep a written record so the team compounds learning instead of repeating it. Your rubric, your retro format, and your invalidation-signal standard become the template the rest of the Growth PM group inherits. Translate results into concrete changes: copy rewrites, schema tweaks, pricing changes, new flows, retired ones. Close the loop with engineering, design, and analytics inside the same week.

Design Self-Serve as a First-Class Path

Most users on your portfolio never speak to sales before they hit a "buy more" moment. Your in-product copy, paywall framing, empty states, activation paths, and upgrade triggers are the product. Apply growth-engineering rigor — credit economics, consumption pacing, signal routing, lifecycle messaging, intelligent gating — so the right offer lands in front of the right user at exactly the right moment. Hand high-intent users to sales with a clean signal; absorb low-intent users with a clean self-serve path.

Diagnose the Funnel With Data, Not Vibes

Data is your default tool, not a thing you ask analytics to do for you. You independently analyze the funnel, segment the cohort, find the leak, and propose the fix — then validate it with an experiment. You know when to trust a 5% lift and when to call it noise. Just as important: you know when to zoom out from a specific funnel drop to a portfolio-level rebalance, and can defend that call.

Shape the Monetization Mechanic

You'll design the credit economics of your portfolio: what's free, what's gated, what gets a "buy more" prompt, what triggers a PQL. You'll model the unit economics — credit cost, revenue per credit, upgrade rate, expansion rate — and you'll defend the pricing decisions in front of finance and sales leadership with the math.

Orchestrate Across Sales, Marketing, and CS

Self-serve doesn't mean alone. You'll route PQLs into the right hands (AE, SC, AM, or no one), partner with marketing on acquisition and lifecycle, and work with CS to understand why activated users churn before upgrade. You'll run the operating cadences that keep your portfolio aligned with the broader PLG portfolio without becoming a meeting machine.

Multiply the Team

Help hire and calibrate the Sr Growth PMs owning adjacent loops. Coach them into ownership. Your retro is their template; your experiment quality is their bar. Raise the craft of the whole Growth PM group as it scales.

Stay Honest About What's Working

Write retrospectives that name the wrong calls as cleanly as the right ones. Update your priors publicly when the data turns. Hold strong opinions weakly. The team that ships the most experiments isn't the team that's right the most — it's the team that updates the fastest.

What You'll Bring

- 8–12 years of product management experience, with 4+ years specifically in growth, PLG, or self-serve product roles

- Direct P&L ownership at portfolio scope — a loop or portfolio you've driven from $Y with your name on the number, not a feature inside someone else's loop

- Experience presenting to CEO / CRO / CFO / board on growth mechanics — the credit-economics deck, the funnel narrative, the "kill this bet" moment

- Track record of hiring, mentoring, or calibrating other growth PMs — comfortable being the bar

- You're a builder. You ship landing pages, signup flows, and in-product experiments — not specs that sit in Jira. You sit with designers and engineers, write copy, and prototype with code.

- AI-fluent with a public POV. You understand that LLMs are becoming a primary discovery surface. You have opinions — publishable ones — about agent-readable flows, MCP-as-distribution, GEO/AEO, and how an AI agent's recommendation impacts a funnel.

- Marketing-fluent. You hold your own with SEO, paid acquisition, content, and lifecycle marketing teams as a peer, not a consumer.

- Demonstrated track record of running structured experimentation (A/B tests, multivariate, holdouts, pre/post) at sprint cadence — including at cohort sizes where 50/50 doesn't have power

- Strong analytics fluency — comfortable in Snowflake without analyst hand-holding

- Working knowledge of consumption-based pricing, credit economics, freemium mechanics, and PQL frameworks

- B2B SaaS background; data, GTM, or sales-tech domain experience is a plus but not required

Who You Are

Core Competencies

Funnel Foundation. Expert-level understanding of full-funnel growth. You can reason about activation rates, time-to-value, retention curves, credit economics, upgrade triggers, and PQL signal quality with depth. You've owned a growth loop — or portfolio — in production. SQL and analytics fluency let you diagnose a funnel drop, prototype the fix, and validate it in the same week.

Portfolio Thinking. You reason about ToF (or an equivalent surface) as a portfolio of channels with different unit economics, decay curves, and compounding dynamics — not a single funnel. You rebalance investment quarterly based on where marginal dollars return the most, and you can defend the rebalance to leadership with the math.

Experimentation Discipline. You don't ship without a hypothesis. You pre-register the metric and the invalidation signal before the test runs. You read results honestly, kill losing variants without ego, and document learnings so the team compounds knowledge instead of relitigating settled questions. You know the difference between an experiment and a launch — and you can tell when each is the right move.

Category POV. You have a public, defensible point of view on where PLG distribution is heading — agent-readable surfaces, MCP-as-channel, GEO/AEO, LLM-first onboarding — grounded in benchmarks from peer companies (Clay, Linear, Vercel, Cursor, Notion), not just internal data. That POV shows up in the roadmap.

Distribution Mindset. Experience designing growth surfaces where sales teams, marketing teams, and self-serve users are simultaneously your customers. You measure success through revenue, consumption, and expansion velocity, not screens shipped. You understand growth economics: each additional entry point, freemium offer, or AI trial compounds in value through shared activation patterns, amortized acquisition costs, and recurring consumption network effects.

Operational Velocity. You read the funnel daily, not quarterly. You prototype emerging mechanics — paywalls, in-app prompts, lifecycle sequences — to understand their practical constraints before committing engineering time. You hold strong opinions weakly, updating your design assumptions as evidence accumulates, publicly, even when the prior thesis was your own.

Strategic Communication. You translate between funnel depth and business impact fluently. You can explain to the CEO why a credit pricing change is worth a quarter of work. You can communicate to engineers why a revenue constraint requires a "quiet release" in two weeks rather than a polished launch in three months. You influence without formal authority through forcing functions, falsifiable invalidation signals, and earned credibility.

Talent Leverage. You coach Sr PMs into full ownership of their loops. Your retro is their template. Your experiment quality is their bar. You help hire the next PMs on the team, and you calibrate — you know what "great" looks like at Sr level and you can articulate the gap to someone who isn't there yet.

Copy Instinct. Microcopy is part of your craft, not someone else's job. You can rewrite a paywall headline, an upgrade modal, an empty state, or an onboarding CTA on instinct — and defend the rewrite with PLG principles. You know when to ask content design for help and when to ship the rewrite yourself.

The Environment

Reporting, Pace & Impact

Reporting & Collaboration. Report to the VP Product, PLG. Peer to the Sr Directors of Marketing, Sales Operations, and Customer Success on the growth contracts (PQL routing, demand-gen alignment, credit economics). Work shoulder-to-shoulder with the engineering and design leaders building the underlying surfaces, the GTM leaders routing PQLs into sales, and a peer PM group covering monetization, lifecycle, viral, onboarding, and analytics. Regular exposure to the CEO, CRO, CMO, and CFO — you own those conversations at your level.

Pace & Problems. Fast-moving teams that understand the space. Weekly experimentation cadence layered under 4-quarter portfolio bets. Expect interesting problems: How do we win activation in a user's first 60 seconds? When should two trial flows become one? How do we expose enough value to convert without giving away the platform? How do we price a credit so that customers consume

title: Senior ML Engineer (R14284)
description:
Headquarters: Remote - India 

Who We Are 

Oportun (Nasdaq: OPRT) is a mission-driven financial services company that puts its members' financial goals within reach. With intelligent borrowing, savings, and budgeting capabilities, Oportun empowers members with the confidence to build a better financial future. Since inception, Oportun has provided more than $22.7 billion in responsible and affordable credit, saved its members more than $2.5 billion in interest and fees, and helped its members set aside an average of more than $1,800 annually. 

A Quick Note on the Role's Focus 

While the title is Senior ML Engineer , this opportunity is specifically focused on ML Platform Engineering rather than ML model development or data science.

We're looking for engineers with strong software engineering fundamentals and hands-on experience building, scaling, and operating the platforms and infrastructure that enable machine learning in production. The emphasis is on ML infrastructure, MLOps, model serving, platform reliability, and production engineering , rather than primarily developing, training, or fine-tuning ML models.

Location Note 

We’re excited to consider talent currently based in India, as well as candidates who are open to relocating to India for this opportunity. Please note that, as this is a "Remote–India" position, the role must be performed from within India. 

The Opportunity 

The Machine Learning Platform team builds the software foundations that enable data scientists and machine learning engineers to develop, validate, deploy, and operate models safely and efficiently in production. In this role, you’ll lead complex platform work from business context through production outcomes, combining hands-on engineering, architectural judgment, production ownership, and mentorship. In your first year, success means leading meaningful platform initiatives, improving reliability and developer experience, and becoming a trusted technical leader for the ML platform. 

At Oportun, we move fast and hold each other to a high bar. You’ll partner across Data Science, Product, Risk, Fraud, and Engineering to solve ambiguous problems and move the needle for members and the business.

What You'll Do 

Your day-to-day 

- You’ll lead the design, implementation, deployment, and operation of complex platform capabilities that support the machine-learning lifecycle. 

- You’ll design scalable systems for model deployment and serving, feature computation, data validation, workflow orchestration, monitoring, and production support. 

- You’ll build reusable platform components, standards, and automation while improving reliability, scalability, observability, and operational readiness across ML systems. 

- You’ll partner with Data Science, Product, Risk, Fraud, and Engineering teams to translate ambiguous business needs into practical technical solutions. 

- You’ll own significant technical initiatives end to end and lead complex production investigations—clarifying requirements, leading design, delivering safely, measuring results, and implementing durable fixes. 

- You’ll raise engineering quality through thoughtful code and design reviews, mentor engineers through pairing and technical guidance, and contribute to platform technical strategy. 

- You’ll look for ways to use AI tools thoughtfully to work smarter, reduce manual work, and make better decisions faster. 

Who You Are 

The right fit looks like this 

You do not need detailed implementation direction to be effective. Given an ambiguous problem and sufficient context, you can define the technical approach, explain trade-offs, align stakeholders, lead delivery, and own the outcome after launch. 

You’re comfortable navigating complexity and don’t wait for perfect information to move forward. You communicate clearly, give direct feedback, mentor others, and connect engineering work to member, business, and operational outcomes. 

What You Bring 

Skills & experience 

- You’ll have 5+ years of professional software-engineering experience building and operating production systems, with strong programming skills in Python and deep knowledge of API design, distributed systems, service architecture, testing, and software-design fundamentals. 

- You’ve demonstrated experience designing and operating reliable, scalable cloud-native services or data-intensive systems, with experience in ML platforms, model serving, feature engineering, data platforms, MLOps, or related systems. 

- You bring practical experience with SQL, databases, caching, and tracing data or requests across multiple systems, plus familiarity with the ML lifecycle from feature engineering and model training through evaluation, deployment, serving, monitoring, and governance. 

- You have experience with Docker, Kubernetes, CI/CD, Git-based workflows, and production observability, and you can evaluate technical alternatives and clearly communicate recommendations, trade-offs, risks, and dependencies. 

- You’ve demonstrated the ability to mentor engineers, improve engineering practices, lead through technical influence, and connect engineering work to member, business, product, and operational outcomes. 

Nice to Have 

- Experience with AWS, Databricks, MLflow, SageMaker, Spark/PySpark, Kafka, or streaming systems. 

- Experience building feature platforms, model-serving systems, workflow-orchestration platforms, or internal developer platforms. 

- Familiarity with monitoring model quality, data quality, feature coverage, latency, reliability, or cost efficiency, and experience working with sensitive data in a regulated or financial-services environment. 

- Experience with Java or another backend language in addition to Python, and familiarity with AI tools such as ChatGPT or Copilot to improve personal productivity. 

Our AI Mindset 

We b uild with AI. We lead with judgment. 

AI isn't a feature here. It's how we work. 

We're excited about what AI makes possible, and we're looking for people who share that curiosity. You don't need to be an expert. You need to be open to experimenting , willing to learn, and able to apply new tools in ways that actually move the needle. 

In this role, you'll be encouraged to explore AI tools, find practical use cases for your function, and bring ideas for working smarter. We believe the best outcomes come when human judgment and AI capability work together . 

Why Oportun 

What's in it for you 

Oportun offers a competitive compensation and benefits package designed to support your physical, financial, and professional well-being. Benefits vary by country of employment. 

Some of the benefits available to eligible employees include: 

India Benefits: 

Medical, Dental & Vision Insurance 

Provident Fund 

Life & Accident Insurance 

Internet, Fuel, Meal & Telephone Allowances 

Eligibility and plan details vary by location and employment status. To learn more about Oportun and our benefits, visit oportun.com/careers #LI-REMOTE #LI-SS1 

We are proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer and consider all qualified applicants for employment opportunities without regard to race, age, color, religion, gender, national origin, disability, sexual orientation, veteran status or any other category protected by the laws or regulations in the locations where we operate. 

California applicants can find a copy of Oportun's CCPA Notice here: https://oportun.com/privacy/california-privacy-notice/ . 

We will never request personal identifiable information (bank, credit card, etc.) before you are hired. We do not charge you for pre-employment fees such as background checks, training, or equipment. If you think you have been a victim of fraud by someone posing as us, please report your experience to the FBI’s Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3).

title: Backend Engineer, Knowledge Graph

More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

As an Intermediate Backend Engineer on the GitLab Orbit team, you'll help build and operate a graph data service that supports GitLab Duo agents, analytics, and architecture-level features across GitLab.com, Dedicated, and Self-Managed deployments. You'll join a Rust-first team that values clear ownership, thoughtful system design, and rigorous thinking about data and reliability.

The Knowledge Graph service is a Rust backend that builds a property graph from GitLab’s software development lifecycle (SDLC) and code data. In your first year, you’ll take clear ownership of specific components or features (for example, parts of the SDLC indexing pipeline or query paths). You’ll help reduce single points of failure with better tests and runbooks, and you’ll help the team ship analytical services that are easier to maintain and evolve over time.

What you’ll do 

- Implement and iterate on backend features in the Rust-based Knowledge Graph service, including changes to the query engine, SDLC and code indexing flows, and API endpoints (including MCP endpoints) under guidance from senior and staff engineers.

- Maintain integrations between Knowledge Graph and the rest of the GitLab platform, working in areas that touch GitLab Rails, the Data Insights Platform (Siphon, NATS, ClickHouse), and GitLab Duo Agent Platform.

- Contribute to system design discussions by proposing options, raising questions, and documenting decisions, with a focus on reliability, scalability, and maintainability for analytical graph workloads.

- Improve the operational maturity of the service by adding or enhancing metrics, logging, runbooks, alerts, and small readiness tasks, and by participating in on-call rotation as appropriate for your level and experience.

- Collaborate asynchronously with product, data, infrastructure, security, and AI counterparts to clarify requirements, align on scope, and ship features safely for customers and sustainably for the team.

- Use AI-assisted development workflows responsibly (for example, using Knowledge Graph-backed agents and internal Duo tooling), and share what works with the team while keeping a strong focus on code quality and correctness.

- Participate in code reviews, knowledge-sharing sessions, and pairing to both learn from others and help maintain consistent standards across the codebase.

- Contribute across the stack when needed, including occasional Ruby work for Rails integration and authorization paths, or small frontend changes related to Knowledge Graph features (for example, Software Architecture Map UI plumbing).

What you’ll bring

- Proficiency in at least one modern backend language and strong interest in Rust, with either prior Rust experience or clear evidence you can ramp quickly and deliver in a Rust-first, performance-sensitive codebase.

- Some exposure to distributed data or analytics systems (for example, OLAP databases, Kafka- or NATS-style messaging, or change data capture (CDC) pipelines), or strong motivation to develop those skills in this role.

- Interest in graph data modeling and query patterns (property graphs, multi-step (n-hop) traversals, aggregations), and willingness to learn the tools and concepts used in Knowledge Graph over time.

- Practical experience (or strong interest) using AI tools in day-to-day development, along with a thoughtful approach to validating outputs and integrating AI into your workflow.

- A language-agnostic mindset and evidence that you can pick up new languages and frameworks as needed (for example, Ruby, Go, or TypeScript/Vue where the work touches adjacent systems).

- Solid fundamentals in system design for your level, including the ability to reason about trade-offs, ask good questions, and align your implementation work with documented architectural decisions.

- Comfort working in a low-process, high-ownership environment where you take responsibility for your work, refine problem statements with teammates, and communicate progress clearly in writing across time zones in an all-remote team.

About the team 

GitLab Orbit sits within the Data Engineering organization. We work closely with partners across AI (Duo Agent Platform), analytics, infrastructure and delivery, and security because our work spans many parts of the platform.

Grade level and salary ranges are determined through interviews and a review of education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities of the applicant, equity with other team members, alignment with market data, and geographic location. title: Principal Enterprise Architect
description:
Headquarters: India (remote)

Enterprise Architect - Cloud & AI 

Role Overview 

Jumio is not just processing transactions; we are pioneering the future of identity intelligence. To lead this transformation, you serve as a visionary AI Adoption Catalyst and Systems Architect , redefining our technical landscape. In this role, you aren’t a traditional gatekeeper—you are a Developer Advocate and mission-driven leader. You take end-to-end ownership of our architecture, positioning machine learning and GenAI at the heart of our DNA. Leveraging your deep expertise in AWS and cloud-native engineering, you provide the engine that empowers our developers to innovate at lightning speed, ensuring our multi-tenant SaaS platform remains the global benchmark for performance and scale.

This is a mandate for a technical doer who thrives on the front lines. Building on our strong, scalable cloud foundation, you will actively champion the adoption of GenAI tools across the software development lifecycle while driving continuous architectural improvement, evolution, and operational cost optimization. Your proven experience in AWS is the toolkit you use to clear architectural roadblocks and optimize performance, enabling engineering teams to move with unprecedented velocity.

As a strategic technical leader who stays close to the code, you inspire an AI-First culture. You bridge the gap between visionary enterprise design and pragmatic execution, driving cross-departmental impact while fostering self-service capabilities and cloud efficiency to ensure that as Jumio grows, our technology scales predictably and elegantly.

Key Responsibilities 

End-to-End System Architecture & Optimization 

- Own the technical vision for scalable, high-performance, cost-efficient systems.

- Define modern architecture patterns that enable growth, high TPS, and seamless scaling.

- Architect and optimize multi-tenant SaaS platforms, ensuring configurability and performance.

- Design self-service capabilities to reduce engineering overhead (e.g., self-service workflow designer, self-service rules engine, self-service reporting).

- Lead cloud cost efficiency initiatives, optimizing infrastructure, model execution, and compute resources.

- Collaborate closely with AWS Support and Solution Architects to optimize infrastructure and leverage cutting-edge cloud capabilities.

Data & AI Infrastructure 

- Architect high-scale, distributed data processing pipelines for batch and real-time workloads.

- Optimize data storage, retrieval, and processing layers to enhance system performance and reduce cost.

- Enable data self-service for analytics, ML, and real-time business use cases.

- Ensure data governance, security, and compliance across all systems.

Technical Leadership & Hands-on Architecture 

- Guide engineering teams on architectural best practices and pragmatic execution.

- Coach teams on scalable microservices, event-driven architectures, and cloud-native patterns.

- Practice "Architecting by Example" through technical prototyping and proof-of-concepts to validate architectural decisions.

GenAI Acceleration & Architectural Advocacy 

- You serve as the AI Adoption Catalyst and engineering champion, actively partnering with developers and business units to integrate LLMs and agentic workflows that securely hyper-automate the development lifecycle.

- You clear roadblocks and deploy agile architectural guardrails that empower teams to experiment rapidly with automated AI tools, building a self-service AI culture while maintaining rigorous cost-performance optimization.

- Your leadership evolves architectural governance into a collaborative platform for ensuring system-wide coherence, security, and world-class scalability.

Architectural Governance & ARC Leadership 

- Lead the Jumio Architecture Review Council (ARC) to drive cross-functional alignment and the evolution of our technical landscape.

- Establish and enforce architectural standards, ensuring consistency, security, and scalability across all product teams.

- Facilitate cross-team architectural reviews to identify technical debt, drive alignment, and ensure strategic coherence.

- Serve as the primary decision-maker for complex architectural trade-offs, balancing immediate delivery needs with long-term system health.

- Mentor engineering leadership on architectural best practices and standardized decision-making processes.

Who You Are 

- Strategic Visionary—you connect long-term business goals with robust technical roadmaps.

- Ultra-technical—you design, build, and optimize systems with a hands-on approach.

- System-First Thinker—you prioritize architecture, efficiency, and scale in every decision.

- Cloud-Native Expert—you utilize your deep AWS knowledge to optimize costs while improving system performance.

- Pragmatic Decision Maker—your impact-driven solutions ensure technical excellence without sacrificing speed.

- Builder’s Mentality—you thrive on automation, self-service, and reducing engineering toil through GenAI adoption.

- Growth-Oriented Mentor—you teach, coach, and elevate the engineering teams through architectural advocacy.

Must-Have Skills & Experience 

- 12+ years of hands-on experience in system architecture, data engineering, cloud engineering, or technical leadership roles.

- Experience with multi-tenant architectures and designing frameworks for configurable SaaS platforms.

- Deep, hands-on expertise in AWS (e.g., EKS, IAM, Lambda, networking) is required; professional experience with GCP is a strong plus.

- Strong experience with distributed systems, microservices, event-driven architectures, and caching strategies.

- Hands-on knowledge of AI/ML model execution—understanding model inference performance, cost trade-offs, and optimization strategies.

- Proficiency in high-scale transactional systems.

- Experience with infrastructure automation (Terraform, CI/CD, Kubernetes, Docker).

- Strong coding skills (Expert in Java, Strong in Python, Knowledgeable in JavaScript/TypeScript & Kotlin).

- Strong experience leading architectural review processes and fostering engineering standards.

- Proven expertise in integrating GenAI and ML methodologies into the software development lifecycle.

- Proven ability in strategic stakeholder management and complex financial/TCO (Total Cost of Ownership) analysis for enterprise technology.

Nice-to-Have Skills 

- Experience with high-volume, real-time data processing and distributed streaming architectures.

- Experience building petabyte-scale distributed data platforms.

- Familiarity with fraud prevention, identity verification, or authentication technologies.

Why Join Us? 

- Impact at scale —we process millions of transactions and solve real-world security and identity challenges .

- Modern technical foundation with room to innovate —leverage our established, scalable cloud architecture while actively driving continuous modernization, operational cost optimization, and solving complex technical challenges.

- Hands-on architecture leadership —you won’t be stuck in meetings; you’ll drive execution.

- Work alongside top engineers and AI/ML experts , pushing the limits of what’s possible.

- Competitive compensation and high ownership —your work will define how Jumio scales.

Jumio Values: 

IDEAL: Integrity, Diversity, Empowerment, Accountability, Leading Innovation 

Equal Opportunities : 

Jumio is a collaboration of people with different ideas, strengths, interests and cultures. We welcome applications and colleagues from all backgrounds and of all statuses. 

About Jumio: 

Jumio is a B2B technology company dedicated to eradicating online identity fraud, money laundering and other financial crimes to help make the internet safer. We leverage AI, biometrics, machine learning, liveness detection and automation to create solutions that are trusted by leading brands worldwide and respected by industry thought leaders. 

Jumio is the leading provider of online identity verification, eKYC and AML solutions. With a global footprint, we’re expanding the team to meet strong client demand across a range of industries including Financial Services, Travel, Sharing Economy, Fintech, Gaming, and others.
