title: Backend / Platform Developer Consultant (Temporal & Kubernetes)
description:
Headquarters: United States

URL: https://bitovi.com 

JOIN OUR TEAM!

Bitovi is looking for a Backend / Platform Developer Consultant to join us as we transform technology delivery. We build and operate durable, distributed systems for enterprise clients — heavy on Java Services, Temporal for workflow orchestration, Kafka for event streaming, and Kubernetes-native platform engineering on AWS to run it all reliably. If you want to build exceptional systems, take orchestration, systems engineering, and infrastructure seriously, and have ideas for making delivery more collaborative, validation-driven, and swift, we want to work with you!

Compensation: $120,000 to $190,000 annually, depending on experience, plus annual bonus opportunity.

PLEASE NOTE: At this time, we are only considering candidates located in and authorized to work in the United States. 

WHO YOU ARE

You're experienced building and running applications at the enterprise level, and you're comfortable owning both the code and the infrastructure it runs on. You think like a systems engineer — reasoning about the whole platform, from JVM services and event streams to the clusters and cloud infrastructure underneath them. You thrive when given opportunities to deliver real-world platforms as an integral team member, including large-scale migrations, and you have the expertise to interface and communicate confidently with stakeholders.

You'll excel in this role at Bitovi if you have:

- Strong working knowledge of Java and the JVM ecosystem (Spring Boot or similar); experience with additional backend languages (Go, Python, TypeScript/JavaScript, C#, etc.) is a plus

- Hands-on experience with a durable execution / workflow engine — Temporal preferred (Apache Airflow, Prefect, or similar also relevant) — including modeling workflows and activities, handling retries and timeouts, and reasoning about idempotency and failure modes

- Experience designing and operating Kafka-based event streaming systems: topic and partition design, consumer groups, schema management, and reasoning about ordering, delivery guarantees, and consumer lag

- Experience designing and building GraphQL APIs — schema design, resolvers, and performance concerns (N+1, caching, pagination); federation experience a plus

- Deep, hands-on AWS experience: architecting, deploying, and operating production systems (EKS, networking, IAM, messaging, and data services)

- Solid Kubernetes experience: deploying, operating, and debugging production workloads

- A systems engineering mindset: understanding of complex scaling issues, concurrency, backpressure, caching strategies, and failure modes across distributed systems

- Experience planning and executing migrations — application replatforming, workflow engine migrations, data/schema migrations, or moving workloads between environments with minimal downtime

- A thorough understanding of CI/CD pipelines and GitOps-style delivery

- Experience with observability in practice — logging, metrics, and tracing (OpenTelemetry a plus)

- Experience building modern microservice-based or serverless applications

- Database schema design and development expertise

Other skills we value

Temporal depth

- Running Temporal in production — self-hosted on Kubernetes and/or Temporal Cloud

- Workflow versioning and patching, safe deployments, and long-running workflow migrations

- Worker deployment and tuning (pollers, task queues, concurrency/slot configuration)

- Namespace management, mTLS (SPIFFE/SPIRE or private CA), and capacity/scaling concerns (e.g. APS/TRU on Temporal Cloud

Kafka & event streaming depth

- Operating Kafka in production (MSK, Confluent, or self-managed on Kubernetes)

- Kafka Connect, Kafka Streams, and schema registry workflows (Avro/Protobuf)

- Migrating between clusters or providers, and integrating Kafka with downstream analytical stores

- Experience with different techniques for processing large datasets, such as Lambda and Kappa architectures

Platform / DevOps depth

- Building or operating an internal developer platform (IDP) — self-service, paved-path infrastructure for application teams

- GitOps with ArgoCD (or Flux) and a low- or zero-manual-apply delivery model

- Infrastructure as code: Terraform/OpenTofu, and provisioning AWS resources via Crossplane, ACK, or similar

- Writing Kubernetes controllers/operators (controller-runtime, kubebuilder) and working with CRDs

- Helm chart authoring and distribution (including OCI/registry-based)

- Secrets management (External Secrets Operator, etc.), autoscaling (Karpenter, KEDA), and service mesh concepts (Istio, SPIFFE/SPIRE)

- EKS or comparable managed Kubernetes at scale

General

- Interest in working across multiple backend languages

- Additional queueing and messaging technologies (AWS SQS/SNS, RabbitMQ)

- API design across paradigms (GraphQL, REST, gRPC)

- AuthN/AuthZ and related technologies (sessions, API tokens, JWTs)

- Automated testing across the stack (unit, integration, performance/benchmarking)

WHO WE ARE

Bitovi partners with companies to build outcome-focused apps and platforms. Our collaborative approach is driven by validation to deliver the swiftest route to the most valuable solution.

We design and build high-profile applications and the infrastructure behind them — with tests, full docs, and a real deployment process. We run a serious Temporal practice (including large-scale migration and security work for enterprise clients) alongside deep Kubernetes, AWS, and platform engineering work. We discuss and design architectures, review code, and research new technologies. We talk to our clients, guiding them through the process, identifying potential problems and unknowns, and tackling challenges.

We help one another freely. We keep a Slack channel called ask-help, which is constantly used. We develop new skills, build better developer tools, and work on new types of projects regularly.

Our fully remote team comprises about 70 developers and designers. We welcome diversity and non-traditional paths into professions — we want the right person, not the right collection of tech keywords.

WHAT YOU'LL DO AT BITOVI

Build durable systems. Design and implement Java services, Temporal workflows, and Kafka-based event pipelines, and help clients adopt durable execution and event streaming the right way — from first workflow to production scale.

Lead modernization efforts. Plan and execute large-scale modernization efforts — moving workflows, services, and data between platforms, clusters, and clouds — with safety, observability, and minimal disruption as first-class requirements.

Own the platform. Build and operate Kubernetes-native infrastructure and CI/CD on AWS so application teams can ship safely and quickly. Treat reliability, observability, and repeatability as part of the deliverable, not an afterthought.

Consult and manage. Consult with clients to build outcome-driven applications and platforms, guiding them through the process, identifying potential problems and unknowns, and tackling challenges.

Travel. This is a remote, full-time position that requires the ability to travel. We travel an average of 3–5 days every quarter, and we'll always do our best to work with your schedule.

Teach. We'll discuss opportunities for you to present at conferences, attend and give training, plan and run meetups or local groups, and create various kinds of content in your area of expertise.

BENEFITS WE OFFER

- Competitive salary and annual bonus opportunity

- Completely remote work with flexible hours

- 401(k) matching

- 4 weeks of paid time off in addition to 8 paid holidays

- Health, dental, and vision insurance offerings

- Paid maternity and paternity leave

- STD, LTD, and Life Insurance coverage

HOW TO APPLY 

Please share a resume or LinkedIn profile and answer the additional questions via the application link. 

OTHER 

Please note that we are not interested in working with recruiters. 

ID Verification required if invited to an interview.

All job offers are contingent on passing a background check. 

Candidates must be located in and authorized to work in the United States; we are unable to provide visa sponsorship at this time.

ABOUT THE COMPANY: 

Salesloft is building the next era of enterprise revenue — one where teams make confident decisions powered by AI and real signals. By combining our scale, insights, and AI innovation, we're building the industry's first Predictive Revenue System, enabling humans and AI to work together to make smarter decisions and drive consistent growth.

With thousands of customers using our platforms every day, we have an unmatched view into how revenue is actually won — the Revenue Context that reveals what happens, when, and with what outcome. This gives us a unique opportunity to transform an entire category and set a new benchmark for how modern revenue teams operate.

Join us to help transform how companies around the world run revenue — and build the platform that will guide leading revenue teams into the future.

THE OPPORTUNITY: 

At Salesloft, as our HR Enablement Lead, you will be a pivotal member of our high-performing People team. Reporting to [manager, confirm], you will own the creation of learning programs and lead high-impact enablement workshops from beginning to end, and you will help build a cohesive, seamless learning journey for our global workforce. You'll have designated programs that you own end to end, from conception through execution, with hands-on support from leadership as the team builds out its capabilities together.

You'll work closely with our People Business Partners, our Associate People Business Partner, and an L&D coordinator who supports the learning platform and content production. Together you will ramp front-line managers faster, equip the People team with the playbooks and training it needs, and make learning part of how the business runs. This role moves beyond administrative operations to focus on strategic partnership and the integration of AI to empower our people.

On a day-to-day basis, you will:

- Own program lifecycles. Oversee end-to-end program lifecycles, including planning, development, delivery, and assessment.

- Create and lead workshops. Design and facilitate creative, robust enablement workshops and learning solutions for employees at all levels.

- Partner with People Business Partners. Work directly with People Business Partners to identify and align on specific talent gaps, and build solutions that fit what each business needs.

- Ramp front-line managers. Build and run manager and leadership programs, working with the PBPs, so new and developing managers can coach, handle performance conversations, and lead with confidence.

- Own onboarding and new-hire enablement. Create a consistent, practical onboarding experience that gets new employees productive faster.

- Enable the People team. Build playbooks, training and job aids for PBPs and Shared Services on topics such as calibration, employee relations and change management.

- Shape the learning architecture. Help architect a system of learning that is cohesive and provides a seamless journey for employees at all levels.

- Innovate with AI. Experiment with and implement AI-powered tools to automate workflows, personalize curriculum creation, and continuously invest in AI for workforce enablement.

- Drive business execution. Develop tailored strategies to address performance gaps, with clear objectives, development plans, and accountability measures, and make sure all programming aligns with near-term and long-term goals.

- Run the learning platform. Own the LMS and content library, working with the L&D coordinator on administration, scheduling and production.

- Analyze and interpret. Use data to identify trends, monitor program completions and impact, and provide actionable insights that inform future learning strategy.

We are seeking a strategic, results-driven partner who moves beyond operations to become a true consultant to the business. You are someone who understands how individual success drives company-wide goals and can build robust learning solutions that reflect the pragmatic needs of a fast-growing organization. You are comfortable embedding with the business and the People team. You build as well as plan: you ship programs, not just roadmaps, and you are equally at home designing a strategy and running the session. You care about proving that what you build works.

- 5+ years of combined experience in learning and development, enablement, organizational development, HR, or a related field, ideally in a technology-driven environment.

- Workshop facilitation: Proven ability to lead engaging enablement workshops across a variety of formats (live, in-person, or remote).

- Manager and onboarding programs: Experience designing and delivering manager development and onboarding programs.

- Instructional innovation: Proven ability to experiment with emerging learning technologies, creative modalities, and unconventional approaches that push beyond traditional training while applying adult learning principles.

- Strategic partnership: Skilled at building trust and credibility with senior leaders and cross-functional stakeholders.

- AI and technical aptitude: Experience leveraging AI to automate workflows, analyze insights, or create curriculum; aptitude for maintaining learning technology systems.

- Systems thinking: Strong business acumen to understand how learning initiatives impact the broader organization and culture.

- Program ownership: Strong project management skills with a demonstrated ability to work independently to see a program from concept to delivery.

- Hands-on execution: A track record of shipping programs and learning assets on a deadline, from design through delivery.

- Communication and influence: Effective communication skills to present findings and influence diverse audiences across many company levels.

Our programs are created and delivered by educators and industry practitioners, giving learners access to professional experts, real world challenges, and practical skills. You'll be one of two developers on the team, working directly with our lead developer. - Build and maintain custom WordPress themes across both of our stacks: modern block-based builds (ACF Blocks, core blocks, block patterns, theme.json) and established classic themes built on PHP templates, Advanced Custom Fields, and Sass.

- Collaborate with our lead developer to shape the team's coding standards, tooling, and workflow, and help migrate our existing sites toward our new modern stack.

- Stay current on emerging web standards and bring ideas to the table where they genuinely fit.

What You Bring 

- 4+ years of front-end web development experience, with strong skills in semantic HTML, CSS, JavaScript, PHP, and WordPress.

- The ability to build a custom WordPress theme from scratch using PHP templates and Advanced Custom Fields.

- Strong CSS skills across Sass and modern native CSS (custom properties, nesting), and solid vanilla JavaScript.

- Comfort working in Git/GitHub with pull requests and code reviews, and with npm-based build tools and the command line.

- A habit of writing semantic, well-structured HTML that covers accessibility basics, with an eye for reuse, cross-browser compatibility, performance, and SEO.

- Experience building and testing HTML emails.

- Strong UX/UI sensibilities and a desire to sweat the small stuff.

- A proactive, self-directed working style – you can run with a project independently and prioritize across several at once.

AI-assisted development is a new and evolving part of our workflow. We use AI coding tools to speed up research, scaffolding, review, and routine work, and you're welcome to do the same.

AI is a tool here, not a substitute for expertise. - You’ll help evolve engineering tools, platforms, and practices and encourage adoption of better ways of working. 

- You’ll look for practical ways to use AI tools to improve engineering productivity, analysis, documentation, and problem-solving. 

Who You Are

You’re a hands-on data engineer who enjoys solving complex technical problems and building systems that others depend on. You combine strong technical depth with a practical understanding of business needs and know how to turn ambiguous requirements into scalable solutions. 

You take ownership, communicate clearly, and are comfortable leading technical work without relying on formal authority. You enjoy mentoring others and helping teams make stronger technical decisions.

- Experience implementing data governance, data quality, or observability frameworks.

- Experience leading cross-functional or multi-month engineering initiatives.

We build with AI. We lead with judgment.

title: Senior Staff Data Scientist
description:
Headquarters: Remote

About the Team: 

Netlify’s Data team helps the company understand and improve the full product-led growth journey, from activation and engagement through conversion, retention, and monetization. We partner closely with Product, Engineering, and Growth to uncover opportunities, evaluate investments, and understand what drives customer and business outcomes.

We’re hiring a Senior Staff Data Scientist to deepen how data shapes our product and growth strategy. You’ll develop an end-to-end understanding of the PLG journey, proactively identify opportunities, and turn complex data into hypotheses, experiments, and recommendations that influence where we invest and what we build. This is a highly autonomous role for someone who can move from identifying an important question to shaping the approach, defining success, and driving toward an answer.

What You'll Do: 

- Own the analytical understanding of Netlify’s PLG performance across activation, engagement, conversion, monetization, and retention, identifying opportunities before they become requests

- Partner with Product and Engineering leadership to turn behavioral insights into product bets, defining what to test, how to measure it, and what the results mean

- Lead experimentation from hypothesis through decision, including study design, methodology, success metrics, guardrails, analysis, and recommendations

- Apply statistical rigor where it matters while recognizing when there is enough signal to make a decision and move forward, and help teams develop that same judgment

- Build scalable analytical systems like semantic models, trusted metrics, proactive monitoring, and AI-powered agents that surface opportunities without waiting to be asked

- Use AI to investigate faster, automate recurring analytical work, and test more hypotheses without sacrificing the judgment that makes the output useful

- Identify gaps in measurement, event instrumentation, and metric definitions, and partner with Data and Product Engineering to close them

- Serve as a trusted analytical partner to PLG leadership, using evidence and product judgment to influence investment decisions and roadmap priorities

- Influence product strategy through evidence, product instincts, and a clear point of view, without relying on formal authority to do it

What You'll Bring: 

- 8+ years of experience in product analytics, growth analytics, or data science, with a track record of high ownership and measurable impact on PLG or consumer product outcomes

- Deep understanding of product and growth dynamics across activation, engagement, conversion, monetization, and retention

- Demonstrated ability to turn behavioral data into product hypotheses and carry them from insight through experimentation and measured outcomes

- Deep experimentation expertise: study design, statistical reasoning, causal inference, and the judgment to know when an experiment has told you what you need to know

- Experience building analytical systems such as metrics layers, monitoring frameworks, or semantic models that teams can rely on over time

- An AI-native approach to analysis: you use AI tools actively to accelerate investigation, automate repetitive work, and surface patterns faster

- A track record of influencing senior stakeholders and product direction through analytical reasoning, clear recommendations, and sound judgment

- Comfort operating with significant autonomy in ambiguous problem spaces, including determining which questions are most important to answer

- Strong written and verbal communication skills in distributed environments, with the ability to make complex findings clear and recommendations actionable

This Role is a Great Fit If: 

- You're energized by finding the opportunity before anyone thought to ask - proactive discovery is how you naturally work, not a mode you shift into

- You think like a product person who happens to be exceptionally rigorous with data, not a data person who occasionally weighs in on product

- You thrive when the problem isn't handed to you - you'd rather define the question worth asking than answer the one that landed in your queue

- You get excited about building systems that keep working after you've moved on to the next problem

- You're comfortable making a call with imperfect information and can articulate clearly why you made it

- You enjoy being a thought partner to senior leaders - shaping how they think about investment and opportunity, not just supporting decisions already made

- You work well in a remote-first, async environment where written clarity and self-direction matter more than proximity

- You're drawn to roles where the measure of success is outcomes, decisions made, bets tested, metrics moved, not volume of output produced

Applying 

Not sure you meet 100% of our qualifications? Please apply anyway! 

When applying please include: 

A resume or short listing of your job history & skills (link to a LinkedIn profile would be fine). We appreciate a cover letter explaining why you would enjoy working in this role at Netlify to get to know you a bit better, though this is not required and will not impact your application. Our mission is to “build a better web” and that cannot be done without a diversity of skill sets, backgrounds and thoughts. 

Of everything we've ever built at Netlify, we are most proud of our team. Netlify is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are devoted to building a team of people with diverse backgrounds and lifestyles. Driving equality empowers our team, enables us to innovate, and helps us maintain a more inclusive environment. We don’t discriminate against employees or applicants based on gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, religion, age, race, military/veteran status, citizenship, pregnancy status, or any other differences. If we can do anything to provide a better interview, i.e. accommodate a disability, then please let us know by emailing accommodations@netlify.com . 

About Netlify 

Netlify is the most popular way to build, deploy, and scale modern web applications, empowering everyone from fast moving solo developers to enterprise teams. Millions of developers and organizations rely on Netlify as their platform of choice for composing web applications that are production ready, performant, and flexible. Now, as we embrace the next era of software development, we are embedding the same fluid, intuitive experience into the Agent Experience (AX), making it just as simple for intelligent agents to understand, interact with, and act on our platform as it is for developers. Whether your user is human or machine, Netlify ensures the path from idea to URL is seamless, fast, and deeply reliable.

We are a Series D company that has raised over $200M from investors such as Andreessen Horowitz, Kleiner Perkins, EQT, Bessemer, BOND, and Menlo Ventures. As a fully distributed company, we aim to create a company culture where the best idea can come from anywhere and strive to be thoughtful, compassionate, and collaborative in our work. title: Business Continuity Management Lead
description:
Headquarters: San Francisco, CA, New York, NY, Portland, OR, or Remote within Canada or United States

About the Role 

Mercury is seeking a Business Continuity Management (BCM) Lead to build and lead an enterprise-wide continuity program as we prepare to become a bank. As part of the Risk team, this leader will establish practical standards, clear accountability, and tested capabilities to maintain critical services and recover effectively from disruptions, with direct visibility to the CRO and senior leadership.

This role fills the need for a dedicated leader to coordinate BCM across the organization. The ideal candidate combines deep continuity and resilience expertise with the judgment to build a proportionate program in a fast-moving environment, working effectively with Engineering, Operations, Product, Information Security, Legal, Compliance, and business teams.

The BCM Lead will own the enterprise framework, coordination, oversight, and reporting. Business and technology owners will remain accountable for their continuity plans and recovery execution.Because this is a new program, the Lead will be hands-on in the initial build: facilitating the first round of BIAs and plans side by side with owners, running exercises, and driving identified gaps through remediation. This leader will also work closely with Engineering on technology disaster recovery and with relevant teams on incident response, crisis management, and third-party resilience.

Key Responsibilities 

- Develop and implement Mercury’s enterprise BCM framework, policies, standards, governance, and operating model, with a prioritized implementation roadmap aligned to bank-launch readiness and critical services.

- Partner with business owners to identify critical services, conduct business impact analyses (customer, financial, operational, and regulatory), and map dependencies across people, processes, technology, facilities, and third parties, including single points of failure.

- Establish recovery time objectives (RTOs) and recovery point objectives (RPOs), where applicable, with business and technology owners; challenge gaps between objectives and recovery capabilities.

- Set standards for continuity plans and recovery procedures, and facilitate and support accountable owners in developing actionable plans and alternative operating arrangements.

- Coordinate business continuity with technology disaster recovery, incident response, and crisis management, with clear activation criteria, escalation paths, and communications responsibilities.

- Design and lead a risk-based exercise program, from tabletop simulations to end-to-end recovery tests, and drive lessons learned, remediation tracking, and verification that gaps are closed.

- Partner with Third-Party Risk Management and vendor owners to assess critical provider recovery capabilities, contingency arrangements, and concentration dependencies.

- Embed continuity considerations into new products, material business changes, and technology implementations.

- Establish metrics and reporting that give management and relevant committees visibility into readiness, testing outcomes, material gaps, and overdue remediation.

- Build and lead a growing BCM team, including hiring and developing analysts as the program scales over the next year.

- Deliver role-based training and promote awareness of continuity responsibilities across the organization.

- Support regulatory examinations and bank-launch readiness reviews with accurate documentation and evidence of recovery capability.

Qualifications 

- 10+ years of experience in business continuity management, operational resilience, disaster recovery, or a related discipline within a fintech, financial institution, technology company, or other highly regulated environment.

- Demonstrated experience building or materially enhancing an enterprise BCM program, including governance, implementation, testing, and reporting.

- Strong skills in business impact analysis, critical-service identification, dependency mapping, and recovery objective development.

- Experience developing actionable continuity plans and leading exercises that test recovery assumptions and expose gaps.

- Sufficient technical fluency to work with Engineering on cloud services, system dependencies, data recovery, and technology disaster recovery.

- Working knowledge of third-party risk management, including assessing critical vendor recovery capabilities, contingency arrangements and concentration risk.

- Proven ability to drive cross-functional remediation through influence, with a clear view of where BCM oversight ends and business or technology ownership begins.

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain readiness gaps and tradeoffs to senior leadership.

- Experience managing a team of Business Continuity analysts.

Preferred Qualifications 

- Familiarity with banking supervisory expectations for business continuity, and operational resilience.

- Experience operating in a company-building or bank-building environment.

- Familiarity with recognized continuity standards, such as ISO 22301, and BCM tools for plan management, exercises, and issue tracking.

- Relevant professional certification, such as CBCP or MBCI.

Leadership Attributes 

- Pragmatic, first-principles builder who turns ambiguous needs into clear priorities and designs a program that fits Mercury’s operations and scale.

- Takes ownership and follows through from identified gaps to demonstrated recovery.

- Collaborative, low-ego, and effective across the three lines of defense.

- Calm under pressure and able to facilitate clear decisions during disruptions.

- Able to challenge constructively, distinguish material gaps from theoretical concerns, and avoid over-engineering.

*Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.

All individuals seeking employment at Mercury are considered without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex, marital status, ancestry, physical or mental disability, veteran status, gender identity, sexual orientation, or any other legally protected characteristic. title: Software Development Engineer II (Remote @ Colombia)
description:

About the role: 

The OfferUp Connect team builds the moments that turn a listing into a sale. Every chat between buyers and sellers, every offer notification, and every saved-search alert runs through services we own, from messaging and notifications to location, meetups, and the subscriptions sellers pay for. We run high-volume Java microservices and streaming pipelines, integrate with partners like Braze, Amazon Pinpoint, Apple, and Google, and use experimentation to decide what ships.

We also take on high-visibility work beyond our domain. Connect built OfferUp's video infrastructure for listing videos and LLM-powered catalog enrichment on Amazon Bedrock, both company priorities that changed what buyers see every day. The roadmap is wide open for someone who wants to help shape it.

As a Software Development Engineer II, you'll own features from concept to rollout: designing and writing well-tested code, launching experiments, and measuring results with Product, Design, and Data partners. You'll raise the quality of the code around you and get the chance to join the next project like video or catalog enrichment.

- Design, build, and deploy backend services and event-driven pipelines for messaging, notifications, location, and subscriptions

- Improve the reliability, latency, and delivery rates of high-volume messaging and notification systems, including retries, rate limiting, and frequency capping

- Integrate with and operate third-party platforms such as Braze, Amazon Pinpoint, Apple and Google push services, and app store billing

- Own features end-to-end: plan, design, develop, deploy, measure, and iterate

You’ll thrive in this role if you have: 

- 2+ years of professional software engineering experience

- Demonstrated ability to own the delivery of multiple features end-to-end (plan, design, develop, and deploy) with high efficiency, including breaking down engineering problems into achievable tasks

- Strong coding skills in Java, with a working understanding of microservices and distributed-systems fundamentals

- Good knowledge of data structures and object-oriented design

- Hands-on experience using AI coding tools (Claude Code or similar) in a real engineering workflow, and a point of view on when they help and when they don't

- A habit of following good coding patterns, writing appropriate tests, considering trade-offs, and seeking out edge cases

- Comfortable giving and receiving feedback in code reviews

- A bias toward shipping, learning from production, and iterating quickly

- An insatiable desire and ability to learn

- BS or MS in Computer Science, or equivalent practical experience

Helpful, but not required: 

- Fluency in another modern object-oriented programming language

- Experience with TypeScript and Node.js

- Experience with Agile development

- Experience building and integrating with REST APIs

- Experience with AWS services such as DynamoDB, SQS, SNS, Lambda, and ElastiCache (Redis)

- Experience with notification and engagement platforms (Braze, Amazon Pinpoint, APNs, FCM) or in-app subscription billing (App Store, Google Play)

- Experience with stream processing frameworks such as Apache Flink or Kafka Streams

- Experience with A/B testing platforms (Statsig, LaunchDarkly, Optimizely) and analytics warehouses (BigQuery, Snowflake)

- Experience consuming or integrating LLM-based APIs (e.g., Bedrock, Vertex AI, OpenAI)

- Familiarity with Kubernetes, Helm, and CI/CD pipelines

title: Director of Security Research, Cribl Detect
description:
Headquarters: Remote - Israel

Join the company that’s building the telemetry infrastructure for the AI era. At Cribl, we partner with IT and Security teams at many of the world’s biggest enterprises, including half of the Fortune 100, to bridge the gap between AI ambition and infrastructure reality. As the AI Platform for Telemetry, we give customers the choice, control, and flexibility to manage and analyze telemetry for both humans and agents, so they can build what’s next.

We’re one of the fastest‑growing private companies and a leading player in a massive, fast‑moving market. With a global workforce, we’re remote‑first and grounded in a simple idea: software is a people business. Cribl is the place where curious, collaborative people can do their best work, grow fast, and bring their full selves to the herd.

Why You’ll Love This Role 

Cribl Detect brings Cribl’s telemetry platform and security expertise together to help customers improve detection coverage, reduce alert noise, and speed investigations—while keeping the flexibility to use the tools they already have. As Director of Security Research, you’ll build and lead a research organization across detection engineering, threat hunting, and AI-driven triage and investigation. You’ll develop the team, set research priorities, and partner with Product and Engineering to shape Cribl Detect. You’ll also publish technical research and collaborate with Cribl’s internal SOC to strengthen Cribl’s defenses.

Based in Israel, this hybrid role works closely with teammates across Israel and the US, with regular overlap with US working hours and periodic travel to the US. The package includes competitive compensation and equity, pension and Keren Hishtalmut contributions subject to local policy, paid time off, a Cibus meal card, and professional development.

As An Active Member Of Our Team, You Will… 

- Build and lead the research organization: hire and develop researchers and research leaders, set shared standards, and align priorities with customer needs, emerging threats, and product goals.

- Own threat-informed detection content and effectiveness by turning threat intelligence into validated rules and hunt packs, maintaining coverage, fidelity, telemetry readiness, and rule health, and delivering timely threat advisories.

- Guide AI-driven investigations by defining how agents test hypotheses, gather evidence, distinguish malicious from legitimate activity, and escalate uncertainty; partner with Engineering to evaluate accuracy, completeness, and false-negative risk.

- Lead telemetry and security-tool research: define evidence needs and tool capabilities, study how telemetry collection and transformation affect security outcomes, and guide data requirements and integrations.

- Shape security methods and evaluation for additional AI-agent workflows, including MITRE mapping, noise tuning, and rule authoring.

- Build technical credibility through substantive publications, practitioner guides, presentations, and selected public tools, frameworks, or datasets.

- Partner with Cribl’s internal SOC on detections, threat hunts, investigation methods, and security validation; use operational feedback to improve research and product quality while respecting the SOC’s operational ownership.

- We are a remote-first company and work happens across many time-zones – you may be required to occasionally perform duties outside your standard working hours.

If You’ve Got It - We Want It 

- 10+ years in security research, detection engineering, threat hunting, or investigation, including 5+ years leading teams and a record of turning research into customer-facing content or product capabilities.

- Experience hiring and developing researchers, growing technical leaders, and building collaborative teams.

- Strong understanding of adversary behavior, MITRE ATT&CK, security telemetry, detection validation, and analyst workflows.

- Experience guiding AI agents across security workflows and evaluating output accuracy, security effectiveness, and appropriate human oversight.

- Practical knowledge of security tools, APIs, and data limitations, with the ability to review detection logic and investigative methods and validate ideas through queries, scripting, or prototypes.

- Strong cross-functional leadership and communication skills, including the ability to prioritize research and influence Product, Engineering, customers, and executives.

- Willingness to travel internationally, including to the US.

- Bonus: Experience spanning detection engineering and automated investigation, or developing investigative guidance or evaluation datasets for AI agents.

title: Architect
description:
Headquarters: Remote - US

Who we are 

At Twilio, we’re shaping the future of communications, all from the comfort of our homes. We deliver innovative solutions to hundreds of thousands of businesses and empower millions of developers worldwide to craft personalized customer experiences.

Our dedication to remote-first work , and strong culture of connection and global inclusion means that no matter your location, you’re part of a vibrant team with diverse experiences making a global impact each day. As we continue to revolutionize how the world interacts, we’re acquiring new skills and experiences that make work feel truly rewarding. Your career at Twilio is in your hands.
. 

Hiring and how we work 

We use Artificial Intelligence (AI) to help make our hiring process efficient. That said, every hiring decision is made by real Twilions! 

Also, while we are a remote-first company, you may be asked to report in person on an ad-hoc basis for team gatherings, functional off-sites or customer meetings.
. 

See yourself at Twilio 

Join the team as Twilio’s next Architect on our Data Substrate team

About the job 

Twilio runs on data, and the platform underneath it is entering a major shift. Open table formats, the convergence of lakes and warehouses, tightening privacy regulation, and AI workloads are all changing what a data platform has to do. We’re hiring an Architect to set our direction through that shift and to make sure the systems we build over the next 3-5 years are the right ones.

You’ll own the technical strategy for our data platform, spanning storage, lake and lakehouse architecture, catalog and governance, and privacy-by-design. You’ll work across org boundaries, setting standards that dozens of teams build on and raising the technical bar for the engineers around you.

Responsibilities 

In this role, you’ll:

- Own the architecture and multi-year technical strategy for the data platform, including the lake/lakehouse, ClickHouse, Elasticsearch, and governance, and keep them coherent as one platform rather than separate systems. Define where each engine fits (for example, ClickHouse versus open table formats on object storage) and the migration path between them.

- Make and document the major design decisions (ADRs, RFCs) on storage and open table formats, catalog strategy, compute engines, tenancy, data placement, and build-versus-adopt tradeoffs, with cost and performance at petabyte scale as explicit design constraints.

- Set the reference architectures for how our core storage and query engines (ClickHouse, Elasticsearch, and lake engines) are deployed, tuned, scaled and operated as shared platforms, including capacity, cost, tenant isolation, and upgrade strategy.

- Define the reliability model for the platform: availability targets, failure domains, disaster recovery, observability, and incident response patterns that teams can adopt.

- Build privacy and compliance into the architecture, not onto it. Design deletion and right-to-erasure, retention, data residency, and PII classification so they work across the platform’s storage layers, backups, and derived datasets, including data that arrives from upstream streaming systems.

- Drive data governance: classification, catalog and metadata, lineage, access control integrated with our authentication and authorization systems, data contracts, quality and integrity standards, and a catalog teams actually use.

- Review designs and technical direction across the org, and act as the escalation point on hard distributed-systems and performance problems.

- Mentor principal and senior engineers, and grow architectural judgment across the org, not only within one squad.

- Partner with product, security, infrastructure and consuming teams to turn business needs into platform roadmaps, and say no or re-sequence when the tradeoffs require it.

- Track emerging data technologies (such as streaming-first architectures, federated query, and AI-ready data layers) and bring forward the ones worth adopting, with evidence from prototypes or benchmarks.

Qualifications 

Twilio values diverse experiences from all kinds of industries, and we encourage everyone who meets the required qualifications to apply. If your career is just starting or hasn't followed a traditional path, don't let that stop you from considering Twilio. We are always looking for people who will bring something new to the table!

Required: 

- Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

- 15+ years of experience in software development or a related field, with at least 8 years in an architecture or senior technical leadership role.

- Proven track record of architecting and delivering large-scale data platforms and setting their technical strategy, on cloud infrastructure such as AWS, deployed with Kubernetes, Terraform and Helm.

- Deep expertise in storage and compute for analytical data: columnar and open table formats, lake and lakehouse architecture, partitioning, indexing, query planning, and how the choices affect cost and performance at petabyte scale.

- Breadth across data storage and retrieval technologies, with hands-on depth in at least two of: analytical/OLAP engines (e.g., ClickHouse), search engines (e.g., ElasticSearch/OpenSearch), and lake or distributed processing engines (e.g., Spark, Trino, Flink). You can reason about when to use each, how they interoperate, and how to migrate between them.

- Working knowledge of streaming systems (e.g., Kafka) and how they interact with downstream storage.

- Practical experience designing data governance at scale: data classification, catalog and metadata management, lineage, and access control integrated with authentication and authorization systems.

- Practical experience implementing privacy and compliance requirements (deletion, retention, residency) across a large, heterogeneous data estate.

- Proficiency in one or more of Python, Java, and Go.

- Track record of writing and driving architecture decisions across multiple teams, and of changing the direction of an organization’s technical roadmap through influence rather than authority.

- Experience elevating engineering standards and mentoring senior engineers across teams.

- Demonstrated commitment to operational excellence: architecting for high availability, observability and incident response in distributed systems, and being credible when a platform is failing in production.

- Strong written and verbal communication, including making a complex tradeoff clear to engineers and to senior leadership.

Desired: 

- Experience operating one of these engines (e.g., ClickHouse, ElasticSearch) at scale, including replication, sharding, ingestion behavior, and multi-tenant isolation.

- Experience with catalog and metadata systems (e.g., Unity Catalog, Glue, Polaris, DataHub) and open table format catalog strategy.

- Experience with a platform migration across domains or ownership models, such as moving from central to domain-owned data.

- A track record of measurable cost optimization on large data platforms.

- Networking and network security knowledge.

Location 

This role will be remote, and based in the United States. 

Travel 

We prioritize connection and opportunities to build relationships with our customers and each other. For this role, you may be required to travel occasionally to participate in project or team in-person meetings.

What We Offer 

Working at Twilio offers many benefits, including competitive pay, generous time off, ample parental and wellness leave, healthcare, a retirement savings program, and much more. Offerings vary by location 

Compensation 

*Please note this role is open to candidates outside of California, Colorado, Hawaii, Illinois, Maryland, Massachusetts, Minnesota, New Jersey, New York, Vermont, Washington D.C., and Washington State. The information below is provided for candidates hired in those locations only. 

The estimated pay ranges for this role are as follows:

- Based in New York, New Jersey, Washington State, or California (outside of the San Francisco Bay area): $224,400 - $280,500.

This role may be eligible to participate in Twilio’s equity plan and corporate bonus plan. All roles are generally eligible for the following benefits: health care insurance, 401(k) retirement account, paid sick time, paid personal time off, paid parental leave.

The successful candidate’s starting salary will be determined based on permissible, non-discriminatory factors such as skills, experience, and geographic location.

Application deadline information 

Applications for this role are intended to be accepted until 1/4/2027 but may change based on business needs. 

. 

Twilio thinks big. Do you? 

We like to solve problems, take initiative, pitch in when needed, and are always up for trying new things. That's why we seek out colleagues who embody our values — something we call Twilio Magic . Additionally, we empower employees to build positive change in their communities by supporting their volunteering and donation efforts.

So, if you're ready to unleash your full potential, do your best work, and be the best version of yourself, apply now! If this role isn't what you're looking for, please consider other open positions.

Stay alert to recruitment fraud 

We care about your safety. Scammers sometimes impersonate Twilio recruiters through fake job postings, emails, websites, or messages. Please ensure you are engaging with an official @ twilio.com email address. We will never ask for payment, gift cards, cryptocurrency, or banking information during the recruiting process. We do not make job offers without a formal interview process or conduct interviews exclusively through text-based messaging apps.

title: Staff Software Engineer, Delivery Engineering
description:
Headquarters: Remote, Canada (EST) OR Remote, US (EST) OR Remote, UK

About CircleCI Engineering

CI/CD has been solved. Now it's being reinvented. AI agents don't just run pipelines. They write code, trigger builds, interpret failures, and propose fixes. The interfaces that developers use to understand and trust that work don't exist yet. We're building them.

At CircleCI, our guiding principles aren't posters on a wall. We learn fast: we run experiments, accept failure, and scale what works. We think like the customer: every decision connects back to the developer sitting in front of a failing build at 2 am. We own the outcome: not just our slice of it, but the whole thing. If that's how you already work, you'll fit here.

About Delivery Engineering

Delivery Engineering enables CircleCI engineers to deliver quickly, confidently, and securely. We provide the tools and resources that make standard patterns and best practices simple to adopt, and we reduce toil.

Our current focus is the agentic software development lifecycle: how changes are found, planned, built, reviewed, merged, and measured as AI agents take on more of the work. We evaluate the harnesses, repository patterns, skills, and agentic tooling available, decide what our teams should standardize on, and build and support the shared tooling other teams depend on.

We're a small, very senior team, and everyone on it shapes where we go. Every improvement we make compounds across the organization.

What You'll Do

- Build AI-natively. AI is how we work. It's not a productivity layer on top of engineering, but the default starting point for how problems get approached and solved.

- Shape how CircleCI builds software with agents. Help define the end-to-end agentic SDLC, from identifying a change through planning, execution, pull request, merge, and measuring impact afterward. Evaluate shared tooling and patterns, and help decide what teams standardize on.

- Start from how our teams actually work. Spend time with engineering teams to understand their workflows and where they get stuck. Use what you learn to drive decisions and direction that teams adopt because the work fits how they operate.

- Build platforms, not one-offs. Build and support shared tooling that other teams depend on, and own its adoption as much as its delivery. A tool nobody uses isn't done.

- Measure what matters. Instrument agent usage and outcomes so we know what improves throughput and quality and what just burns tokens. Treat cost, model choice, and reliability as design concerns.

- Make build-vs-buy calls. Evaluate models, vendors, and open-source tools against our needs, and choose the path that gets engineers the most leverage.

- Lead through influence. Write the design docs, lead technical discussions across teams, and mentor engineers across the org as they adopt agentic workflows.

What You'll Bring

- Direct experience driving agentic developer experience efforts. You've driven an initiative that changed how an engineering organization builds software with AI agents. You can speak to what you built, how you measured its impact, how you drove adoption, and what didn't work.

- Hands-on depth with agentic tooling. You work daily with coding agents, agent harnesses, MCP, and skills or prompt design. You know how to evaluate agent output and reason about model and token economics.

- A platform mindset. You've built and supported internal platforms or developer tooling that other engineers build on and rely on, and driven their adoption.

- Backend depth in Go. You've owned production backend services in Go, including API design, data modeling, and service integration.

- A track record at staff scope. 8+ years of production engineering experience, including technical decisions that spanned multiple teams and accountability for whether they landed.

- Decision-making grounded in your users. You build direction by listening first. You turn the needs of many teams into clear tradeoffs, document your reasoning, and bring people along.

This role is open to candidates based in Europe or in the Eastern time zone.

Sound like you?

You've stopped waiting for AI to mature and are already building with it, not as a productivity trick, but as a core part of how you think about problems. You care about the engineers using your tools as much as the code behind them. You're drawn to work where the patterns don't exist yet and the best answer requires you to invent it with the people who'll use it. If that's how you already operate, we want to talk.

description:
Headquarters: United States - Remote

Tebra only initiates contact with candidates via email from an official Tebra email address (@ tebra.com , @ patientpop.com , or @ kareo.com ) or through our applicant tracking system, Greenhouse. We will only ask you to provide sensitive personal information through our official application portal — not via social media or text message. We do not conduct interviews via instant messaging.

About the Role

Tebra helps private practices bring modernized care to patients everywhere. To run our own business well, every team needs numbers it can trust.

We're looking for a Senior Analytics Engineer to help build Tebra's new internal analytics platform. You'll turn data from Salesforce, NetSuite, Stripe, our product, and other systems into one shared, tested set of business data and metrics that Finance, Customer Success, Growth, and Payments all use. You'll lead projects end to end, set the standards others build on, and partner with business leaders to define the metrics that matter most.

Your Area of Focus

- Data Modeling & Shared Datasets: Design, build, and maintain enterprise-wide business data that teams across Finance, Customer Success, Growth, and Payments build on. Apply dimensional modeling and layered design (staging, intermediate, and marts) so business logic lives in one place and isn't rebuilt by each team.

- Metric Definition & Semantic Layer: Partner with metric owners in Finance and the business to define each key metric once, with a named owner and documented logic. Publish governed metrics in a semantic layer that Tableau, AI assistants, and other tools query, and reconcile them to current reporting and the general ledger before teams switch over.

- Self-Service Enablement: Build easy-to-use datasets that let non-technical teammates and analysts answer their own questions without writing complex joins.

- Platform Migration: Lead projects end to end on the new internal analytics platform, from source data to dashboards. Move each team's reporting over one domain at a time, with clear cutover and rollback plans, and onboard the analysts who contribute to new conventions, review processes, and tools.

- Data Quality & Testing: Build automated tests and pull-request checks so data issues are caught before they reach reports. Monitor scheduled jobs, fix failures, and recover runs as part of shared production support.

- Performance & Efficiency: Tune SQL, models, and pipeline schedules so data refreshes on time and dashboards load in seconds. Monitor compute usage and cost, and choose how each model is built and refreshed to keep both in check.

- Forecasting & Machine Learning: Partner with analysts and data scientists to prepare clean, documented datasets for forecasting and machine learning models, such as retention and revenue projections.

- Code Review & Mentorship: Review code from analysts and engineers across teams, and coach them on modeling, SQL, and testing standards.

- Governance & Documentation: Follow data-sharing and privacy rules that keep protected health information (PHI) and personal data out of internal analytics. Maintain model documentation, lineage, and metric definitions via dbt, GitHub, Confluence, and Jira.

Your Professional Qualifications

- Experience: 5+ years of experience in analytics engineering, data engineering, or a similar role, with 2+ years hands-on in dbt in production.

- SQL Fluency: Expert SQL, including window functions, CTEs, and performance tuning for queries and pipelines on large datasets.

- Data Modeling: Deep proficiency in dimensional modeling (Kimball), including shared datasets that serve many teams.

- Tech Stack: Proven experience with Snowflake or a similar cloud data warehouse, and with dbt.

- Business Partnership: Experience defining business metrics with Finance or business stakeholders, and reconciling data to financial systems.

- Software Mindset: Experience with GitHub for version control and code review, automated builds (GitHub Actions or similar), and Jira and Confluence for work tracking and documentation.

- Communication: Strong communication with people who aren't data specialists, and ability to execute under minimal supervision.

- Growth Mindset: Motivated to learn new technologies and develop new skills.

- Education: Bachelor's degree in computer science, statistics, economics, information systems, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

- Semantic Layer: Experience with a semantic layer, such as Snowflake semantic views or the dbt Semantic Layer, preferred.

- Domain Knowledge: Experience with Salesforce, NetSuite, or Stripe data, and with subscription revenue, retention, or payments metrics, preferred.

- Forecasting & ML: Experience preparing data for forecasting or machine learning models preferred.

- Healthcare: Healthcare or HIPAA experience preferred.

- Additional Tools: Familiarity with Tableau, Terraform, or Okta a plus.

- Certifications: dbt Analytics Engineering or SnowPro certifications preferred.

As Fin becomes mission-critical for our most strategic customers, we’re growing our team of Forward Deployed Engineers to help bridge the gap between customer needs and product innovation. 

As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you’ll work hands-on with strategic customers, partnering closely with our R&D and Go-to-Market teams to design and deliver high-impact solutions. - Work hands-on with customers’ technical teams as a trusted technical expert, coding side-by-side to drive projects through to completion.

- Contribute to the evolution of Forward Deployed Engineering by codifying best practices and sharing insights from customer engagements to help the team scale and grow.

- Strong cross-functional collaboration skills, with the ability to navigate organisational boundaries and bring people together to achieve the best outcomes for our customers.

- Deep knowledge of at least one high-level programming language, such as JavaScript, Python or Ruby. It doesn’t need to be a language we use today - great people learn quickly and can introduce us to better ways of working.

- The ability to prototype and ship software quickly while maintaining a high bar for quality and a clear focus on business goals and outcomes.

- Strong communication skills. You can comfortably discuss the same topics with engineers and non-technical audiences, adapting the depth and detail as needed.

We have a radically open and accepting culture at Fin. We avoid spending time on divisive subjects to foster a safe and cohesive work environment for everyone. title: Solutions Engineer
description:
Headquarters: United States

URL: https://www.backblaze.com 

Solutions Engineer 

Backblaze (Nasdaq: BLZE) | Remote, US | AI and application storage Solutions Engineering | Reports to the Solutions Engineering Manager (the VP of Solutions Engineering until the manager is hired) | Works with Account Executives, Product, Support, and the Solutions Engineering team

Salary range: $128,000-$144,000 plus variable pay and RSUs.

How We Got Here 

We started by building storage servers from scratch in a Palo Alto apartment to save 90% on hardware. Turns out hard constraints make for pretty good engineering. That discipline forged a platform that performs as well or better than competitors, scales to multi-exabyte workloads, and costs a fraction of what AWS or Google charge. AI infrastructure runs on data. Storage gets hard at scale. We've been breaking, rebuilding, and improving that storage layer for 20 years.

Today, the world's leading AI infrastructure providers, neoclouds, and data-intensive businesses run on Backblaze. Our platform includes:

- B2 Overdrive - high-throughput object storage engineered for AI infrastructure, GPU workloads, and massive-scale data pipelines

- B2 Neo - white-label enterprise cloud storage powering neocloud platforms for AI, HPC, and media

- B2 Cloud Storage - S3-compatible object storage with predictable pricing, free egress, and no lock-in

- Computer Backup - automatic, continuous endpoint backup for Macs and PCs

500,000+ customers. 175 countries. Nasdaq: BLZE. backblaze.com

The Role 

Backblaze sells a technical product, so Solutions Engineers join the deal at the first discovery conversation, before it is qualified. You will partner with Account Executives to learn what a customer needs, run the proof of concept that shows Backblaze fits, and stay close after the deal closes. This role focuses on AI and application storage customers.

Nearly every customer is replacing something they already run. Your job is to show where Backblaze slots into what they have already built, not to design their stack from scratch. You will earn trust by being curious, hands-on, and straight with customers about what the test shows.

This is not a demo-and-handoff role. If your instinct is to open a terminal, test a customer's real workload, and write down what you find, keep reading.

What You Will Do 

- Join discovery early. Work with the AE from the first conversation to learn the customer's workload, success criteria, and timeline.

- Run proofs of concept. Define success with the customer, test Backblaze against what they run today, and report results plainly, including ones they didn't hope for.

- Show where Backblaze fits. Explain how Backblaze slots into the customer's AI data pipeline alongside the compute, networking, and storage they already use.

- Hand off cleanly. Take the lead through the technical win, then step back so the AE can carry the deal through negotiation.

- Stay engaged after the sale. Answer questions in shared customer channels, help customers adopt the platform, and work with the AE on expansion.

- Carry the field back to Product. Capture gaps and requests with evidence.

- Share what you learn. Contribute benchmarks, technical content, and events.

What We Are Looking For 

- Curiosity. You dig into technical workflows and pick apart what customers tell you. This is the trait that matters most.

- Programming fluency. You are comfortable in at least one language, any language, and use it to script tests and automate work.

- Customer-facing experience. You have worked directly with customers in solutions engineering, support, technical account management, consulting, or a similar role. A sales background is not required.

- Working knowledge of cloud infrastructure. You can explain how compute, storage, and networking fit into an AI data pipeline and where a storage layer sits. Experience on any cloud counts, whether AWS, Google, Azure, or CoreWeave. You don't need to have built these systems yourself.

- Strong communication. You can explain a technical result clearly to an engineer or an executive, and you listen well.

- Hands-on habits. You test things yourself and write down what you find.

Also True of the Right Person 

- Experience across a whole deal at a smaller company, from discovery through post-sale

- Experience with object storage or the S3 API, or with AI and GPU workloads such as training, inference, and checkpointing

- Familiarity with a sales qualification method such as MEDDPICC

- Experience supporting customers after close, including expansions

This Is Not the Role for You If 

- You want to stay at the demo layer rather than test real workloads

- You wait for an AE to ask before you engage

- You see the job as finished at signature rather than after the customer is live

How We Will Interview 

You will have four conversations: a recruiter screen, the hiring manager, our principal solutions architect, and a member of the Solutions Engineering team. We will ask you to walk us through a proof of concept you ran, including a result the customer did not hope for and how you reported it. We will ask about a technical problem you dug into yourself, and how you work with customers and Account Executives. 

What We Offer 

- Competitive compensation and equity package

- Full benefits including medical, dental, vision, and 401(k) with matching

- RSU grants for full-time employees

- ESPP program

- Flexible vacation policy

- Maternity & paternity leave

- MacBook to use for work, plus a generous stipend to personalize your workstation

- Childcare bonus (human children only)

- Fertility treatment and support

- Learning & development program

- Commuter benefits

- A collaborative and transparent culture that supports a healthy work-life balance

Pay Transparency and Equal Opportunity 

To provide greater transparency to candidates, we share base pay ranges for all US-based job postings regardless of state. Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors including candidate location, skills, depth of work experience, and relevant licenses/credentials.

Salary range: $128,000-$144,000 plus variable pay and RSUs.

We are committed to fostering a workforce where all employees feel a sense of belonging regardless of race, ethnicity, nationality, gender, sexual orientation, age, religion, socio-economic status, ability, veteran status, and education. We are proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer.

description:

Why Go1 exists: 

Work keeps changing. Skills evolve, compliance requirements increase, and people need to continually learn and adapt. Go1 builds technology around how people learn and work. We bring together technology innovation, trusted content and intelligence to help organizations develop their people and support workforce progress. 

Why join Go1? 

- Build what comes next. Go1 is evolving from a trusted learning foundation into a broader workforce enablement portfolio, including Morgan by Go1. There is still plenty to shape, build and improve.

- Have real ownership. We’re founder-led, start-up minded and deliberately low on layers. You’ll have scope to influence decisions, solve problems beyond a narrow job description and be accountable for outcomes.

- Work AI-native. AI is becoming part of how we work across Go1. We expect people to experiment, build smarter workflows and use technology to improve the quality and speed of their work, while applying strong judgement.

- Grow through the work. Growth isn’t limited to promotion. It comes through harder problems, broader scope, new capabilities, cross-functional exposure and increasing the impact you can have.

- Work globally, with flexibility and trust. We’re remote-first across APAC, EMEA and North America. You’ll have autonomy and flexibility, alongside the responsibility to communicate clearly, build relationships proactively and stay connected across time zones.

We’re looking for a Finance Systems Engineer who is obsessed with end-to-end operational outcomes across systems. You’ll improve the reliability and efficiency of Go1’s finance operations, starting with quote-to-cash, working with Finance, RevOps and technical partners. Strong finance-domain expertise comes first, supported by practical familiarity with data, APIs and AI tools. Experience applying AI to finance workflows is a bonus. 

What you’ll do 

- Own defined improvements to NetSuite order-to-cash workflows , from customer and sales-order data through invoicing, payments, credits, refunds, reconciliation and close support. 

- Configure and troubleshoot NetSuite workflows, transaction forms, saved searches and invoice templates. Work with technical partners on changes that require deeper scripting or integration expertise . 

- Follow data between systems, investigate mapping and integration errors, and help improve APIs, webhooks and automated workflows. Check that records remain complete, accurate , and reconciled. 

- Investigate financial-system incidents and data-quality issues. Identify root causes, coordinate fixes , and reduce recurring manual work. 

- Work with Accounting , Tax and RevOps to turn operational needs into clear requirements. Escalate accounting and tax-policy decisions to the accountable owner. 

- Test changes in the appropriate environment , coordinate user acceptance and release readiness, and maintain clear documentation and support guidance. Preserve approvals, exception handling , and financial controls. 

- Use AI tools where they help with analysis, documentation, troubleshooting , or test preparation. Check their outputs, protect financial data and retain human review before using results in a financial workflow. 

What you’ll bring 

Four or more years of experience in finance systems, ideally in B2B. We’ll assess your experience in this order: 

1 . Finance -domain expertise 
Hands -on NetSuite experience and a strong understanding of operational finance and order-to-cash. You understand invoices, payments, refunds, reconciliation, revenue dates, and multi-currency considerations, and can explain the downstream impact of a system chang . Y ou can de monstrate o wnership of a finance workflow or system improvement, investigate discrepancies methodically, and re cognise w hen Finance or Tax approval is needed. Clear communication and careful testing are essential. Familiarity with record to report is nice to have. 

2 Data and API fundamentals 
You understand records, identifiers, field mappings and how data moves between systems. You can inspect an API request or response, follow an integration error and work with technical partners to diagnose the issue. Practical familiarity with APIs, webhooks or workflow automation is expected. You do not need to be an integration architect or an expert across every tool in our environment. 

3 . Practical AI familiarity 
You have some experience using AI tools for everyday work, such as analysis, documentation, troubleshooting or test preparation. You can check the output, recognise limitations and explain when human review is We value curiosity and a willingness to develop this capability. Advanced AI engineering, machine-learning expertise and production agent-building experience are not prerequisites. 

The Technology environment 
Hands-on NetSuite experience is required. Experience with the other platforms listed below is helpful, but not essential. 

- NetSuite: OneWorld, ARM, SuiteScript, SuiteFlow, SuiteAnalytics, SQL, SuiteQL, consolidated reporting, reconciliation and reporting 

- Experience in a subscription based B2B or multi-entity environment, or with more advanced integrations and AI-assisted workflows preferable

- Salesforce, Stripe and Upflow across customer and order data, billing, payments and collections.

- Tipalti, Expensify and Brex across supplier payments, expenses and spend management.

- Vertex and Pagero for indirect-tax and e-invoicing workflows.

- Workato, APIs and webhooks to connect systems, investigate data flows and improve automation.

- NetSuite reporting tools, SQL and emerging AI capabilities to support analysis, troubleshooting and controlled improvement

- Enterprise access to Chatgpt and Codex 

What this role is not 

- A NetSuite administrator role limited to access management and routine configuration. 

- A transactional accounting, invoice-processing or reporting-only role.

- A project manager coordinating technical work without hands-on involvement.

- A role limited to maintaining existing workflows without addressing underlying problems

description:

Why Mozilla? 

Mozilla Corporation is the non-profit-backed technology company that has shaped the internet for the better over the last 25 years. We make pioneering brands like Firefox, the privacy-minded web browser. Now, with more than 225 million people around the world using our products each month, we’re shaping the next 25 years of technology and helping to reclaim an internet built for people, not companies. Our work focuses on diverse areas including AI, social media, security and more. And we’re doing this while never losing our focus on our core mission – to make the internet better for people. 

The Mozilla Corporation is wholly owned by the non-profit 501(c) Mozilla Foundation. This means we aren’t beholden to any shareholders — only to our mission. Along with thousands of volunteer contributors and collaborators all over the world, Mozillians design, build and distribute open-source software that enables people to enjoy the internet on their terms. 

About the OS Integration team: 

The OS Integration team ensures Firefox works well with the host operating system and environment. We’re a distributed team with expertise in Windows, macOS, and Linux-based operating systems. Our responsibilities include developing fixes and improvements for Firefox related to Windows, macOS, and Linux environments. This might include integration with a new OS feature or fixing an OS-specific user interface bug. Other responsibilities include native crash reporting, OS abstraction layers, sandboxing, hardening, installer, updater, device APIs, and enterprise DLP support. 

About the role: 

As a member of the OS Integration team, you’ll develop fixes, improvements, and new features for Firefox. The role will lean on your Windows expertise, but projects may have a cross-platform component. This role will include development of features for Firefox in enterprise environments especially implementation of Data Loss Prevention (DLP) features. As a Staff Software Engineer, you’re a clear communicator and expert in your domain, ready to work on multi-month projects. You’ll contribute to the team through code review, mentoring, and discussion. 

What you’ll do:

- Lead projects that improve the stability, security, and performance of Firefox. 

- Collaborate with experienced software engineers. 

- Perform code reviews and provide technical direction. 

- Work with a geographically-distributed development team. 

- Interact with teams throughout the organization. 

What you’ll bring:

- Knowledge of web technologies such as Javascript, HTML, and CSS.
